163	     `SYS_TIME` is already initialised by Harmony before the scheduler starts, so the configure macro is a no-op. `SYS_TIME_Counter64Get` returns the full 64-bit TC0 CH0 counter; the matching `configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE = uint64_t` overrides FreeRTOS's `uint32_t` default so cumulative `ulRunTimeCounter` values don't wrap (uint32_t at 266 MHz wraps after ~16 s of accumulated CPU time across all tasks, which made percentages garbage almost immediately). Bare `extern` (rather than including a Harmony header) keeps `FreeRTOSConfig.h` consumable by low-level kernel sources that don't pull in `definitions.h`.

165	  7. **`drv_usb_udphs_device.c` — multi-IRP DMA arming in completion ISRs.** Stock UDPHS device driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch (line 1604+); IRPs appended to a non-empty queue link in (line 2273-2284 of patched file via `iterator->next = irp_t`) but never get armed for transmission. `Tasks_ISR_DMA` advances `irpQueue = irp->next` after firing the callback but does not re-program DMA hardware. Result: only one IRP per "queue idle" sequence ever transmits — the rest sit `STATUS_PENDING` forever.

Then add a call after the queue advance in **two** places:
168	
169	      - `Tasks_ISR_DMA` immediately after `endpointObj->irpQueue = irp->next; irp->callback(...)` — the normal DMA-completion path.
170	      - The ZLP-completion path inside `Tasks_ISR` (under "endpoint interrupt on a DMA capable endpoint, so it should be a ZLP"), same place: after queue advance.
171	
172	      Both call sites guarded by `if (endpointObj->irpQueue != NULL)`. Patch markers `/* PATCH: */` make the change findable after MCC regen. Helper carries the same cache-clean and DMA-program shape as the inline original, including the `__DSB(); __ISB();` barriers and the `SYS_CACHE_CleanDCache_by_Addr` for the IRP data buffer.
173	
174	      Without this patch, the lever-1 multi-IRP work (`queueSizeWrite=3`, `USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED=5`) accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch. With it, multi-IRP pipelining works as designed at the driver level. Patch is specific to Harmony USB v3.16.0 device driver; check whether future versions wire the post-completion arm and obviate the patch.

176	  8. **`driver/input/drv_maxtouch.c` — bounded maXTouch init so an absent touch panel can't hang the whole system.** Stock `mxt_initialize()` does `while (1) { mxt_read_info_block(); if (!error) break; }`. With the display/maXTouch panel disconnected the info-block read never succeeds, so it spins forever — and because each `mxt_read_info_block()` allocates from the FreeRTOS heap (heap_1, no free), the retries leak until the heap is exhausted and the system hangs in `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. This is exactly what blocked the JTAG load-to-RAM bring-up (fault landed in `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks`, `xNextFreeByte`=40,944/40,960). Three-part fix: (a) `__mxt_read_reg` now propagates the real `DRV_I2C_WriteReadTransfer` result (`? 0 : -EIO`) instead of hardcoding `ret = 0`, so a NAK from an absent controller is detected at the *first* read and bails before the second, garbage-sized `OSAL_Malloc`; (b) `mxt_initialize` retries at most `MXT_INIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (10, 20 ms apart) then returns the error; (c) `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks` `DEVICE_STATE_MXT_INITIALIZE` parks the driver in `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR` (not READY) on failure, so the rest of the system runs headless without touch. Syntax-checked clean with XC32 v4.60, then **validated on hardware (2026-06-08)**: with the display/maXTouch panel disconnected, marvin loaded via the JTAG load-to-RAM flow now boots *past* maXTouch init (driver → `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR`) and runs headless — PC samples land in `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit` / `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read` (perf-log USB-CDC path) and advance across the codebase, instead of hanging at `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. Re-apply after every maXTouch MCC regen.

227	### 2026-06-26 — Splash bring-up #4: splash only filled one scratch tile → render-to-idle pump

229	After the RGBMODE fix the splash decoded **perfectly but only in a ~400×300 top-left region**. 231	### 2026-06-26 — Splash bring-up #3: garbled splash root-caused to the XLCDC per-layer color-mode gotcha
232	
233	On hardware the splash came up garbled/magenta (a transparent, wrong-format image), then the dashboard came up correct. Root cause (read from the driver, not guessed): the **GFX-XLCDC driver never commits a per-layer color mode**. `drv_gfx_xlcdc.c`'s canvas commit path (`SET_LAYER_UNLOCK`) writes address/alpha/pos/size/stride/enable but **not `RGBMODE`** — it assumes every layer is the project framebuffer (`FB_COL_MODE` = RGB565, `FB_TYPE_SZ` = 2). So the canvas's `SET_LAYER_COLOR_MODE` (our RGBA8888) is staged in `drvLayer.pixelformat` and dropped; OVR2 stayed RGB565 and read the 32bpp splash buffer as 16bpp → garbled. (RGB565 dashboard/nav matched the default, so they were fine — which is why only the splash garbled, in both cuts.) **Fix:** `ui_manager` sets OVR2 directly with `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR2, RGBA_8888, true)` after binding the splash canvas; the driver never rewrites RGBMODE so it sticks (same runtime poke `video.c` uses for HEO). Confirmed the JPEG path itself is fine: decoder handles restart markers + standard subsampling, and skips Exif/APP13 by length; streaming interface (`LE_STREAMING_ENABLED`) is **not** needed because we load the whole file into RAM (`LE_STREAM_LOCATION_ID_INTERNAL`). **Still open after this fix:** (1) splash opacity — OVR2 blends per-pixel alpha (`OVR2CFG9` SFACTC=A0×As), fine if the decoder writes α=0xFF, else needs an opaque-blend tweak (note: `XLCDC_SetLayerOpts` rewrites CFG9 each canvas commit, so a CFG9 poke would be clobbered — would need the pixels opaque instead); (2) nav hamburger button does nothing — event is wired (`le_gen_screen_Dashboard.c:301`), so suspect input/pick path; investigate after the garble fix.

243	### 2026-06-26 — Splash bring-up #1: reveal-before-paint diagnosis → pre-render + persistent-widgets direction
244	
245	First on-hardware run of the splash. Symptoms: yellow screen, briefly garbled (JPEG), then dashboard with the **top 1/3 noise and the bottom 2/3 progressively drawn**, then everything settled correct after ~1–2 s; opening the nav showed the same noise-then-redraw.
246	
247	**Root cause (single):** not a color-mode/stride bug — it's **reveal-before-paint over uninitialized DRAM**. We make a canvas visible (backlight already on) while Legato is still incrementally painting its widget tree; unpainted regions show fresh-RAM noise. The Dashboard MGS tree is ~200+ widgets, software-painted, so a full first paint takes ~1–2 s — the whole visible fill-in. Confirmed by the code: every screen is **non-persistent** (`screenHide_*` does `leWidget_Delete(root0)` + NULLs all member pointers), so each show **rebuilds and repaints from scratch**.
248	
249	**Direction (Greg's call): pre-render every screen onto its own canvas + make widgets persistent**, then switch screens by re-pointing the layer — no rebuild, no repaint-from-scratch. This is the original compositor vision (`ui_compositor.md` §1). Enabling facts found: `CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ = 8` (room for per-screen surfaces; `LE_LAYER_COUNT` is only 3), and MGS has a per-screen **"persistent"** option (stops `screenHide` from deleting the tree). The splash's ≥1.2 s on-screen hold is useful cover to pre-paint the heavy Dashboard behind it.
250	
251	**Open design questions** (before building — see `ui_compositor.md` §10):
252	- Live-telemetry screens (Dashboard) must keep repainting while shown, so "pre-render once, never repaint" only covers the *first reveal*; while visible it repaints live, and on switch-away the persistent surface keeps the last frame.
253	- Legato renders attached roots into their layer's canvas; with only 3 Legato layers, pre-painting an off-screen screen into its own surface needs either a spare layer or `gfxcSetBaseCanvasID` multiplexing across the 8 canvas objects.
254	- The "render to completion before reveal" mechanism: how to drive `leUpdate` to a fully-painted state for an off-screen screen without racing `LEGATO_Tasks`.
255	- **Interim mitigation** (cheap, until the rearchitecture lands): `memset` each canvas buffer to its background color before first reveal so the gap reads as a clean solid fill, not RAM noise.

```text
101	
102	void APP_Initialize ( void )
103	{
104	    appData.state = APP_STATE_INIT;
105	
106	    /* Logging shim: thin wrapper over libc printf with severity filter
107	     * and FreeRTOS-aware locking. Initialized first so subsequent code
108	     * (including video task startup) can use LOG_*. Default level is
109	     * INFO; flip to DEBUG via log_set_level() to enable verbose. */
110	    log_init(LOG_LEVEL_INFO);
111	
112	    /* UI manager: owns the canvas surface pool + LCDC layer mapping and screen
113	     * startup (string table + screenInit/Show — the MGS screen state machine is
114	     * disabled). Runs before the scheduler so surfaces exist and the canvas is
115	     * RUNNING before the first render; the Dashboard screen's On-Show hook binds the
116	     * dashboard to BASE and hands the nav drawer to ui/nav. */
117	    UiManager_Initialize();
118	
119	    /* Spawn the video task. xTaskCreate is safe before vTaskStartScheduler;
120	     * the task runs once the scheduler picks it up. The video module owns
121	     * its capture-pipeline init (ISC, TC358743, backlight, HEO unbind),
122	     * the capture/display state machine, and the bridge-status polling. */
123	    Video_Initialize();
124	
125	    /* Per-frame performance log: producer-side queues + drain task.
126	     * Init the queues here so any producer that posts before the
127	     * scheduler starts will not crash; the drain task is launched
128	     * separately by PerfLog_Start once the scheduler is up. */
129	    PerfLog_Initialize();
130	
131	    /* Video go-live (window + capture + display) is deferred to the boot loader
132	     * so the camera comes up only after the splash → dashboard handoff — the
133	     * splash owns the panel during startup. See Loader_Start below. */
134	
135	    /* Reference detector (cv_marvin_v1) + detector-state bus. M1 stub
136	     * publisher; real detection logic lands incrementally. Must follow
137	     * Video_Initialize since cv_marvin_v1 subscribes to the video frame
138	     * queue from inside its task. Detectors default disabled; explicitly
139	     * enable + select the active one for the timing pipeline. */
140	    Detector_Initialize();
141	    Detector_Enable(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1);
142	    Detector_SetActive(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1);
143	
144	    /* M2 actuator path: fretboard_link owns the submit queue + FLEXCOM1
145	     * USART writer and the RX parse task. The FLEXCOM1 peripheral is brought
146	     * up by SYS_Initialize (FLEXCOM1_USART_Initialize), so this just arms the
147	     * ring-buffer RX notification and starts the link tasks. */
148	    FretboardLink_Initialize();
149	
150	    /* timing_pipeline runs the chord-window + strum scheduler against the
151	     * active detector and pushes the resulting 7-bit mask through
152	     * FretboardLink_Send. */
153	    TimingPipeline_Initialize();
154	
155	    /* manual_control is a peer producer for direct UI-driven actuation
156	     * (game-menu navigation, manual test). UI buttons are authored in
157	     * Microchip Graphics Composer; the generated screenShow_Screen0
158	     * registers the event_Screen0_Button_Manual_* callbacks defined in
159	     * ui/manual_input.c, so no explicit bind step is needed here. */
160	    ManualControl_Initialize();
161	
162	    /* Game-state observer (spec §4.8, M9): a video-frame consumer that
163	     * classifies the current GH3 screen and publishes game_state_t events on
164	     * xGameStateQueue. Like cv_marvin_v1 it subscribes to the video frame queue
165	     * from inside its task, so it follows Video_Initialize. Enable observation
166	     * explicitly (default off, per the §6 game_observe_enable toggle). */
167	    GameplayEngine_Initialize();
168	    GameplayEngine_SetObserveEnabled(true);
169	
170	    /* SD-card storage: sets up mount state only (no I/O here — the SDMMC
171	     * driver hasn't analyzed the card pre-scheduler). The card is mounted on
172	     * demand by the `sd` console command; see storage/storage.h. */
173	    Storage_Initialize();
174	
175	    /* Per-player results log (CSV on the card). State only here; file I/O is
176	     * lazy (mounts on demand) from Results_Append / the player/scores/results
177	     * console commands. */
178	    Results_Initialize();
179	
180	    /* Song catalog (labels keyed by the recognizer's (setlist,index)). State
181	     * only here; the CSV is lazy-loaded from the card on first lookup / the
182	     * `catalog` console command. A missing catalog degrades to "Unknown song"
183	     * and never affects recognition. See game/catalog.h. */
184	    Catalog_Initialize();
185	
186	    /* Interactive operator console on FLEXCOM2 (115200), separate from the
187	     * DBGU log channel. Started after the actuator/detector modules so its
188	     * commands can drive their setters. */
189	    Console_Initialize();
190	
191	    /* Boot loader task: mounts the SD card, paints the splash image, lights the
192	     * backlight, runs asset pre-load, then swaps BASE splash → dashboard and
193	     * brings the camera up. Created here (pre-scheduler); runs once the
194	     * scheduler is up (it needs blocking SD/FatFs I/O). Self-deletes after the
195	     * handoff. Follows Storage/Video/UiManager init, which it depends on. */
196	    Loader_Start();
197	
198	    /* Drain task is launched last so every producer's queue handle is
199	     * already valid when the first records hit the sink. Marvin creates
200	     * all tasks pre-scheduler (Harmony brings the scheduler up after
201	     * APP_Initialize returns); xTaskCreateStatic before vTaskStartScheduler
202	     * is the standard FreeRTOS pattern. */
203	    PerfLog_Start();
204	}
205	
206	
207	/******************************************************************************
208	  Function:
209	    void APP_Tasks ( void )
210	
211	  Remarks:
212	    See prototype in app.h.
213	 */
214	
215	void APP_Tasks ( void )
216	{
217	    /* All tasks have been created by now, so this is the heap_1 startup floor
218	     * (heap_1 never frees — free space only shrinks). Surfaces remaining
219	     * headroom so a future allocation walking into the wall is visible rather
220	     * than a silent malloc-failed spin. */
221	    LOG_INFO("freertos heap: %u bytes free\r\n", (unsigned)xPortGetFreeHeapSize());
222	
223	    /* APP is a one-shot launcher — task creation happened in APP_Initialize.
224	     * Self-delete here so the (1024-word) stack and TCB are released to the
225	     * idle task. The MCC-generated lAPP_Tasks loop will not iterate again
226	     * because vTaskDelete(NULL) never returns to its caller. */
227	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
228	}
```

```text
57	 * (no card, missing file, too large, short read) — caller falls back to the
58	 * splash's solid fill. */
59	static uint32_t load_splash_file(void)
60	{
61	    if (!Storage_Mount()) { return 0u; }
62	
63	    char path[64];
64	    (void)snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s%s", Storage_MountPoint(), SPLASH_REL_PATH);
65	
66	    SYS_FS_HANDLE h = SYS_FS_FileOpen(path, SYS_FS_FILE_OPEN_READ);
67	    if (h == SYS_FS_HANDLE_INVALID)
68	    {
69	        LOG_WARN("LOADER: no splash %s (fs err %d)\r\n", path, (int)SYS_FS_Error());
70	        return 0u;
71	    }
72	
73	    int32_t sz = SYS_FS_FileSize(h);
74	    if (sz <= 0 || (uint32_t)sz > SPLASH_JPEG_MAX)
75	    {
76	        LOG_WARN("LOADER: splash size %ld invalid (cap %u)\r\n",
77	                 (long)sz, (unsigned)SPLASH_JPEG_MAX);
78	        (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);
79	        return 0u;
80	    }
81	
82	    uint32_t total = 0u;
83	    bool err = false;
84	    while (total < (uint32_t)sz)
85	    {
86	        size_t want = (size_t)((uint32_t)sz - total);
87	        if (want > SPLASH_READ_CHUNK) { want = SPLASH_READ_CHUNK; }
88	
89	        size_t got = SYS_FS_FileRead(h, &s_jpeg[total], want);
90	        if (got == 0u || got == (size_t)-1) { err = true; break; }
91	        total += (uint32_t)got;
92	    }
93	    (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);
94	
95	    if (err || total != (uint32_t)sz)
96	    {
97	        LOG_WARN("LOADER: splash read short %lu/%ld\r\n", (unsigned long)total, (long)sz);
98	        return 0u;
99	    }
100	    LOG_INFO("LOADER: splash %lu B loaded\r\n", (unsigned long)total);
101	    return total;
102	}
103	
104	/* Block until the Legato render task has fully painted all pending damage.
105	 *
106	 * We do NOT drive leUpdate ourselves — the normal LEGATO_Tasks + GFX_CANVAS_Task
107	 * pair renders the full screen correctly (a full-screen surface spans several
108	 * scratch tiles, and the scratch is freed by the canvas commit between render
109	 * passes; that only happens when those tasks actually run). So the loader just
110	 * yields and polls the public idle flag. First wait for the task to pick up the
111	 * queued damage (go busy), then wait for it to finish — both bounded so a render
112	 * stall can't hang boot. */
113	static void wait_render_idle(void)
114	{
115	    TickType_t  deadline   = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS);
116	    TickType_t  idle_since = 0;
117	    bool        idle_run   = false;
118	
119	    while (xTaskGetTickCount() < deadline)
120	    {
121	        if (leRenderer_IsIdle())
122	        {
123	            /* Idle must hold continuously — a lone idle sample is just an
124	             * inter-frame gap, not a finished paint. */
125	            if (!idle_run)
126	            {
127	                idle_run   = true;
128	                idle_since = xTaskGetTickCount();
129	            }
130	            else if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - idle_since) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_STABLE_MS))
131	            {
132	                return;
133	            }
134	        }
135	        else
136	        {
137	            idle_run = false;   /* a frame started → reset the streak */
138	        }
139	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_POLL_MS));
140	    }
141	    LOG_WARN("LOADER: render-idle wait timed out\r\n");
142	}
143	
144	static void loader_task(void *param)
145	{
146	    (void)param;
147	
148	    /* The splash, dashboard, and nav were built on their own canvases by
149	     * UiManager_Initialize (pre-scheduler); the Legato render task is now
150	     * painting them (backlight still off). Load the splash image, wait for the
151	     * render to finish, then light the panel — the first lit frame is the
152	     * fully-painted splash, with the dashboard finished behind it on BASE. No
153	     * image (no card / too large) → the panel's solid fill is the fallback. */
154	    uint32_t len = 0u;
155	    for (uint32_t a = 0u; (a < SD_LOAD_ATTEMPTS) && (len == 0u); a++)
156	    {
157	        if (a > 0u) { vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(SD_RETRY_MS)); }
158	        len = load_splash_file();
159	    }
160	    if (!((len > 0u) && Splash_SetImageJpeg(s_jpeg, len)))
161	    {
162	        LOG_WARN("LOADER: solid-fill splash (no image)\r\n");
163	    }
164	
165	    wait_render_idle();
166	    UiManager_EnableBacklight();
167	    TickType_t shown_at = xTaskGetTickCount();
168	
169	    /* --- Asset pre-load goes here (album art → DDR cache, etc.). The 32bpp
170	     * splash buffer (ui_manager) is free to reuse as decode scratch once the
171	     * splash leaves the screen. None yet. --- */
172	
173	    /* Hold the splash a minimum time so a fast boot doesn't flash it away. */
174	    TickType_t elapsed   = xTaskGetTickCount() - shown_at;
175	    TickType_t min_ticks = pdMS_TO_TICKS(SPLASH_MIN_MS);
176	    if (elapsed < min_ticks) { vTaskDelay(min_ticks - elapsed); }
177	
178	    /* Drop the splash → the dashboard (painted behind it) is revealed, complete.
179	     * Then bring the camera up. */
180	    UiManager_RevealDashboard();
181	    Video_SetWindow(VIDEO_WIN_X, VIDEO_WIN_Y, VIDEO_WIN_W, VIDEO_WIN_H);
182	    Video_CaptureEnable();
183	    Video_DisplayShow();
184	
185	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
186	}
187	
188	void Loader_Start(void)
189	{
190	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(loader_task, "LoaderTask", LOADER_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
191	                            NULL, LOADER_TASK_PRIORITY, s_task_stack, &s_task_tcb);
192	}
193
```

```text
28	/* Scratch for the bench write/read. Static so it stays off the caller's
29	 * (console) task stack. Cache-line aligned so disk_write takes the multi-block
30	 * fast path: the FatFs diskio bounces a cache-unaligned write buffer through a
31	 * single 512 B sector buffer (~10x slower), while reads stay multi-block even
32	 * when unaligned — which is why an unaligned buffer is write-slow but read-fast.
33	 * Any buffer handed to SYS_FS_FileWrite for throughput wants this alignment. */
34	static uint8_t s_chunk[STG_CHUNK] __ALIGNED(CACHE_LINE_SIZE);

38	static void diag_printf(storage_print_fn out, void *ctx, const char *fmt, ...)

48	/* Throughput in whole MB/s ×10 (one decimal), integer math. */
49	static uint32_t mbps_x10(uint32_t bytes, uint32_t ms)
50	{
51	    if (ms == 0u) { return 0u; }
52	    return (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)bytes * 1000u * 10u) / ((uint64_t)1024u * 1024u * ms));
53	}
54	
55	/* Deterministic pattern as a function of absolute byte offset, so a read can
56	 * verify without retaining what was written. */
57	static void fill_chunk(uint8_t *b, uint32_t chunk_index)
58	{
59	    uint32_t base = chunk_index * STG_CHUNK;
60	    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < STG_CHUNK; i++)
61	    {
62	        uint32_t off = base + i;
63	        b[i] = (uint8_t)(off ^ (off >> 8));
64	    }
65	}

67	static bool verify_chunk(const uint8_t *b, uint32_t chunk_index)
68	{
69	    uint32_t base = chunk_index * STG_CHUNK;
70	    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < STG_CHUNK; i++)
71	    {
72	        uint32_t off = base + i;
73	        if (b[i] != (uint8_t)(off ^ (off >> 8))) { return false; }
74	    }
75	    return true;
76	}

124	/* FatFs time hook. Overrides the __WEAK stub in the generated diskio.c (which
125	 * returns a fixed 2013 date) so file timestamps come from the RTC, in UTC.
126	 * FatFs calls this on every create/modify (FF_FS_NORTC=0). The DOS format
127	 * stores year-1980 and seconds/2; FatFs rejects years before 1980, so an
128	 * unset/implausible RTC falls back to the 1980 epoch. */
129	DWORD get_fattime(void)
130	{
131	    struct tm now;
132	    memset(&now, 0, sizeof(now));
133	    RTC_TimeGet(&now);
134	
135	    SYS_FS_TIME t;
136	    t.packedTime = 0u;
137	
138	    int year = now.tm_year + 1900;
139	    if (year < 1980)
140	    {
141	        t.discreteTime.year  = 0u;   /* 1980 */
142	        t.discreteTime.month = 1u;
143	        t.discreteTime.day   = 1u;
144	        return t.packedTime;
145	    }
146	
147	    t.discreteTime.year   = (unsigned)(year - 1980);
148	    t.discreteTime.month  = (unsigned)(now.tm_mon + 1);
149	    t.discreteTime.day    = (unsigned)now.tm_mday;
150	    t.discreteTime.hour   = (unsigned)now.tm_hour;
151	    t.discreteTime.minute = (unsigned)now.tm_min;
152	    t.discreteTime.second = (unsigned)(now.tm_sec / 2);   /* DOS stores sec/2 */
153	    return t.packedTime;
154	}

225	void Storage_DiagBench(storage_print_fn out, void *ctx, uint32_t mbytes)
226	{
227	    if (!Storage_Mount())
228	    {
229	        diag_printf(out, ctx, "not mounted");
230	        return;
231	    }
232	
233	    if (mbytes == 0u)               { mbytes = 4u; }
234	    if (mbytes > STG_BENCH_MAX_MB)  { mbytes = STG_BENCH_MAX_MB; }
235	
236	    uint32_t chunks      = (mbytes * 1024u * 1024u) / STG_CHUNK;
237	    uint32_t total_bytes = chunks * STG_CHUNK;
238	
239	    /* write */
240	    SYS_FS_HANDLE h = SYS_FS_FileOpen(STG_TESTFILE, SYS_FS_FILE_OPEN_WRITE);
241	    if (h == SYS_FS_HANDLE_INVALID)
242	    {
243	        diag_printf(out, ctx, "open(write) failed (fs err %d)", (int)SYS_FS_Error());
244	        return;
245	    }
246	    TickType_t t0 = xTaskGetTickCount();
247	    bool write_err = false;
248	    for (uint32_t c = 0u; c < chunks; c++)
249	    {
250	        fill_chunk(s_chunk, c);
251	        if (SYS_FS_FileWrite(h, s_chunk, STG_CHUNK) != STG_CHUNK)
252	        {
253	            write_err = true;
254	            break;
255	        }
256	    }
257	    (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);
258	    uint32_t wms = (uint32_t)((xTaskGetTickCount() - t0) * portTICK_PERIOD_MS);
259	    if (write_err)
260	    {
261	        diag_printf(out, ctx, "write failed (fs err %d)", (int)SYS_FS_Error());
262	        return;
263	    }

265	                (unsigned long)(total_bytes / 1024u), (unsigned long)wms,
266	                (unsigned long)(mbps_x10(total_bytes, wms) / 10u),
267	                (unsigned long)(mbps_x10(total_bytes, wms) % 10u));
268	
269	    /* read back + verify */

271	    if (h == SYS_FS_HANDLE_INVALID)
272	    {
273	        diag_printf(out, ctx, "open(read) failed (fs err %d)", (int)SYS_FS_Error());
274	        return;
275	    }
276	    TickType_t r0 = xTaskGetTickCount();

278	    for (uint32_t c = 0u; c < chunks; c++)

280	        if (SYS_FS_FileRead(h, s_chunk, STG_CHUNK) != STG_CHUNK)
281	        {
282	            read_err = true;
283	            break;
284	        }
285	        if (!verify_chunk(s_chunk, c))

289	        }
290	    }
291	    (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);
292	    uint32_t rms = (uint32_t)((xTaskGetTickCount() - r0) * portTICK_PERIOD_MS);
293	    if (read_err)
294	    {
295	        diag_printf(out, ctx, "read failed (fs err %d)", (int)SYS_FS_Error());
296	        return;

301	                (unsigned long)(mbps_x10(total_bytes, rms) % 10u));
```

Good instinct to pull on, but let me lay out the boot timeline precisely first, because it changes what "taking control in main" actually buys you.

## What runs when today

```
main()                          [main.c:40]
 └─ SYS_Initialize(NULL)        ── all PLIB/driver/middleware _Initialize, single-threaded, NO scheduler
     ├─ DRV_SDMMC_Initialize    [initialization.c:470]
     ├─ SYS_FS_Initialize       [initialization.c:495]
     └─ APP_Initialize()        [initialization.c:499]  ← Harmony calls this LAST, still pre-scheduler
 └─ SYS_Tasks()                 ── creates ALL task threads, then vTaskStartScheduler() (never returns)
```

Two facts that matter:

1. **`APP_Initialize` runs *before* any Harmony task exists.** `SYS_Tasks` is what `xTaskCreate`s the SDMMC/FS/GFX/XLCDC/LEGATO/USB threads, and it does so *after* `APP_Initialize` returns. So your earlier idea — "adjust task priorities in app init" — can't work as written: the handles don't exist yet. The only valid place to `vTaskPrioritySet` the Harmony tasks is **post-scheduler**, i.e. from inside our [loader task](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/loader.c) (or the APP launcher). That's fine — the loader is already our post-scheduler entry point.

2. **`SYS_Tasks` bundles *all* task creation + the scheduler start into one non-returning call.** This is the key constraint for your main.c idea.

## What taking over main.c actually gives you

Honestly: less than it looks like. If you remove APP from the MCC config and call `APP_Initialize` yourself from main.c, you've moved one function call out of `SYS_Initialize` — but it's still pre-scheduler either way, so reordering it only reorders *single-threaded init*. It does **not** let you interleave task creation or start the scheduler with a reduced task set, because `SYS_Tasks` still owns the create-all-then-`vTaskStartScheduler` sequence and never returns. To get staged scheduler bring-up (start with only SD+render+loader, splash up, *then* spawn USB/video/detector/etc.) you'd have to stop using the generated `SYS_Tasks` for orchestration and create tasks yourself — which is exactly the generated-architecture surgery you want to avoid, and it's fragile across every MCC regen.

So: removing APP from Harmony is a fine *ownership* cleanup, but it isn't the timing lever.

## Where the timing actually goes (and the real levers)

The win is achievable entirely from code we already own, no generated-code edits:

**First — measure, don't guess.** The journal says ~2–3 s is "mount." Look at the retry math before tuning: [`Storage_Mount`](firmware/marvin/default/src/storage/storage.c#L89) spins **50 × 20 ms = up to 1 s** internally, and the [loader wraps that in 5 × 300 ms retries](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/loader.c#L155). If the card isn't ready for ~1.5 s, the first `Storage_Mount` burns its full second failing, the loader sleeps 300 ms, then the second call finally succeeds — that alone is most of the "2–3 s," and it's **inherent card power-up + analysis latency**, which no priority tuning fixes. I'd add timestamps around mount / decode / render-idle and read the real split first.

**Then, two levers, both ours:**

- **Defer our own task spawns past the splash.** Today [`APP_Initialize`](firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c#L102) spins up video, detector, gameplay, manual, perf, console — all competing for CPU from the first tick while we're trying to mount + paint. You already deferred *video go-live*; extend that: keep only what the splash needs (UiManager surfaces + the loader task) created early, and move the rest into the loader's post-`RevealDashboard` phase. This is the biggest contention reduction and touches zero generated code.

- **Runtime priority shaping from the loader.** SDMMC and SYS_FS are both at **priority 1** (the floor), while render is 2 and USB is **3** (the ceiling). So during boot the SD driver is preempted by everything. From the loader task (post-scheduler, handles exist), boost `DRV_SDMMC0_Tasks` + `SYS_FS_TASKS` for the mount window and optionally knock USB/maxtouch down, then restore after reveal — via `vTaskPrioritySet(xTaskGetHandle("..."), ...)`. No generated edits.

Note the SDMMC task self-paces at `DRV_SDMMC_RTOS_DELAY_IDX0 = 10 ms` per state step — if analysis is many steps, that pacing (an MCC value), not CPU starvation, may dominate. Measurement tells us whether priority shaping even helps.

## My recommendation

Skip the main.c restructure for timing (do it later if you want the ownership cleanup, separately). For boot speed: **(1) instrument the mount/decode/render split, (2) defer non-essential task spawns to post-splash, (3) add bounded runtime priority shaping in the loader.** All three are reversible, generated-code-free, and target the actual serialization.

Want me to start with the instrumentation pass so we're tuning against real numbers, or do you already have a feel for the mount-vs-decode split and want to go straight to deferring the task spawns?

Confirmed — everything needed is already on: `configGENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS`, `configUSE_TRACE_FACILITY`, and `configUSE_STATS_FORMATTING_FUNCTIONS` are all `1`, with the 64-bit TC0 counter. So `uxTaskGetSystemState()` will hand us per-task `ulRunTimeCounter` values, and we can answer your exact question without disabling or restructuring anything.

## The measurement

Snapshot every task's cumulative run-time counter at two points and diff them. The decisive number is the **idle task's share of the window**:

- **High idle %** → the mount window is dominated by *inherent waiting* — card power-up, the SDMMC driver's 10 ms-per-step RTOS pacing, and your own retry sleeps ([`Storage_Mount`](firmware/marvin/default/src/storage/storage.c#L89) 50×20 ms + [loader](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/loader.c#L155) 5×300 ms). Nothing is starving the SD; priority shaping won't help, only starting earlier/overlapping or cutting the retry padding will.
- **Low idle %, USB/LEGATO/XLCDC/maxtouch eating it** → genuine CPU contention. Deferring task spawns + priority shaping is the fix.
- **SDMMC+SYS_FS share** → the actual cost of the SD work itself.

That's precisely "SD mount vs. everything else," quantified.

## What I'd build

A small static-allocation helper (no malloc) — `util/boot_profile.{c,h}` — with one call:

```c
BootProfile_Mark("loader start");   // stores baseline snapshot
...mount...
BootProfile_Mark("mount ok");       // logs per-task CPU % for [loader start → mount ok]
...wait_render_idle...
BootProfile_Mark("splash up");      // logs per-task CPU % for [mount ok → splash up]
```

Each `Mark` after the first dumps the window: wall-clock ms (from tick count) plus each task's % of CPU and the **idle %**, using one `uxTaskGetSystemState()` into a fixed `TaskStatus_t[24]` and diffing against the prior snapshot by handle. Drop the three marks into [loader.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/loader.c) — splitting the mount window from the decode/render window — and one run prints the whole breakdown.

This is read-only, generated-code-free, and self-deletes in spirit (the loader self-deletes anyway). Want me to write it and wire the three marks into the loader?

```h
 * RTOS pacing, retry sleeps) from CPU contention (other tasks eating the
 * window). Zero-alloc; relies on configGENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS +
 * configUSE_TRACE_FACILITY (both on). */
```

```c
#include "util/boot_profile.h"

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"

#include "log.h"

/* Upper bound on tasks we account for. The system has ~12 (SD/FS/render/USB/
 * input/loader/app + idle + timer); 24 leaves headroom. Over-capacity tasks are
 * dropped from the report by uxTaskGetSystemState (it returns 0). */
#define BP_MAX_TASKS  24u

/* Compact baseline kept between marks: only what the diff needs (run-time
 * counters are cumulative since boot, so a window is cur - prev per handle). */
typedef struct
{
    TaskHandle_t            handle;
    configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE rt;
} bp_entry_t;

static bp_entry_t  s_prev[BP_MAX_TASKS];
static UBaseType_t s_prev_n;
static TickType_t  s_prev_tick;
static bool        s_have_prev;

/* Cumulative run-time counter for a handle in the previous snapshot, or 0 if it
 * wasn't present (task created during the window — count its whole counter). */
static configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE prev_rt_for(TaskHandle_t h)
{
    for (UBaseType_t i = 0u; i < s_prev_n; i++)
    {
        if (s_prev[i].handle == h) { return s_prev[i].rt; }
    }
    return 0u;
}

void BootProfile_Mark(const char *label)
{
    static TaskStatus_t cur[BP_MAX_TASKS];   /* off-stack: ~1 KB */

    configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE total_now = 0u;
    UBaseType_t n = uxTaskGetSystemState(cur, BP_MAX_TASKS, &total_now);
    TickType_t  tick_now = xTaskGetTickCount();

    if (s_have_prev)
    {
        /* Total CPU "ticks" (run-time counter units) charged across all tasks
         * during this window — the denominator for each task's share. */
        configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE total_prev = 0u;
        for (UBaseType_t i = 0u; i < s_prev_n; i++) { total_prev += s_prev[i].rt; }
        configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE total_delta = total_now - total_prev;

        uint32_t window_ms = (uint32_t)((tick_now - s_prev_tick) * portTICK_PERIOD_MS);
        LOG_INFO("BOOTPROF [%s]: %lu ms window\r\n", label, (unsigned long)window_ms);

        if (total_delta == 0u)
        {
            LOG_INFO("BOOTPROF   (no CPU charged in window)\r\n");
        }
        else
        {
            for (UBaseType_t i = 0u; i < n; i++)
            {
                configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE d =
                    cur[i].ulRunTimeCounter - prev_rt_for(cur[i].xHandle);
                if (d == 0u) { continue; }   /* task idle this window — skip noise */

                uint32_t pct_x10 = (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)d * 1000u) / total_delta);
                LOG_INFO("BOOTPROF   %-16s %2lu.%lu%%\r\n",
                         cur[i].pcTaskName,
                         (unsigned long)(pct_x10 / 10u),
                         (unsigned long)(pct_x10 % 10u));
            }
        }
    }

    /* Store this snapshot as the baseline for the next mark. */
    s_prev_n = (n < BP_MAX_TASKS) ? n : BP_MAX_TASKS;
    for (UBaseType_t i = 0u; i < s_prev_n; i++)
    {
        s_prev[i].handle = cur[i].xHandle;
        s_prev[i].rt     = cur[i].ulRunTimeCounter;
    }
    s_prev_tick = tick_now;
    s_have_prev = true;
}

```

```
BOOTPROF   USB_DEVICE_TASKS   2.5%
...
```

**How to read it:** the `IDLE` line in the `mount + read` window is the verdict. High idle (like the sketch above) means the 2–3 s is inherent waiting — card power-up, the SDMMC driver's 10 ms-per-step pacing, and your retry sleeps — and priority shaping won't help; cutting the retry padding and starting earlier will. Low idle with USB/LEGATO/XLCDC/maxtouch eating the window means genuine contention, and deferring task spawns + boosting SDMMC/FS priority is the fix.

It won't build from here (needs your MPLAB build). Once you've run it, paste the `BOOTPROF` lines and we'll tune against the real numbers.

One note: the `mount + read` window currently lumps the SD mount together with the JPEG file read (both are SD I/O). If you want the *mount alone* split out from the file read, say so and I'll add a fourth mark between them.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 10:56:11Z)**_

Real numbers change the picture — and they kill the priority-shaping idea outright. Here's what the data says.

## Headline: the SD mount is not CPU-bound, and not starved

In the **mount + read** window, `DRV_SDMMC0_Task` and `SYS_FS_TASKS` are both at **0.0% CPU**. They're not waiting for the CPU — they're waiting for the *card*. Boosting their priority would do nothing; they already get the CPU whenever they have a step to run, and the steps are cheap. So your original "raise SD priority during boot" instinct is **dead** — confirmed by measurement. Good thing we measured.

What actually fills the 2453 ms window:

| | mount + read (2453 ms) | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| LEGATO_Tasks | 45.3% (~1110 ms) | painting dashboard + nav + solid-fill splash |
| IDLE | 35.7% (~875 ms) | waiting on the card (retry sleeps + RTOS pacing) |
| VideoTask | 14.6% (~360 ms) | capture-pipeline init (ISC/bridge), not even go-live yet |
| SDMMC + SYS_FS | ~0% | **the SD work itself** |

The `STG: mount failed (fs err 3)` → `mounted` confirms the first `Storage_Mount` burned its full **50×20 ms = 1 s** failing because the card wasn't ready, then the loader slept **300 ms** and the retry succeeded. So ~1.3 s of that window is pure retry latency waiting for card-ready, and LEGATO/Video opportunistically paint during it.

## The decode + render window is all LEGATO

**LEGATO 88.8%, IDLE 6.8%** over 1756 ms — CPU-bound rendering. But here's the thing: the splash *image* can't be the bulk of this (it's one full-screen blit into a single 4 MB tile). Most of this 1.75 s is **LEGATO finishing the 200+ widget dashboard** — the paint that started in window 1 but didn't complete because it was sharing the CPU with VideoTask and the card-wait idle. And backlight-on sits *after* this window, so the dashboard paint is gating when the splash becomes visible.

## Two real levers (priority shaping is not one of them)

**Lever A — defer non-essential task spawns to post-splash (our code, cheap, safe).** VideoTask (14.6%) and PerfDrain are eating CPU during the card-wait that LEGATO could use to *finish the dashboard while we're blocked on the card anyway*. There's 35.7% idle in window 1 — spare CPU — but Video is still stealing ~360 ms. Move `Video_Initialize`, `PerfLog_Start`, detector, gameplay, etc. out of [`APP_Initialize`](firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c#L102) into the loader's post-`RevealDashboard` phase. This is exactly your "gate other tasks until the splash is up" idea — and the data now justifies it (it's *render* contention, not SD). Likely collapses most of window 2's dashboard tail into the card-wait.

**Lever B — cut the card-ready floor (MCC config + retry logic).** The ~1.3 s is retry quanta + the SDMMC driver's `DRV_SDMMC_RTOS_DELAY_IDX0 = 10 ms`-per-step pacing (consistent with 0% CPU). Two parts: (1) lower that delay in MCC and regenerate (allowed — it's a config value, not a hand-edit); (2) collapse the double-retry so we proceed the instant the card is ready instead of in 1 s + 300 ms chunks.

## Recommendation

Start with **Lever A** — it's the cleanest, touches only code we own, directly tests the render-contention theory, and should shrink the 1.75 s render window by letting the dashboard finish during the card-wait. Then re-run BootProfile, and go after **Lever B**'s card-ready floor.

Want me to do Lever A: pull the non-essential task spawns (video, perf, detector, gameplay, manual) out of `APP_Initialize` and start them from the loader after the dashboard is revealed?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 11:03:08Z)**_

I dug into the SDMMC driver to answer the card-detect question concretely. Here are direct answers to all five.

## 1. What is the SD card-detect delay?

Our config is `DRV_SDMMC_CD_METHOD_POLLING` (not the SDCD line), so the driver **skips** the 250 ms card-detect debounce and goes straight to media init. The delay is the **media-init sequence itself**, dominated by the **ACMD41 power-up loop**: [`lDRV_SDMMC_SendOpCond_ACMD41`](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/driver/sdmmc/src/drv_sdmmc.c#L1580) repeats CMD55+ACMD41 until the card reports "internal init complete" (response bit 31), with a **2000 ms timeout**. How long the card takes to set that bit is its own intrinsic power-up time. On top of that, every command step is paced by the SDMMC task's `DRV_SDMMC_RTOS_DELAY_IDX0 = 10 ms` tick (the state machine advances ~one poll per tick).

So "card-detect delay" = card intrinsic power-up (ACMD41 ready) + the CMD0/CMD8/ACMD41/CMD2/CMD3/CMD9/CMD7 sequence at 10 ms/step + **our** retry quantization. The `STG: mount failed (err 3)` → `mounted` confirms the first `Storage_Mount` (50×20 ms = 1 s) ran *while the card was still in this power-up loop*, returned `FR_NOT_READY`, then we slept 300 ms and the retry caught it. Net: the card became ready somewhere around **~1.0–1.3 s**, and it's **wait, not compute** (SDMMC at 0% CPU). It's not detection that's slow — it's card power-up + our coarse retry. (I can pin the exact card-ready instant with one more `BootProfile_Mark` between mount-success and the file read if you want the precise number.)

## 2. Is Legato rendering the dashboard while we wait for the SD?

**Yes.** LEGATO at 45.3% during `mount + read` = ~1.1 s of painting. All screens are built pre-scheduler and marked dirty, so LEGATO paints dashboard + nav + solid-fill splash from the moment the scheduler starts. That overlap is free and good.

## 3. Is the dashboard ready before we even show the splash?

**Yes — confirmed your suspicion.** Backlight-on (splash becomes visible) happens *after* [`wait_render_idle()`](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/loader.c#L113), and that waits for the **entire** frame — splash image **and** the dashboard tail — to go idle. So by the time the splash lights up, the dashboard is already fully painted behind it. Then the splash shows for the 1200 ms hold over a finished dashboard, and the reveal is just a canvas-hide. We're paying to finish the whole dashboard *before* showing the splash. Backwards for "splash fast."

(One nuance: the dashboard is only ~40% painted at the end of window 1 — the remaining ~1.6 s of its paint is exactly what makes window 2 take 1.75 s. So the splash is waiting on the dashboard's tail.)

## 4. Are we 100% prioritizing the splash once the SD is ready?

**No.** Once the card's ready and the JPEG is read, we block on global render-idle, which lumps the splash image together with finishing the dashboard. The splash is on its own OVR2 canvas but `leRenderer_IsIdle()` is global, so we don't light the panel the instant the splash alone is composited — we wait for the dashboard too. Within LEGATO there's no sub-priority for the splash canvas.

## 5. Since you're OK with the splash up longer — the fix

This is the clean lever. **Decouple backlight-on from dashboard completion:** light the panel as soon as the *splash image alone* is painted, then let the dashboard paint behind the opaque splash during a longer hold, and reveal when the hold elapses (dashboard guaranteed done by then).

Concretely:
- Build + attach **only the splash** pre-scheduler; load JPEG → paint splash (cheap, one full-screen blit) → **backlight on** as soon as it's idle. Splash appears right after card-ready instead of after the full dashboard render.
- *Then* attach dashboard + nav and let them paint during the (now longer) hold.
- Reveal when the hold expires.

Trade-off to call out: this gives up the ~1.1 s of free dashboard-paint that currently overlaps the card-wait, so the dashboard's full ~2.7 s paint moves into the hold — fine since you want a longer splash, and **Lever A** (deferring VideoTask/PerfDrain/detector spawns out of `APP_Initialize`) frees the CPU so that 2.7 s shrinks and we can keep the hold shorter. **Lever B** (lower the 10 ms SDMMC pacing in MCC + collapse the double-retry) still attacks the ~1–1.3 s card-ready floor underneath all of this.

Recommended order: **(5) splash-first reveal** (biggest win for your actual goal) → **(A) defer task spawns** → **(B) card-ready floor**. Want me to start on the splash-first restructure?

You're right to be skeptical — and the data actually doesn't prove the card takes 2 s. Let me separate the two before I touch code, because it changes what I instrument while I'm in the loader.

**The 2.4 s is mostly our retry padding, not the card.** That window is: first `Storage_Mount` burning its full **50×20 ms = 1 s** failing, **+300 ms** loader sleep, **+** the second (successful) mount **+** the 337 KB read. What it tells us for certain is only that the card wasn't mountable within the *first 1 s* — but whether that's the card's intrinsic power-up, the driver's 10 ms-per-step pacing through the CMD0/CMD8/ACMD41/CMD2/CMD3 sequence, or just our coarse 20 ms+300 ms quantization, the current marks **can't distinguish**. I share your gut: a card that's already seated shouldn't need a full second.

So while I'm restructuring the loader, I'll **collapse the double-retry into a single tight poll** (~10 ms granularity, no 1 s + 300 ms chunks) and log elapsed-at-first-success. That does two things at once: kills the padding (Lever B), and the next boot prints the *true* card-ready latency so we stop guessing. If it comes back ~150 ms, great — the 2 s was entirely our artifact. If it's genuinely ~800 ms, we go after the 10 ms SDMMC pacing in MCC.

```text
140	static void loader_task(void *param)
141	{
142	    (void)param;
143	
144	    /* The splash, dashboard, and nav were built on their own canvases by
145	     * UiManager_Initialize (pre-scheduler); the Legato render task is now
146	     * painting them (backlight still off). Load the splash image, wait for the
147	     * render to finish, then light the panel — the first lit frame is the
148	     * fully-painted splash, with the dashboard finished behind it on BASE. No
149	     * image (no card / too large) → the panel's solid fill is the fallback. */
150	    BootProfile_Mark("loader start");
151	
152	    /* Mount the card and read the splash JPEG. Storage_Mount polls until the
153	     * SDMMC driver finishes card analysis and logs how long that took, so this
154	     * is one bounded attempt — no outer retry needed. No image (no card / too
155	     * large) → the panel's solid fill is the fallback. */
156	    uint32_t len = load_splash_file();
157	    BootProfile_Mark("mount + read");
158	    if (!((len > 0u) && Splash_SetImageJpeg(s_jpeg, len)))
159	    {

161	    }
162	
163	    /* Only the splash is attached to the renderer right now (ui_manager detached
164	     * the dashboard + nav), so render-idle here means the splash alone is painted
165	     * — light the panel immediately, without waiting on the heavy dashboard. */
166	    wait_render_idle();
167	    BootProfile_Mark("splash painted");
168	    UiManager_EnableBacklight();
169	    TickType_t shown_at = xTaskGetTickCount();
170	
171	    /* Splash is up. Now pull the dashboard + nav into the render path; they paint
172	     * behind the opaque splash while it's held, off the splash-to-screen path. */
173	    UiManager_AttachMainScreens();
174	
175	    /* --- Asset pre-load goes here (album art → DDR cache, etc.). The 32bpp
176	     * splash buffer (ui_manager) is free to reuse as decode scratch once the
177	     * splash leaves the screen. None yet. --- */
178	
179	    /* Wait for the dashboard to finish painting (bounded) so the reveal never
180	     * shows a partial frame, then hold the splash at least SPLASH_MIN_MS so a
181	     * fast paint doesn't flash it away. */
182	    wait_render_idle();
183	    BootProfile_Mark("dashboard painted");
184	    TickType_t elapsed   = xTaskGetTickCount() - shown_at;
185	    TickType_t min_ticks = pdMS_TO_TICKS(SPLASH_MIN_MS);
186	    if (elapsed < min_ticks) { vTaskDelay(min_ticks - elapsed); }
187	
188	    /* Drop the splash → the dashboard (painted behind it) is revealed, complete.
189	     * Then bring the camera up. */
```

## Splash-first restructure

**[ui_manager.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.c):** still builds all three screens pre-scheduler (no construction race), but now **detaches** the dashboard + nav roots at the end of init so only the splash paints when the scheduler starts. New `UiManager_AttachMainScreens()` re-attaches them — and crucially this mirrors the post-scheduler `leRemoveRootWidget` that `RevealDashboard` already does in shipped code, so it's the same class of operation, not a new hazard.

**[loader.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/loader.c):** new sequence — load JPEG → wait for splash-alone render-idle → **backlight on** (splash now appears as soon as card+decode allow, not gated behind the 200+ widget dashboard) → `AttachMainScreens` (dashboard/nav paint behind the opaque splash) → bounded render-idle wait (reveal never shows a partial frame) → min-hold → reveal. `SPLASH_MIN_MS` 1200 → 1500.

The trade-off, as discussed: we give up the ~1.1 s of dashboard paint that used to overlap the card-wait, so the full dashboard paint moves into the hold — which is fine since you wanted the splash up longer, and the splash will now naturally linger ~as long as the dashboard takes to paint behind it.

## SD card — measure the real latency

You're right to doubt the 2 s. **[storage.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/storage/storage.c):** collapsed the double-retry (removed the loader's 5×300 ms wrapper; tightened `Storage_Mount` from 50×20 ms to 300×10 ms) so we proceed the instant the card is ready, and it now logs **elapsed-at-mount**. Next boot you'll see:

```
STG: mounted /dev/mmcblka1 at /mnt/marvin (NNN ms)
```

That `NNN` is the truth. If it's ~150–300 ms, the old 2 s was entirely our retry quantization and we're done. If it's genuinely ~800 ms+, it's the SDMMC media-init (POLLING mode skips the 250 ms debounce; the ACMD41 power-up loop is paced by `DRV_SDMMC_RTOS_DELAY_IDX0 = 10 ms`), and the next lever is lowering that 10 ms in MCC.

The `BOOTPROF` marks are now `loader start → mount + read → splash painted → dashboard painted`, so you'll see exactly how long the splash-alone paint takes vs. the dashboard tail.

It won't build from here — needs your MPLAB build. When you run it, paste the `STG: mounted (… ms)` line and the new `BOOTPROF` windows and we'll decide whether **Lever A** (deferring the video/perf/detector task spawns to post-reveal) is worth doing to shrink the dashboard paint. Journal's updated with the analysis and the pending items.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 11:17:28Z)**_

Two big findings, and one of them overturns what the journal previously concluded.

## Card-ready is genuinely ~1.27 s — not our padding

`STG: mounted … (1272 ms)` with the tight 10 ms poll proves it: we now proceed the instant the card is ready, and it's still **1272 ms**. So your skepticism was half-right — the old 2.4 s was inflated by retry quantization (now gone), but there's a real ~1.27 s floor underneath. It's **idle waiting** (62.2% IDLE in that window, SDMMC at 0% CPU): the SDMMC media-init walking CMD0/CMD8/ACMD41/CMD2/CMD3 with each step paced by the driver's `DRV_SDMMC_RTOS_DELAY_IDX0 = 10 ms` tick, plus the card's intrinsic ACMD41 power-up. **Lever B-part-2:** lower that 10 ms in MCC and re-measure — if the number drops, it was pacing; if it holds near 1.27 s, it's the card's own power-up and we've hit the floor.

## The splash JPEG decode is the real bottleneck — 1.77 s

This is the surprise. The **splash painted** window — with *only the splash attached* — is **1767 ms at 88.2% LEGATO**. That's the JPEG decode + full-screen blit of the splash *alone*. My earlier "the dashboard is the cost" theory was wrong: the dashboard paint is actually **cheaper** (the `dashboard painted` window is 1311 ms). The journal's prior call — *"decode isn't the bottleneck, don't chase a RAW asset"* — is contradicted by this data. A 337 KB / 1280×800 baseline JPEG taking 1.55 s of CPU is an unoptimized software decoder, and it's now the single largest item on the splash critical path.

## What this means for the levers

The splash-first restructure worked: **splash now appears at ~3.0 s (card 1.27 s + decode 1.77 s), down from ~4.2 s**, dashboard at ~4.5 s. But note the critical path is now **two uncontended serial segments** — card-ready is 62% idle, the decode is 88% single-task LEGATO with 7% idle. **CPU contention is no longer the problem**, which means **Lever A (deferring VideoTask/etc.) is now low-value for splash latency** — VideoTask is at 0% during the decode; there's nothing to steal back. I'd shelve Lever A.

The two real levers, both attacking serial floor time:

1. **Kill the decode (~1.77 s → ~0.3 s): pre-decoded RAW splash.** Store the splash as raw RGBA8888 (4 MB, matches `s_fb_splash`) and read it straight into the canvas buffer — no JPEG decode, no Legato image-widget paint at all, just a file read + damage. Biggest single win. Cost: a 4 MB asset on the card and a small change to the splash path.
2. **Overlap or cut the card-ready (~1.27 s).** Two sub-options: (a) lower the SDMMC RTOS delay in MCC (cheap test); (b) move the splash asset **off the SD into the firmware image** so the splash paints while the card mounts in parallel — that removes card-ready from the splash path entirely (the SD mount + dashboard happen behind the already-shown splash).

The ceiling: **RAW asset in the firmware image** → splash appears in ~0.3 s (just the blit), card mount fully hidden behind it. Cost is a 4 MB-larger binary (fine in DDR; slower JTAG load). RAW-on-SD is the lighter compromise (~1.57 s: still pays the mount, skips the decode).

## My recommendation

Do the **RAW splash** (lever 1) — it's the biggest, most certain win and it's all in code we own. In parallel, you do the one-line **MCC `DRV_SDMMC_RTOS_DELAY` drop** and re-measure to see if the 1.27 s card floor is pacing or intrinsic. Decide on in-flash-vs-on-SD for the asset based on whether you want to pay 4 MB of binary to also hide the mount.

Which way do you want to take the RAW asset — keep it on the SD (lighter, splash ~1.57 s), or embed it in the image (splash ~0.3 s, mount fully overlapped, +4 MB binary)?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 11:25:36Z)**_

That's the smoking gun. Here are the priorities:

| task | priority | source |
|---|---|---|
| **VideoTask** | **4** | `video/video.c:20` (ours) |
| USB device / UDPHS | 3 | generated |
| **PerfDrain** | **3** | `perf_log/perf_log.c:20` (ours) |
| GFX_CANVAS / XLCDC / LEGATO / MAXTOUCH / SYS_INPUT | 2 | generated |
| LoaderTask | 2 | ours |
| **DRV_SDMMC0 / SYS_FS** | **1** | generated (MCC) |

Your hypothesis is mechanically confirmed. **VideoTask is priority 4 — the highest task in the system — and the SD driver + filesystem are at priority 1, the floor.** Under FreeRTOS's strict-priority scheduler, whenever VideoTask (or PerfDrain at 3) is ready, the prio-1 SD tasks **cannot run at all** — not "share the CPU," but are fully starved until the higher task blocks. So the 27.2% aggregate for VideoTask is almost certainly front-loaded into its capture-pipeline init burst (ISC + TC358743 I2C bring-up), and during that burst the SDMMC state machine simply doesn't advance. The window % can't show that concentration, but the priority table tells you it's not just *possible*, it's *guaranteed* whenever Video is runnable.

## On your conceptual question — is SD bring-up inherently slow?

No, and your instinct is right. Breaking down where time can actually go:

- **The bus commands** (CMD0/CMD8/CMD2/CMD3/CMD9/CMD7): each is a few bytes at 400 kHz then full clock — *microseconds*. Not significant.
- **The FS mount**: FatFs reads the MBR + boot sector + maybe FSInfo — a handful of 512 B sectors, single-digit ms. Not significant.
- **The one genuinely card-dependent part — ACMD41**: the card does its internal power-up (charge pumps, controller boot) and the host polls CMD55+ACMD41 until the card sets its ready bit. The spec *allows* up to 1 s; real cards are usually tens to low-hundreds of ms. This is the only legitimate silicon-side latency.

Everything above that floor in our measurement was **software**: the 10 ms-per-step driver pacing (you just clawed ~470 ms back by dropping it to 1 ms) and — the part you just identified — **higher-priority tasks preempting the prio-1 SD tasks during init**. The card's actual work is quick; we were stalling it.

## The decisive test (and the fix)

Defer **VideoTask** and **PerfDrain** out of `APP_Initialize` into the loader's post-reveal phase, then re-measure the mount. This is exactly Lever A, now strongly justified by the priority data rather than guessed:
- Video go-live is *already* deferred to post-reveal — the video task doing its init burst during boot serves nothing on the splash path, so moving its whole `Video_Initialize` to post-reveal costs us nothing and removes the prio-4 preemption.
- If the mount time drops again after this, your "Video hogs the first ~500 ms" theory is confirmed in one shot.

If you'd rather *see* the timeline than infer it, I can also add a time-sliced sampler (snapshot the run-time counters every ~25 ms across the mount window and dump a mini-timeline) — but given Video is prio 4 vs SD at prio 1, I'd just defer-and-remeasure; it's both the experiment and the cure.

Want me to move `Video_Initialize` and `PerfLog_Start` to the loader's post-reveal phase and leave the rest of `APP_Initialize` as-is for now?

```text
/* ─── Task body ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static void video_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    /* One-time init in task context (scheduler running, so synchronous I²C
     * and SYS_TIME work). Brings up capture pipeline, TC358743 bridge, and
     * parks the panel in UI-only mode. The backlight is NOT enabled here — the
     * boot loader enables it (UiManager_EnableBacklight) once the splash is on
     * screen, so the panel never shows a pre-splash/garbage frame. */
    ISC_Capture_Initialize();
    ISC_Capture_SetFrameCallback(on_frame_done, 0);
    TC358743_Initialize();
    lcd_unbind();

    for (;;)
    {
        TC358743_Tasks();
        reconcile();
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(VIDEO_POLL_MS));
    }
}

/* ─── Public API ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static StackType_t  s_task_stack[VIDEO_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t s_task_tcb;

void Video_Initialize(void)
{
    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(video_task,
                                       "VideoTask",
                                       VIDEO_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
                                       NULL,
                                       VIDEO_TASK_PRIORITY,
                                       s_task_stack,
                                       &s_task_tcb);
    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_VIDEO, h);
}

void Video_CaptureEnable(void)  { s_capture_enabled = true;  }
void Video_CaptureDisable(void) { s_capture_enabled = false; }
```

Done. Here's what changed for the task deferral.

## What I did

**[app.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c) — split boot into two phases:**
- `APP_Initialize` now creates **only what the splash needs**: logging, `UiManager_Initialize`, PerfLog queues, Storage/Results/Catalog state (no tasks), and the loader.
- New **`App_StartServices()`** holds everything that spawns a task above SD's priority: Video, Detector, FretboardLink (which also brings up T1S), TimingPipeline, ManualControl, GameplayEngine, Console, and the PerfLog drain — in dependency order (Video first; the detector + gameplay observer subscribe to its frame queue).

**[app.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/app.h):** declared `App_StartServices`.

**[loader.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/loader.c):** after `UiManager_RevealDashboard()`, the loader calls `App_StartServices()`, then does the camera go-live (which is just intent flags the now-running video task reconciles, so ordering is safe).

Net effect: during the card mount + splash render, the **only** tasks running are the SD/FS drivers, the render tasks, and the loader. Nothing of ours preempts the prio-1 SD tasks anymore.

## What to look for on the next boot

The decisive line is the **`BOOTPROF [mount + read]`** window:
- It was **848 ms** with VideoTask (prio 4) eating 27% of it. If your "Video hogs the first ~500 ms" theory is right, this should now drop noticeably — the residual is the card's genuine ACMD41 power-up floor (the part that's actually silicon, not software).
- VideoTask should no longer appear in that window at all (it doesn't exist yet).

The **1.77 s splash decode** is now the biggest single item on the splash path, and it's pure software JPEG decode. RAW is the lever for it — kept on the SD (skip decode, ~split-second) or in-image (also hides the mount). Boost reverted, journal updated. Where the SD investigation lands:

## SD is at its floor

- **mount 411 ms, read 38 ms** (337 KB → ~8.7 MB/s, near the card's sequential bandwidth — read is done).
- SYS_FS delay 10→1 ms shaved another ~30 ms → **mount ~381 ms**.
- The priority boost did nothing, which definitively closes it: the SD tasks were never CPU-starved, so the ~380 ms is the card's own ACMD41 power-up plus residual driver self-pacing. Priority and contention are off the table.

The only ways further down are diminishing (sub-1 ms driver pacing = generated edits) or *hiding* the mount by putting the splash in the firmware image so the decode overlaps it. Not worth chasing on its own.

## The real remaining prize

Splash-visible is now **~2.2 s** (mount 381 + read 38 + decode ~1767), down from ~4.2 s when we started. The breakdown is now lopsided:

| segment | time | nature |
|---|---|---|
| SD mount | ~381 ms | card floor — done |
| file read | ~38 ms | done |
| **JPEG decode + paint** | **~1767 ms** | **software decode — the lever** |

The decode is ~80% of the splash path and worth ~10× anything left on the SD side. That's the RAW-asset decision you flagged earlier:

- **RAW on SD** → skip the decode entirely (read ~4 MB raw straight into the splash canvas buffer, no JPEG, no Legato image paint). Splash ≈ mount 381 + ~300 ms read ≈ **~0.7 s**. Keeps it on the card (changeable), at the cost of a 4 MB file + a small splash-path change.
- **RAW in firmware image** → also hides the mount (decode/blit overlaps it). Splash ≈ **~0.3 s**. Costs 4 MB of binary and gives up easy swapping — your stated dispreference.

Given you want to keep it swappable, **RAW-on-SD** is the natural next step and gets you most of the win (~2.2 s → ~0.7 s) without baking anything in. Want me to implement that — generate a raw asset from the splash and add a raw-load path that blits straight into `s_fb_splash`, bypassing the JPEG decoder? Or are you happy enough at 2.2 s to leave it here for now?

Done — raw generated and the firmware wired to use it.

## What I did

**Generated the asset** — `data/ui/splash.raw`, **3,072,000 bytes** (1280×800 × 3, RGB888, row-major R,G,B), via Pillow under uv:
```
Image.open("splash.jpg").convert("RGB").tobytes()
```
I kept `splash.jpg` as the master; regenerate the `.raw` the same way if the art changes. I chose **RGB888** because it matches the mode the old JPEG path already decoded to (`LE_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888`), so the byte order is proven — lowest risk of color swap.

**Firmware:**
- [screen_splash.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/splash/screen_splash.c)/[.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/splash/screen_splash.h): `Splash_SetImageJpeg` → `Splash_SetImageRaw`, leImage now `LE_IMAGE_FORMAT_RAW` with `buffer.mode = RGB_888`. Legato blits the raw pixels straight to the canvas (converting RGB888→RGBA8888 on blit) — no decode.
- [loader.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/loader.c): path → `/ui/splash.raw`; staging buffer `s_jpeg[1 MB]` → `s_raw[3 MB]` in `.region_nocache` (so SD DMA-in and the blit-out are coherent with no cache fuss, and there's plenty of room — 32 MB region, ~11 MB used); exact-size check since raw has no header.

## To test (your side)

1. Build in MPLAB.
2. **Copy `data/ui/splash.raw` onto the SD card at `/ui/splash.raw`** (the old `splash.jpg` is no longer read; you can leave it).
3. Boot and watch for:
   - **Colors correct?** If the splash looks color-swapped (red↔blue), Legato's `RGB_888` is BGR — I'll flip the byte order in the generator. (Unlikely, since the JPEG path used the same mode.)
   - **`BOOTPROF [splash painted]` window** — should drop from ~1767 ms to a few hundred ms. The `read in … ms` line will now show ~350 ms (3 MB vs 38 KB) but that's traded against eliminating the ~1.77 s decode.

Expected net: splash-visible ~2.2 s → **~0.8 s**.

If the convert-blit turns out slower than hoped, the next step is RGBA8888 + the `LE_IMAGE_DIRECT_BLIT` fast path (straight memcpy, no conversion) — I noted that in the journal. Paste the new `BOOTPROF` windows and the color result when you've run it.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 12:18:35Z)**_

Found it. A GPU **is** registered (`leInitialize(&gfxDriverInterface, &gfxGPUInterface)`), and the raw decoder's `INTERNAL + RAW` branch hands the buffer straight to `leGPU_BlitBuffer` *first* (line 314) — whereas the JPEG path skips that branch and uses the software convert stages. The SAM9X75 2D GPU almost certainly can't blit a 24bpp RGB888 source into a 32bpp target, so it produces nothing → blank. The JPEG path worked precisely because it never hit the GPU blit.

The clean fix: make the source match the canvas exactly (RGBA8888) and use the `LE_IMAGE_DIRECT_BLIT` memcpy path — no GPU, no conversion. I need Legato's exact RGBA_8888 byte order.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 12:19:41Z)**_

That's the answer: RGBA_8888 packs as `0xRRGGBBAA` (masks `R=0xFF000000 … A=0x000000FF`), so in little-endian memory each pixel is bytes **[A, B, G, R]**. And `LE_IMAGE_DIRECT_BLIT` exists. So the fix is: regenerate the raw as RGBA8888 in that exact byte order (opaque A=0xFF) and set the direct-blit flag — a pure memcpy into the canvas, no GPU, no conversion.

Let me regenerate the asset:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 12:19:49Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Regenerate splash.raw as RGBA8888 in Legato byte order

```bash
cd /Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin && export UV_CACHE_DIR="$TMPDIR/uv-cache" && uv run --no-project --with pillow python3 - <<'PY'
from PIL import Image
src, dst = "data/ui/splash.jpg", "data/ui/splash.raw"
im = Image.open(src).convert("RGB")
assert im.size == (1280, 800), im.size
r, g, b = im.split()
a = Image.new("L", im.size, 255)                  # opaque
# Legato RGBA_8888 = packed 0xRRGGBBAA → little-endian memory bytes [A,B,G,R].
# merge in physical channel order (A,B,G,R); tobytes() writes bands in that order.
out = Image.merge("RGBA", (a, b, g, r))
data = out.tobytes()
open(dst, "wb").write(data)
print("wrote", dst, len(data), "bytes  (", im.size[0], "x", im.size[1], "x4, ABGR-bytes/opaque )")
PY
ls -la data/ui/splash.raw
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 12:21:16Z)**_

Good news in the blank: the decode is gone (`splash painted` **1767 → 261 ms**), so the raw path is doing its job — it's purely that the pixels weren't getting drawn.

## Why it was blank

The raw decoder's `INTERNAL + RAW` branch hands the buffer **straight to the 2D GPU** before any software path (legato_imagedecoder_raw.c:298), and a GPU *is* registered (`leInitialize(…, &gfxGPUInterface)`). The SAM9X75 2D GPU can't blit a **24bpp RGB888** source into the **32bpp** canvas, so it drew nothing. The JPEG path never hit that branch (it's not `RAW`), which is why it worked. RGB888 was the wrong call.

## The fix (done)

Match the source to the canvas exactly and bypass the GPU:
- **RGBA8888** source = same mode as the OVR2 layer, plus the **`LE_IMAGE_DIRECT_BLIT`** flag → the decoder `memcpy`s the pixels straight into the render buffer. No GPU, no conversion.
- Byte order pinned from `legato_color.c`: RGBA_8888 packs `0xRRGGBBAA`, so little-endian memory is **`[A,B,G,R]`** per pixel — that's exactly how I regenerated the file (opaque A=0xFF).

Changes: `data/ui/splash.raw` is now **4,096,000 B**; `screen_splash.c` uses `RGBA_8888` + `LE_IMAGE_DIRECT_BLIT`; loader buffer is 4 MB.

## To test

1. Rebuild.
2. **Re-copy `data/ui/splash.raw` to the card** (it's the new 4 MB version — the old 3 MB file will now fail the exact-size check and fall back to solid-fill).
3. Boot — you should see the actual splash image now, opaque, correct colors.

If colors come out swapped this time (e.g. red↔blue), it means the XLCDC RGBA_8888 channel order differs from Legato's packing and I'll swap the byte order in the generator — but since this matches `legato_color.c` exactly, I expect it correct.

Timing should land around: mount ~340 ms + read ~450 ms (4 MB) + blit (tens of ms) → **splash-visible ~0.8–0.9 s**, down from ~4.2 s when we started. Paste the `BOOTPROF` windows and whether the image looks right.

```text
=== _directBlit impl ===
static void _directBlit(const lePixelBuffer* src,
                        const leRect* srcRect,
                        const leRect* destRect)
{
    void* srcPtr;
    void* destPtr;
    lePixelBuffer dest;
    int32_t row, rowSize;
    leRect frameRect;

    leRenderer_GetFrameRect(&frameRect);

    dest.pixel_count = leGetRenderBuffer()->pixel_count;
    dest.size.width = leGetRenderBuffer()->size.width;
    dest.size.height = leGetRenderBuffer()->size.height;
    dest.mode = leGetRenderBuffer()->mode;
    dest.buffer_length = leGetRenderBuffer()->buffer_length;
    dest.pixels = (gfxBuffer)leGetRenderBuffer()->pixels;

    rowSize = srcRect->width * gfxColorInfoTable[src->mode].size;

    for(row = 0; row < srcRect->height; row++)
    {
        srcPtr = lePixelBufferOffsetGet(src, srcRect->x, srcRect->y + row);
        destPtr = lePixelBufferOffsetGet(&dest, destRect->x - frameRect.x, destRect->y - frameRect.y + row);

        memcpy(destPtr, srcPtr, rowSize);
    }
}
```

```text
94	    {
95	        size_t want = (size_t)((uint32_t)sz - total);
96	        if (want > SPLASH_READ_CHUNK) { want = SPLASH_READ_CHUNK; }
97	
98	        size_t got = SYS_FS_FileRead(h, &s_raw[total], want);
99	        if (got == 0u || got == (size_t)-1) { err = true; break; }
100	        total += (uint32_t)got;
101	    }
102	    (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);
103	
104	    if (err || total != (uint32_t)sz)
105	    {
106	        LOG_WARN("LOADER: splash read short %lu/%ld\r\n", (unsigned long)total, (long)sz);
107	        return 0u;
108	    }
109	    uint32_t read_ms = (uint32_t)((xTaskGetTickCount() - read_t0) * portTICK_PERIOD_MS);
110	    LOG_INFO("LOADER: splash %lu B read in %lu ms\r\n",
111	             (unsigned long)total, (unsigned long)read_ms);
112	    return total;
113	}
114	
115	/* Block until the Legato render task has fully painted all pending damage.
116	 *
117	 * We do NOT drive leUpdate ourselves — the normal LEGATO_Tasks + GFX_CANVAS_Task
118	 * pair renders the full screen correctly (a full-screen surface spans several
119	 * scratch tiles, and the scratch is freed by the canvas commit between render
120	 * passes; that only happens when those tasks actually run). So the loader just
121	 * yields and polls the public idle flag. First wait for the task to pick up the
122	 * queued damage (go busy), then wait for it to finish — both bounded so a render
123	 * stall can't hang boot. */
124	static void wait_render_idle(void)
125	{
126	    TickType_t  deadline   = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS);
127	    TickType_t  idle_since = 0;
128	    bool        idle_run   = false;
129	
130	    while (xTaskGetTickCount() < deadline)
131	    {
132	        if (leRenderer_IsIdle())
133	        {
134	            /* Idle must hold continuously — a lone idle sample is just an
135	             * inter-frame gap, not a finished paint. */
136	            if (!idle_run)
137	            {
138	                idle_run   = true;
139	                idle_since = xTaskGetTickCount();
140	            }
141	            else if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - idle_since) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_STABLE_MS))
142	            {
143	                return;
144	            }
145	        }
146	        else
147	        {
148	            idle_run = false;   /* a frame started → reset the streak */
149	        }
150	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_POLL_MS));
151	    }
152	    LOG_WARN("LOADER: render-idle wait timed out\r\n");
153	}
154	
155	static void loader_task(void *param)
156	{
157	    (void)param;
158	
159	    /* UiManager_Initialize built all screens pre-scheduler but left only the
160	     * splash attached to the renderer (dashboard + nav detached). So the splash
161	     * is the only thing painting now, with the backlight still off. Sequence:
162	     * load + show the splash, light the panel, then attach the dashboard + nav so
163	     * they paint behind the splash while it's held, then reveal. */
164	    BootProfile_Mark("loader start");
165	
166	    /* Mount the card and read the splash JPEG. Storage_Mount polls until the
167	     * SDMMC driver finishes card analysis and logs how long that took, so this
168	     * is one bounded attempt — no outer retry needed. No image (no card / too
169	     * large) → the panel's solid fill is the fallback. */
170	    uint32_t len = load_splash_file();
171	    BootProfile_Mark("mount + read");
172	    if (!((len > 0u) && Splash_SetImageRaw(s_raw, len)))
173	    {
174	        LOG_WARN("LOADER: solid-fill splash (no image)\r\n");
175	    }
176	
177	    /* Only the splash is attached to the renderer right now (ui_manager detached
178	     * the dashboard + nav), so render-idle here means the splash alone is painted
179	     * — light the panel immediately, without waiting on the heavy dashboard. */
180	    wait_render_idle();
181	    BootProfile_Mark("splash painted");
182	    UiManager_EnableBacklight();
183	    TickType_t shown_at = xTaskGetTickCount();
184	
185	    /* Splash is up. Now pull the dashboard + nav into the render path; they paint
186	     * behind the opaque splash while it's held, off the splash-to-screen path. */
187	    UiManager_AttachMainScreens();
188	
189	    /* --- Asset pre-load goes here (album art → DDR cache, etc.). The 32bpp
190	     * splash buffer (ui_manager) is free to reuse as decode scratch once the
191	     * splash leaves the screen. None yet. --- */
192	
193	    /* Wait for the dashboard to finish painting (bounded) so the reveal never
194	     * shows a partial frame, then hold the splash at least SPLASH_MIN_MS so a
195	     * fast paint doesn't flash it away. */
196	    wait_render_idle();
197	    BootProfile_Mark("dashboard painted");
198	    TickType_t elapsed   = xTaskGetTickCount() - shown_at;
199	    TickType_t min_ticks = pdMS_TO_TICKS(SPLASH_MIN_MS);
200	    if (elapsed < min_ticks) { vTaskDelay(min_ticks - elapsed); }
201	
202	    /* Drop the splash → the dashboard (painted behind it) is revealed, complete. */
203	    UiManager_RevealDashboard();
204	
205	    /* Splash handoff done — bring up the deferred subsystems (video, detector,
206	     * actuator links, gameplay, console, perf drain). Held off until now so
207	     * their higher-priority tasks didn't preempt the SD mount + splash render. */
208	    App_StartServices();
209	
210	    /* Camera go-live: these just set intent flags the (now-running) video task
211	     * reconciles, so the order relative to Video_Initialize above is benign. */
212	    Video_SetWindow(VIDEO_WIN_X, VIDEO_WIN_Y, VIDEO_WIN_W, VIDEO_WIN_H);
213	    Video_CaptureEnable();
214	    Video_DisplayShow();
215	
216	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
217	}
218	
219	void Loader_Start(void)
220	{
221	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(loader_task, "LoaderTask", LOADER_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
222	                            NULL, LOADER_TASK_PRIORITY, s_task_stack, &s_task_tcb);
223	}
224
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 12:34:37Z)**_

Done — the splash is now a pure framebuffer, exactly as you described.

## What changed

The 1462 ms was `_directBlit` doing two 4 MB `memcpy` passes through nocache (source → Legato render buffer → canvas). I confirmed in `gfx_canvas.c` that `_gfxcCanvasUpdate` programs the **OVR2 layer base address = `s_fb_splash`** directly — so that buffer *is* the scanout. So:

- **[ui_manager.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.c):** the splash is no longer a Legato screen at all — just set up the OVR2 canvas (RGBA8888, shown), pre-fill opaque black as the no-card fallback, and the RGBMODE poke. Added `UiManager_SplashFramebuffer(&bytes)` (hands out `s_fb_splash`) and `UiManager_CommitSplash()` (re-latch OVR2). `RevealDashboard` just hides the canvas now — and since the splash has no Legato root, the old touch-swallowing problem can't come back.
- **[loader.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/loader.c):** reads `splash.raw` **straight into `s_fb_splash`** — the SD read *is* the load. No staging buffer, no decode, no blit, no render wait. Backlight on right after.
- **Deleted** `ui/screens/splash/screen_splash.{c,h}` (the image-widget wrapper, now dead) and its build entry. Asset unchanged (4 MB RGBA8888).

## To test

1. Rebuild (note: `screen_splash.c` is gone from the build, and `splash.raw` is already on your card from last time).
2. Boot.

Expected: the splash paint cost drops to ~zero — the only splash cost is the ~450 ms SD read of the 4 MB file, now folded into the `mount + read` window (~830 ms). There's no more `splash painted` window (I removed that wait). **Splash-visible ≈ mount 380 + read 450 ≈ ~0.8 s**, down from ~4.2 s when we started.

If the image shows correctly, we're essentially done — the splash is as fast as the SD card can deliver it, and the dashboard paints behind it during the hold. Paste the `mount + read` window and confirm the image looks right.

   Dropping the Splash *screen* shouldn't reduce any of these below what we need, but it's worth a glance after regen.
