git commit -F - <<'EOF'
marvin: fast boot splash — direct framebuffer + deferred tasks (~5s → ~0.8s)

Splash now appears in ~0.8 s (was ~4.2–5 s). Reworked the boot path so the
splash comes up as soon as the SD card can deliver it, with everything else
moved off the splash critical path.

- Splash is a raw RGBA8888 framebuffer (data/ui/splash.raw) read straight into
  the OVR2 scanout buffer — the SD read IS the load. No JPEG decode (~1.77 s),
  no Legato widget/render, no blit. Retired the MGS Splash screen and the
  screen_splash image-widget wrapper.
- Defer non-splash subsystems (video, detector, actuator links, gameplay,
  console, perf drain) out of APP_Initialize into App_StartServices, called by
  the loader post-reveal. They spawn tasks above the SDMMC/FS priority, so
  starting them during boot starved the card mount (mount 848 → 456 ms).
- Splash-first reveal: dashboard paints behind the splash during the hold
  rather than gating when the panel lights.
- SD: collapsed the mount retry padding into one tight poll (logs true latency)
  and dropped the SDMMC/SYS_FS RTOS task delay 10 → 1 ms (mount 456 → ~380 ms);
  SD is now at its ACMD41 power-up floor.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 12:49:07Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```md
---
name: marvin-canvas-layer-binding
description: marvin UI canvases/screens do NOT own LCDC hardware layers — binding is transient, done at display time.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

In marvin's Legato/GFX_CANVAS UI, canvases and screens do **not** own a hardware layer. MGS-generated code builds every screen into Legato **layer 0** by default; `UiManager` disconnects it from layer 0 after build (`leRemoveRootWidget`). A canvas is bound to a specific hardware layer (BASE / OVR1 / OVR2) via `gfxcSetLayer` **only when it needs to be displayed**, and that binding is transient and reassignable. We avoid leaving screens on layer 0 at init solely because layer 0 is MGS's default build target — not an ownership claim.

**Why:** I have repeatedly mis-reasoned that "nav is on OVR1" or "splash is on OVR2" are fixed assignments that conflict. They are not — two canvases that are never shown at the same time can use the same hardware layer; whoever binds it at display time wins.

**How to apply:** When changing which HW layer a screen displays on, just rebind at display time and don't treat another screen's current layer use as a blocking conflict. Check the display-time sequence (who calls `gfxcSetLayer`/`gfxcShowCanvas` when), not init-time "ownership." Related: [[marvin-journal]].

```

20	#define NAV_W   320u
21	#define NAV_H   800u
22	
23	/* gfxcStartEffectMove delta — slide feel (DEC = ease-out). Tune to taste. */
24	#define NAV_SLIDE_DELTA  6u

26	/* Off-screen-left X for the closed drawer / slide-out target.
27	 *
28	 * A canvas layer can't truly sit off-screen — the window-clip (gfx_canvas.c
29	 * _gfxcCanvasUpdate) emulates a negative X by shifting the source pointer right
30	 * and shrinking the window. But it first aligns X *down* to a multiple of
31	 * CANVAS_WIN_X_ALIGN (`x &= ~0x3` for non-32bpp surfaces), and once |X| reaches
32	 * the surface width the shifted pointer wraps to the next row, flashing the
33	 * panel's left columns through. So the furthest the drawer can validly sit is
34	 * the largest aligned X with |X| < NAV_W. We slide to there; nav_fx_done then
35	 * disables the layer, clearing the residual edge sliver. Derived from NAV_W so
36	 * it tracks the surface width, not a hard-coded pixel count. */
37	#define CANVAS_WIN_X_ALIGN  4u   /* mirrors the clip's `x &= ~0x3` */
38	#define NAV_CLOSED_X        (-(int)((NAV_W - 1u) & ~(CANVAS_WIN_X_ALIGN - 1u)))

41	 * skin's background draw but isn't exposed in MGS, so we set it in code. */
42	#define NAV_CORNER_RADIUS  12u
43	
44	#define FB_NOCACHE   __attribute__((section(".region_nocache"), aligned (32)))
45	
46	static uint16_t FB_NOCACHE s_fb_nav[NAV_W * NAV_H];

48	static bool s_nav_open = false;
49	
50	/* Navigation entries, in panel order. The selected one is the active screen. */
51	#define NAV_COUNT  6u
52	
53	static leButtonWidget *nav_button(unsigned int i)
54	{
55	    switch (i)
56	    {
57	        case 0:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DASHBOARD;
58	        case 1:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_LOGS;
59	        case 2:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_PERFORMANCE;
60	        case 3:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_SYSTEM_INFO;
61	        case 4:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DIAGNOSTICS;
62	        default: return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_SETTINGS;
63	    }
64	}
65	
66	static void nav_close(void);   /* forward decl — nav_on_release may close the drawer */
67	
68	/* Single-active highlight: paint the active entry selected, the rest unselected. */
69	static void nav_highlight(leButtonWidget *active)
70	{
71	    unsigned int i;
72	
73	    for (i = 0u; i < NAV_COUNT; i++)
74	    {
75	        leButtonWidget *b = nav_button(i);
76	        b->fn->setScheme(b, (b == active) ? &SCHEME_NAV_BUTTON_SELECTED
77	                                          : &SCHEME_NAV_BUTTON_UNSELECTED);
78	    }
79	}
80	
81	/* Released-event sink for every nav entry. Switch the highlight; Dashboard means
82	 * "back to the main view" so it also closes the drawer, while the other entries
83	 * just change the selection and stay open. The active screen-switch will hook
84	 * here once the per-screen canvas model lands. */
85	static void nav_on_release(leButtonWidget *btn)
86	{
87	    nav_highlight(btn);
88	
89	    if (btn == Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DASHBOARD)
90	    {
91	        nav_close();
92	    }
93	}
94	
95	static void nav_buttons_init(void)
96	{
97	    unsigned int i;
98	
99	    /* Route every nav-entry release through nav_on_release (runtime-registered
100	     * here — the Navigation screen wires no button events itself) and round the
101	     * corners (not an MGS option). */
102	    for (i = 0u; i < NAV_COUNT; i++)
103	    {
104	        nav_button(i)->fn->setReleasedEventCallback(nav_button(i), nav_on_release);
105	        nav_button(i)->fn->setCornerRadius(nav_button(i), NAV_CORNER_RADIUS);
106	        ButtonAA_Enable(nav_button(i));
107	    }
108	
109	    /* Dashboard is the active entry at startup — set the highlight only (calling
110	     * the release sink here would close the not-yet-open drawer). */
111	    nav_highlight(Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DASHBOARD);
112	}
113	
114	/* Animate the drawer to target_x from wherever it currently sits. Cancel any
115	 * in-flight slide first: gfxcStartEffectMove is a no-op while a move is running
116	 * (it only starts from status IDLE), so without the stop a mid-slide reversal
117	 * would be silently dropped — the original move would run to completion and fire
118	 * nav_fx_done with a now-stale s_nav_open, hiding the drawer and wedging the
119	 * toggle. Reading the live position makes the reversal retarget smoothly. */
120	static void nav_slide_to(int target_x)
121	{
122	    int x, y;
123	
124	    gfxcStopEffect(NAV_CANVAS, GFXC_FX_MOVE);
125	    gfxcGetWindowPosition(NAV_CANVAS, &x, &y);
126	    gfxcStartEffectMove(NAV_CANVAS, GFXC_FX_MOVE_DEC, x, 0, target_x, 0, NAV_SLIDE_DELTA);
127	}
128	
129	static void nav_open(void)
130	{
131	    /* Force a full repaint of the panel into the canvas before revealing it — the
132	     * paint queued at startup (parked off-screen) doesn't fully land in the
133	     * buffer, so without this the drawer slides in partially drawn until touch
134	     * damage fills it in. The repaint lands over the next frames as it slides.
135	     * Show first so the move is visible (the FX engine enables the layer from
136	     * canvas.active). */
137	    Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->invalidate(Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION);
138	    gfxcShowCanvas(NAV_CANVAS);
139	    nav_slide_to(0);
140	    s_nav_open = true;
141	}
142	
143	static void nav_close(void)
144	{
145	    /* Slide out to NAV_CLOSED_X (off-screen), then nav_fx_done disables the
146	     * layer. NAV_CLOSED_X avoids the -NAV_W window-clip row-wrap (see its
147	     * definition); the layer update busy-waits for the vsync latch, so the final
148	     * frame is displayed before the hide lands — keeping it in-bounds makes that
149	     * frame a harmless edge sliver instead of the panel's left columns. */
150	    nav_slide_to(NAV_CLOSED_X);
151	    s_nav_open = false;
152	}
153	
154	/* Move-effect completion callback. At the off-screen end of a close slide the
155	 * window clip leaves a degenerate sliver of the drawer composited at screen
156	 * left; disabling OVR1 outright once the slide finishes removes it cleanly. Only
157	 * acts on a completed close — an open leaves the layer shown, and a re-open
158	 * mid-close restarts the move (so this won't fire for the abandoned close). */
159	static void nav_fx_done(unsigned int canvasID, GFXC_FX_TYPE effect,
160	                        GFXC_FX_STATUS status, void *parm)
161	{
162	    (void)canvasID;
163	    (void)parm;
164	
165	    if (effect == GFXC_FX_MOVE && status == GFXC_FX_DONE && !s_nav_open)
166	    {
167	        gfxcHideCanvas(NAV_CANVAS);
168	        gfxcCanvasUpdate(NAV_CANVAS);
169	    }
170	}
171	
172	void Nav_InitSurface(void)
173	{
174	    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(NAV_CANVAS, NAV_W, NAV_H, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, s_fb_nav);
175	}
176	
177	/* Navigation screen composition root (declared in le_gen_screen_Navigation.h),
178	 * raised by screenShow_Navigation. The MGS screen authors its content on canvas
179	 * 0; move that root so it renders into NAV_CANVAS instead (the dashboard keeps
180	 * canvas 0), then bind NAV_CANVAS to the OVR1 hardware layer. Keep the panel
181	 * visible+enabled so Legato renders it into the canvas continuously, and start
182	 * closed (parked off-screen + hidden); the touch pick rect follows the canvas
183	 * window position (LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE), so a closed (off-screen) nav can't
184	 * intercept dashboard touches. The off-screen X also seeds the slide-in. */
185	void Navigation_OnShow(void)
186	{
187	    leWidget *root = screenGetRoot_Navigation(0);
188	    leRemoveRootWidget(root, 0);
189	    leAddRootWidget(root, NAV_CANVAS);
190	
191	    Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->setEnabled(Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION, LE_TRUE);
192	    Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->setVisible(Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION, LE_TRUE);
193	
194	    gfxcSetWindowSize(NAV_CANVAS, NAV_W, NAV_H);
195	    gfxcSetWindowPosition(NAV_CANVAS, NAV_CLOSED_X, 0);
196	    gfxcSetLayer(NAV_CANVAS, HW_OVR1);
197	    gfxcSetEffectsCallback(NAV_CANVAS, nav_fx_done, NULL);
198	    gfxcCanvasUpdate(NAV_CANVAS);
199	
200	    nav_buttons_init();
201	}
202	
203	/* Hamburger on the Dashboard screen (BASE) toggles the nav drawer. */
204	void event_Dashboard_BUTTON_SYSYEM_NAVIGATION_OnPressed(leButtonWidget* btn)
205	{
206	    (void)btn;
207	    if (s_nav_open) { nav_close(); } else { nav_open(); }
208	}

Good catch, and you're right — the fill is pure waste on the happy path. Let me answer the timing question and then make the change.

**The prefill cost:** it's `1280×800 = 1.024M` 32-bit writes to **nocache** DRAM, one at a time, pre-scheduler. Nocache writes don't get write-combining/cache benefit, so this is meaningfully slower per-write than normal memory — roughly low-tens of ms, and it's blocking boot before the scheduler even starts. But the exact number doesn't matter because, as you say, **on the happy path the loader's SD read overwrites the entire buffer before the backlight comes on** — so the fill is needed *only* when the read fails. Moving it to the failure branch eliminates it from every successful boot.

Let me make that change.

Now, your broader questions:

**Other big hits in `UiManager_Initialize` (all pre-scheduler, so all on the path *before* the splash can appear):**
- `screenInit_Dashboard()` — builds the **200+ widget** dashboard tree. This is the main remaining cost: each widget is a `_New` + setters + `addChild`. Construction only (no paint), normal memory, so likely single-digit to low-tens of ms — smaller than the prefill we just removed, but it *is* on the pre-splash critical path.
- `screenInit_Navigation()` — same shape, ~dozens of widgets, smaller.
- `initializeStrings()` — string-table setup, modest.
- Everything else (`gfxcSetPixelBuffer`, `Nav_InitSurface`, `GFX_CANVAS_Task`, the `screenShow_*`/`leRemoveRootWidget` calls) is config/cheap.

**Could the dashboard build move after the loader starts, like the fill?** Plausibly now — and it's more interesting than before. The splash is no longer a Legato screen, and the dashboard/nav roots are detached until `AttachMainScreens`, so during the splash phase **LEGATO_Tasks has zero attached roots → it renders nothing**. That means building the dashboard tree post-scheduler wouldn't race the render task the way the journal got burned by in bring-up #5. So `screenInit_Dashboard/Navigation` *could* move into the loader (after the splash is lit, before `AttachMainScreens`), shaving their construction time off the pre-splash path.

But I'd **measure before doing it**: it reverses the journal's "build everything pre-scheduler" decision, and the payoff is only worth it if construction is genuinely large. Relative to the ~380 ms mount + ~446 ms read that dominate boot, a few ms of widget construction may not be worth the risk.

**Other `*_Initialize` routines:** `APP_Initialize` is now lean — `log_init`, `PerfLog_Initialize` (queue alloc), `Storage/Results/Catalog_Initialize` (state only), `Loader_Start` (task create). All cheap. The heavy subsystems (video, detector, etc.) already moved to `App_StartServices` post-reveal. So `UiManager_Initialize` really is the bulk of pre-scheduler time.

## Findings: Marvin UI Layer Architecture & Detachment Analysis

Based on systematic exploration of the Marvin firmware UI layer, here are the answers to your five specific questions:

---

### 1. **Dashboard Interactivity & Event Callbacks**

**Dashboard widgets with event callbacks:**
- `Dashboard_BUTTON_SYSYEM_NAVIGATION` (hamburger): line 301 of `le_gen_screen_Dashboard.c` has `setPressedEventCallback(Dashboard_BUTTON_SYSYEM_NAVIGATION, event_Dashboard_BUTTON_SYSYEM_NAVIGATION_OnPressed)`
- `Dashboard_BUTTON_GUITAR_STRUM_UP`: line 1124-1125 has both `setPressedEventCallback` and `setReleasedEventCallback`
- `Dashboard_BUTTON_GUITAR_STRUM_DOWN`: line 1160-1161 has both callbacks

**Repaint mechanism:** When a button is pressed, `setPressed()` in `/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/button/legato_widget_button.c` line 191 executes:
1. Calls the `pressedEvent` callback (line 203-205)
2. Marks the widget dirty if the pressed/released images differ or if there's a pressed offset (lines 232-249)
3. Calls `_this->fn->invalidate(_this)` at line 253, which **queues damage to the renderer's damage rect array**

**Legato attachment requirement:** YES, the screen's root **must remain attached** to the layer (canvas) for damage tracking to work. The `invalidate()` call queues damage into `leRendererState.currentRenderLayer->currentDamageRects` (line 481 of `legato_renderer.c`). If the root is detached via `leRemoveRootWidget()` (which removes it as a child of `layer->root`), it is no longer in the widget tree that the renderer traverses during damage computation, so invalidations will be silently ignored or operate on a dangling tree.

---

### 2. **Nav Drawer Re-rendering**

**Nav re-render triggers:**
- `nav_open()` line 137: calls `Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->invalidate()` to force full repaint before showing
- `nav_close()` line 150: calls `nav_slide_to(NAV_CLOSED_X)` which uses canvas effects; no widget-tree damage
- `nav_highlight()` line 69: calls `b->fn->setScheme()` on each button; setScheme internally marks the button dirty (calls `invalidate`)
- Slide animation: via `gfxcStartEffectMove()` (canvas-level, not Legato widget damage)

**Navigation_OnShow (lines 185-201 of `screen_nav.c`):**
1. Removes nav root from canvas 0 (line 188)
2. Re-adds it to NAV_CANVAS (canvas 1) via `leAddRootWidget()` at line 189
3. Sets nav panel enabled/visible at lines 191-192
4. Configures canvas window position (off-screen at NAV_CLOSED_X) and layer binding at lines 195-198
5. Calls `nav_buttons_init()` which registers runtime event callbacks (lines 104, 106)

**Root attachment:** The nav root is **continuously attached to NAV_CANVAS** while the drawer exists. It is detached only if explicitly removed. The slide animation works at the **canvas window level** (gfxcStartEffectMove clips the canvas window position) independent of Legato's widget tree attachment; however, widget damage (from `nav_highlight` via `setScheme`) still requires the root to be attached to propagate `invalidate()` calls into the renderer's damage system.

---

### 3. **Live Telemetry Updates**

**Current state:** No runtime text updates found wired into dashboard widgets. Search for `setText`/`setString` calls targeting `Dashboard_*` widgets outside generated files yields **no results**. All label text (CPU, MEMORY, TEMP, UPTIME, LATENCY, SCORE, ACCURACY, COMBO, HIT, MISS, voltage "12.4V", etc.) in `le_gen_screen_Dashboard.c` are authored statically at generation time (e.g., line 426: `Dashboard_label_START->fn->setString(Dashboard_label_START, (leString*)&string_figmaStr_START)`).

**Telemetry wiring:** No application-side update loop discovered binding live telemetry to dashboard labels. If telemetry updates were to be added, they would call `setString()` on the label widget, which internally triggers `invalidate()` via string callbacks (lines 277-281 of `legato_widget_button.c` show the pattern; labels follow the same model).

---

### 4. **Steady-State Render Cost (Attached, No Damage)**

**Damage early-out:** In `legato_renderer.c` line 487-491, the `preLayer()` function checks if the scratch damage rect list is empty after merging prev + current damage:

```c
if(_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList.size == 0)
{
    _rendererState.frameState = LE_FRAME_POSTLAYER;
    return;
}
```

**Cost when attached with no damage:** **Minimal, nearly free.** If no widgets have been invalidated:
- `leUpdate()` (line 376 of `legato_state.c`) calls `leEvent_ProcessEvents()` (line 385), then `updateWidgets()` (line 438), then `leRenderer_Paint()` (line 440)
- `leRenderer_Paint()` advances through frame states; at `PRELAYER` (line 303 of `legato_renderer.c`), `preLayer()` runs, the damage list is empty, and it early-returns to `POSTLAYER` without drawing anything
- This is a **O(1) skip** per layer per frame

**Cost when detached:** The root is simply not in the widget tree; no traversal, no damage accumulation. However, re-attaching requires a full paint (line 126 of `ui_manager.c`: `dash->fn->invalidate(dash)` after `leAddRootWidget`).

---

### 5. **Concurrency: leAddRootWidget / leRemoveRootWidget Safety**

**Root-list mutation & locking:** 

In `legato_state.c` lines 755-790, `leAddRootWidget()` and `leRemoveRootWidget()` mutate `_state.layerList` by calling `leList_Get()` (line 763, 780) and then `LE_OCALL(layer->root, addChild/removeChild, wgt)` (lines 767, 782). 

**No locking found:** Inspection of `legato_list.c` (the underlying list implementation) and `legato_state.c` reveals **no mutex, semaphore, critical section, or atomic operations**. The code is not RTOS-aware:
- No `portENTER_CRITICAL()` / `portEXIT_CRITICAL()` (FreeRTOS guards)
- No `xSemaphoreTake()` / `xSemaphoreGive()`
- No volatile or atomic qualifiers on shared state

**Race condition exists:** If `leAddRootWidget()` / `leRemoveRootWidget()` is called while `leUpdate()` → `leRenderer_Paint()` traverses the `layerList` (lines 390-417 of `legato_state.c` iterate over `state->layerList.size`), a concurrent modification would corrupt the list or skip layers. The current architecture assumes **single-threaded Legato operation** or that the caller (ui_manager.c, screen_nav.c) serializes add/remove calls with render task scheduling.

**Evidence of single-threaded design:** In `ui_manager.c` lines 106-113, `leRemoveRootWidget()` is called **before the scheduler starts** (pre-scheduler in `UiManager_Initialize`), avoiding any concurrency. Re-attachment in `UiManager_AttachMainScreens()` is called by the loader task, which must be externally synchronized with the render task (no in-code protection observed).

---

### Summary

- **Dashboard buttons emit damage via invalidate()** → requires root attached for damage to be queued and rendered
- **Nav drawer slide is canvas-level** (independent of widget attachment), but nav-menu selection (setScheme → invalidate) **requires root attached**
- **No live telemetry wiring** currently; if added, would follow setString → invalidate pattern
- **No damage = no render work** (early-out in preLayer at ~487 lines of legato_renderer.c); steady-state cost is negligible
- **No thread-safety** on root-list mutations; single-threaded operation or external serialization required

13	/* A canvas is a RAM surface Legato renders into; each screen has its own
14	 * (the CANVAS_* ids below — gfxcSetPixelBuffer assigns each one's buffer).
15	 * A hardware layer is what the LCDC scans out. These are independent: at
16	 * runtime we bind a canvas onto whatever hardware layer suits its current need
17	 * with gfxcSetLayer(canvasId, hwLayer), so a canvas id is unrelated to a hw
18	 * layer index. Screens are persistent (built once, never torn down), so a canvas
19	 * keeps its last-painted pixels; switching screens just re-binds canvases to
20	 * hardware layers.
21	 *
22	 *   canvas          shown on hw layer        color mode
23	 *   CANVAS_DASH      BASE                     RGB565
24	 *   CANVAS_NAV       OVR1                     RGB565   (ui/nav, shown on demand)
25	 *   CANVAS_SPLASH    OVR1                     RGBA8888 (boot only)
26	 *
27	 * The splash and the nav both use OVR1, but never at the same time: the splash
28	 * shows on it during boot, then is hidden at reveal, and the nav shows on it only
29	 * afterward (when opened). The splash covers the dashboard (on BASE) while it
30	 * paints underneath. OVR2 (topmost) is left free for an overlay drawn over the
31	 * splash — e.g. a boot loading bar. */
32	#define CANVAS_DASH    0u
33	#define CANVAS_NAV     1u
34	#define CANVAS_SPLASH  2u
35	
36	/* LCDC hardware-layer indices (drvLayer/layerOrder): BASE 0, HEO 1, OVR1 2,
37	 * OVR2 3. HEO is the live camera (off-limits). */
38	#define HW_BASE   0u
39	#define HW_OVR1   2u   /* splash (boot) + nav (ui/nav) — never shown together */
40	#define HW_OVR2   3u   /* reserved (topmost): overlay over the splash, e.g. a loading bar */
41	
42	#define BASE_W   1280u
43	#define BASE_H    800u
44	
45	/* Splash fallback fill: opaque black. The splash canvas is RGBA_8888, which packs
46	 * 0xRRGGBBAA, so a little-endian pixel word of 0x000000FF is R=G=B=0, A=0xFF. */
47	#define SPLASH_FILL   0x000000FFu
48	
49	#define FB_NOCACHE   __attribute__((section(".region_nocache"), aligned (32)))
50	
51	/* Per-screen surfaces, non-cached so the 2D engine and LCDC DMA read CPU-
52	 * rendered pixels coherently (matches FB_CACHE_NC). The dashboard is RGB565
53	 * (steady-state UI needs no more); the splash is 32bpp so the photo keeps full
54	 * color depth. The splash buffer is also the natural decode scratch for the
55	 * (future) album-art pre-load, once the splash leaves the screen. */
56	static uint16_t FB_NOCACHE s_fb_base[BASE_W * BASE_H];
57	static uint32_t FB_NOCACHE s_fb_splash[BASE_W * BASE_H];
58	
59	void UiManager_Initialize(void)
60	{
61	    /* Assign the per-screen canvas surfaces before the canvas runs. The nav owns
62	     * its own (canvas 1, via Nav_InitSurface). */
63	    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(CANVAS_DASH,   BASE_W, BASE_H, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565,   s_fb_base);
64	    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(CANVAS_SPLASH, BASE_W, BASE_H, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888, s_fb_splash);
65	    Nav_InitSurface();
66	
67	    /* Drive the canvas state machine to RUNNING now, before the scheduler, so a
68	     * blit into a canvas is not dropped by the RUNNING gate in GFXC_BlitBuffer. */
69	    GFX_CANVAS_Task();
70	
71	    leSetStringTable(&stringTable);
72	    initializeStrings();
73	
74	    /* Splash: a raw full-screen RGBA8888 bitmap, NOT a Legato-rendered screen. The
75	     * loader reads splash.raw off the SD straight into this canvas's buffer
76	     * (s_fb_splash), which the splash layer scans out directly — no widget, no
77	     * render, no blit. The MGS Splash screen is unused. No pre-fill here: on the
78	     * happy path the loader's read overwrites the whole buffer before the backlight
79	     * comes on, so filling it would be ~1M wasted nocache writes; the loader fills
80	     * the fallback colour (UiManager_FillSplash) only if the read fails. The layer
81	     * bind/show happens below, after the dashboard + nav are built. */
82	
83	    /* Build + host the dashboard + nav now, pre-scheduler (no render-task
84	     * concurrency); they're persistent, built once. Dashboard keeps its authored
85	     * canvas 0 (RGB565, bound to BASE); Navigation_OnShow re-hosts the nav onto
86	     * canvas 1 and binds it to OVR1. They paint behind the splash. */
87	    screenInit_Dashboard();
88	    screenShow_Dashboard();    /* Dashboard_OnShow binds canvas 0 to BASE */
89	    screenInit_Navigation();
90	    screenShow_Navigation();   /* Navigation_OnShow binds nav → OVR1 */
91	
92	    /* Show the splash on OVR1 — done AFTER Navigation_OnShow so the splash's bind
93	     * is the one OVR1 ends up holding at boot (the splash and nav share OVR1 but
94	     * are never shown together; the nav reclaims it when first opened, post-reveal).
95	     * OVR2 stays free for an overlay over the splash (e.g. a loading bar). OVR1's
96	     * color mode must be poked to 32bpp: the GFX-XLCDC driver never writes RGBMODE
97	     * (it assumes the RGB565 project format), so OVR1 would read the 32bpp splash as
98	     * RGB565 → garbled. RevealDashboard pokes it back to RGB565 for the nav. */
99	    gfxcSetWindowPosition(CANVAS_SPLASH, 0, 0);
100	    gfxcSetWindowSize(CANVAS_SPLASH, BASE_W, BASE_H);
101	    gfxcSetLayer(CANVAS_SPLASH, HW_OVR1);
102	    gfxcShowCanvas(CANVAS_SPLASH);
103	    gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_SPLASH);
104	    XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888, true);
105	
106	    /* Detach the dashboard and nav roots so that when the scheduler starts the
107	     * render task paints only what's needed — the panel comes up as fast as the
108	     * SD read allows, not gated behind the 200+ widget dashboard. Both trees are
109	     * fully built and their canvases bound; the loader re-attaches them with
110	     * UiManager_AttachMainScreens once the splash is lit, so they paint behind it.
111	     * Detaching here is pre-scheduler, so there's no race with the render task. */
112	    leRemoveRootWidget(screenGetRoot_Dashboard(0),  CANVAS_DASH);
113	    leRemoveRootWidget(screenGetRoot_Navigation(0), CANVAS_NAV);
114	}
115	
116	/* Bring the dashboard + nav into the render path, behind the splash. Called by
117	 * the loader after the splash is painted and the backlight is on: the heavy
118	 * dashboard paint then happens while the splash is held, off the
119	 * splash-to-screen critical path. invalidate() forces a full first paint (the
120	 * trees were detached before the scheduler, so they've never been drawn). The
121	 * add-root mirrors UiManager_RevealDashboard's post-scheduler remove-root. */
122	void UiManager_AttachMainScreens(void)
123	{
124	    leWidget *dash = screenGetRoot_Dashboard(0);
125	    leAddRootWidget(dash, CANVAS_DASH);
126	    dash->fn->invalidate(dash);
127	
128	    leWidget *nav = screenGetRoot_Navigation(0);
129	    leAddRootWidget(nav, CANVAS_NAV);
130	    nav->fn->invalidate(nav);
131	}
132	
133	/* The splash canvas's pixel buffer (OVR2 scanout). The loader reads splash.raw
134	 * straight into this — it's RGBA8888 in the layer's native byte order, so the
135	 * read IS the load; no decode or blit. *bytes (if non-NULL) = its size. */
136	void *UiManager_SplashFramebuffer(uint32_t *bytes)
137	{
138	    if (bytes != NULL) { *bytes = (uint32_t)sizeof(s_fb_splash); }
139	    return s_fb_splash;
140	}
141	
142	/* Fill the splash buffer with the fallback colour (opaque black). The loader
143	 * calls this only when the SD splash read fails — the happy-path read overwrites
144	 * the whole buffer, so there's no point pre-filling it at init. */
145	void UiManager_FillSplash(void)
146	{
147	    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < (BASE_W * BASE_H); i++) { s_fb_splash[i] = SPLASH_FILL; }
148	}
149	
150	/* Re-latch the splash canvas after the loader writes new pixels into it, so the
151	 * splash layer scans the updated buffer. */
152	void UiManager_CommitSplash(void)
153	{
154	    gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_SPLASH);
155	}
156	
157	/* Reveal the (already painted, behind-the-splash) dashboard by dropping the
158	 * splash overlay. The dashboard canvas is already bound to BASE and full; hiding
159	 * the splash's OVR1 uncovers it instantly. Called by the loader once the dashboard
160	 * is painted. The splash has no Legato root (it's a raw framebuffer), so there's
161	 * nothing in the input pick path to detach — just hide the canvas. */
162	void UiManager_RevealDashboard(void)
163	{
164	    gfxcHideCanvas(CANVAS_SPLASH);
165	    gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_SPLASH);
166	
167	    /* Restore OVR1 to RGB565. The splash poked it to 32bpp, but the nav drawer
168	     * (the other OVR1 user, shown only after this) is RGB565 and the XLCDC driver
169	     * won't rewrite the layer mode on its own. */
170	    XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, true);
171	}
172	
173	/* Turn on the LCD backlight. The backlight is a plain GPIO enable
174	 * (AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN / PC18), NOT the LCDC PWM that XLCDC_EnableBacklight()
175	 * drives — that PWM output isn't wired to this board's backlight, so enabling it
176	 * does nothing visible. Drive the enable pin directly instead. The pin starts
177	 * low at boot (MCC PIO config), so the panel stays dark until the loader calls
178	 * this once the splash is painted — no pre-splash frame. Active-high assumed
179	 * (the _Set name == enable); flip to _Clear if the board is active-low. */
180	void UiManager_EnableBacklight(void)
181	{
182	    AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN_Set();
183	}
184	
185	/* Dashboard screen composition root (declared in le_gen_screen_Dashboard.h).
186	 * Binds the dashboard canvas to the BASE hardware layer. The nav drawer is its own screen
187	 * (Navigation), hosted by ui/nav from its own OnShow hook. */
188	void Dashboard_OnShow(void)
189	{
190	    gfxcSetWindowPosition(CANVAS_DASH, 0, 0);
191	    gfxcSetWindowSize(CANVAS_DASH, BASE_W, BASE_H);
192	    gfxcSetLayer(CANVAS_DASH, HW_BASE);
193	    gfxcShowCanvas(CANVAS_DASH);
194	    gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_DASH);
195	}

9	#include "gfx/legato/legato.h"
10	#include "gfx/legato/generated/le_gen_scheme.h"
11	#include "gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Dashboard.h"   /* hamburger event decl */
12	#include "gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Navigation.h"  /* nav widgets + OnShow */
13	
14	/* The nav drawer is authored as its own MGS Screen (Navigation) and rendered
15	 * into its own canvas (NAV_CANVAS), which we bind to the OVR1 hardware layer.
16	 * (Canvas ids and hardware-layer indices are independent — see ui_manager.c.) */
17	#define NAV_CANVAS   1u   /* canvas the drawer renders into */
18	#define HW_OVR1      2u   /* OVR1 hardware-layer index (drvLayer/layerOrder) */
19	
20	#define NAV_W   320u
21	#define NAV_H   800u
22	
23	/* gfxcStartEffectMove delta — slide feel (DEC = ease-out). Tune to taste. */
24	#define NAV_SLIDE_DELTA  6u
25	
26	/* Off-screen-left X for the closed drawer / slide-out target.
27	 *
28	 * A canvas layer can't truly sit off-screen — the window-clip (gfx_canvas.c
29	 * _gfxcCanvasUpdate) emulates a negative X by shifting the source pointer right
30	 * and shrinking the window. But it first aligns X *down* to a multiple of
31	 * CANVAS_WIN_X_ALIGN (`x &= ~0x3` for non-32bpp surfaces), and once |X| reaches
32	 * the surface width the shifted pointer wraps to the next row, flashing the
33	 * panel's left columns through. So the furthest the drawer can validly sit is
34	 * the largest aligned X with |X| < NAV_W. We slide to there; nav_fx_done then
35	 * disables the layer, clearing the residual edge sliver. Derived from NAV_W so
36	 * it tracks the surface width, not a hard-coded pixel count. */
37	#define CANVAS_WIN_X_ALIGN  4u   /* mirrors the clip's `x &= ~0x3` */
38	#define NAV_CLOSED_X        (-(int)((NAV_W - 1u) & ~(CANVAS_WIN_X_ALIGN - 1u)))
39	
40	/* Rounded button corners. The widget cornerRadius is honored by the classic
41	 * skin's background draw but isn't exposed in MGS, so we set it in code. */
42	#define NAV_CORNER_RADIUS  12u
43	
44	#define FB_NOCACHE   __attribute__((section(".region_nocache"), aligned (32)))
45	
46	static uint16_t FB_NOCACHE s_fb_nav[NAV_W * NAV_H];
47	
48	static bool s_nav_open = false;
49	
50	/* Navigation entries, in panel order. The selected one is the active screen. */
51	#define NAV_COUNT  6u
52	
53	static leButtonWidget *nav_button(unsigned int i)
54	{
55	    switch (i)
56	    {
57	        case 0:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DASHBOARD;
58	        case 1:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_LOGS;
59	        case 2:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_PERFORMANCE;
60	        case 3:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_SYSTEM_INFO;
61	        case 4:  return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DIAGNOSTICS;
62	        default: return Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_SETTINGS;
63	    }
64	}
65	
66	static void nav_close(void);   /* forward decl — nav_on_release may close the drawer */
67	
68	/* Single-active highlight: paint the active entry selected, the rest unselected. */
69	static void nav_highlight(leButtonWidget *active)
70	{
71	    unsigned int i;
72	
73	    for (i = 0u; i < NAV_COUNT; i++)
74	    {
75	        leButtonWidget *b = nav_button(i);
76	        b->fn->setScheme(b, (b == active) ? &SCHEME_NAV_BUTTON_SELECTED
77	                                          : &SCHEME_NAV_BUTTON_UNSELECTED);
78	    }
79	}
80	
81	/* Released-event sink for every nav entry. Switch the highlight; Dashboard means
82	 * "back to the main view" so it also closes the drawer, while the other entries
83	 * just change the selection and stay open. The active screen-switch will hook
84	 * here once the per-screen canvas model lands. */
85	static void nav_on_release(leButtonWidget *btn)
86	{
87	    nav_highlight(btn);
88	
89	    if (btn == Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DASHBOARD)
90	    {
91	        nav_close();
92	    }
93	}
94	
95	static void nav_buttons_init(void)
96	{
97	    unsigned int i;
98	
99	    /* Route every nav-entry release through nav_on_release (runtime-registered
100	     * here — the Navigation screen wires no button events itself) and round the
101	     * corners (not an MGS option). */
102	    for (i = 0u; i < NAV_COUNT; i++)
103	    {
104	        nav_button(i)->fn->setReleasedEventCallback(nav_button(i), nav_on_release);
105	        nav_button(i)->fn->setCornerRadius(nav_button(i), NAV_CORNER_RADIUS);
106	        ButtonAA_Enable(nav_button(i));
107	    }
108	
109	    /* Dashboard is the active entry at startup — set the highlight only (calling
110	     * the release sink here would close the not-yet-open drawer). */
111	    nav_highlight(Navigation_BUTTON_NAV_DASHBOARD);
112	}
113	
114	/* Animate the drawer to target_x from wherever it currently sits. Cancel any
115	 * in-flight slide first: gfxcStartEffectMove is a no-op while a move is running
116	 * (it only starts from status IDLE), so without the stop a mid-slide reversal
117	 * would be silently dropped — the original move would run to completion and fire
118	 * nav_fx_done with a now-stale s_nav_open, hiding the drawer and wedging the
119	 * toggle. Reading the live position makes the reversal retarget smoothly. */
120	static void nav_slide_to(int target_x)
121	{
122	    int x, y;
123	
124	    gfxcStopEffect(NAV_CANVAS, GFXC_FX_MOVE);
125	    gfxcGetWindowPosition(NAV_CANVAS, &x, &y);
126	    gfxcStartEffectMove(NAV_CANVAS, GFXC_FX_MOVE_DEC, x, 0, target_x, 0, NAV_SLIDE_DELTA);
127	}
128	
129	static void nav_open(void)
130	{
131	    /* Force a full repaint of the panel into the canvas before revealing it — the
132	     * paint queued at startup (parked off-screen) doesn't fully land in the
133	     * buffer, so without this the drawer slides in partially drawn until touch
134	     * damage fills it in. The repaint lands over the next frames as it slides.
135	     * Show first so the move is visible (the FX engine enables the layer from
136	     * canvas.active). */
137	    Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->invalidate(Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION);
138	    gfxcShowCanvas(NAV_CANVAS);
139	    nav_slide_to(0);
140	    s_nav_open = true;
141	}
142	
143	static void nav_close(void)
144	{
145	    /* Slide out to NAV_CLOSED_X (off-screen), then nav_fx_done disables the
146	     * layer. NAV_CLOSED_X avoids the -NAV_W window-clip row-wrap (see its
147	     * definition); the layer update busy-waits for the vsync latch, so the final
148	     * frame is displayed before the hide lands — keeping it in-bounds makes that
149	     * frame a harmless edge sliver instead of the panel's left columns. */
150	    nav_slide_to(NAV_CLOSED_X);
151	    s_nav_open = false;
152	}
153	
154	/* Move-effect completion callback. At the off-screen end of a close slide the
155	 * window clip leaves a degenerate sliver of the drawer composited at screen
156	 * left; disabling OVR1 outright once the slide finishes removes it cleanly. Only
157	 * acts on a completed close — an open leaves the layer shown, and a re-open
158	 * mid-close restarts the move (so this won't fire for the abandoned close). */
159	static void nav_fx_done(unsigned int canvasID, GFXC_FX_TYPE effect,
160	                        GFXC_FX_STATUS status, void *parm)
161	{
162	    (void)canvasID;
163	    (void)parm;
164	
165	    if (effect == GFXC_FX_MOVE && status == GFXC_FX_DONE && !s_nav_open)
166	    {
167	        gfxcHideCanvas(NAV_CANVAS);
168	        gfxcCanvasUpdate(NAV_CANVAS);
169	    }
170	}
171	
172	void Nav_InitSurface(void)
173	{
174	    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(NAV_CANVAS, NAV_W, NAV_H, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, s_fb_nav);
175	}
176	
177	/* Navigation screen composition root (declared in le_gen_screen_Navigation.h),
178	 * raised by screenShow_Navigation. The MGS screen authors its content on canvas
179	 * 0; move that root so it renders into NAV_CANVAS instead (the dashboard keeps
180	 * canvas 0), then bind NAV_CANVAS to the OVR1 hardware layer. Keep the panel
181	 * visible+enabled so Legato renders it into the canvas continuously, and start
182	 * closed (parked off-screen + hidden); the touch pick rect follows the canvas
183	 * window position (LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE), so a closed (off-screen) nav can't
184	 * intercept dashboard touches. The off-screen X also seeds the slide-in. */
185	void Navigation_OnShow(void)
186	{
187	    leWidget *root = screenGetRoot_Navigation(0);
188	    leRemoveRootWidget(root, 0);
189	    leAddRootWidget(root, NAV_CANVAS);
190	
191	    Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->setEnabled(Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION, LE_TRUE);
192	    Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->setVisible(Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION, LE_TRUE);
193	
194	    gfxcSetWindowSize(NAV_CANVAS, NAV_W, NAV_H);
195	    gfxcSetWindowPosition(NAV_CANVAS, NAV_CLOSED_X, 0);
196	    gfxcSetLayer(NAV_CANVAS, HW_OVR1);
197	    gfxcSetEffectsCallback(NAV_CANVAS, nav_fx_done, NULL);
198	    gfxcCanvasUpdate(NAV_CANVAS);
199	
200	    nav_buttons_init();
201	}
202	
203	/* Hamburger on the Dashboard screen (BASE) toggles the nav drawer. */
204	void event_Dashboard_BUTTON_SYSYEM_NAVIGATION_OnPressed(leButtonWidget* btn)
205	{
206	    (void)btn;
207	    if (s_nav_open) { nav_close(); } else { nav_open(); }
208	}

755	leResult leAddRootWidget(leWidget* wgt,

376	leResult leUpdate(uint32_t dt)

382	    leLayerState* layerState;
383	#endif
384	
385	    leEvent_ProcessEvents();
386	
387	#if LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE == 1
388	    state = leGetState();
389	
390	    for(itr = 0; itr < state->layerList.size; ++itr)
391	    {
392	        layerRect.layer.id = itr;
393	        layerRect.x = 0;
394	        layerRect.y = 0;
395	        layerRect.width = 0;
396	        layerRect.height = 0;
397	
398	        leRenderer_DisplayInterface()->ioctl(GFX_IOCTL_GET_LAYER_RECT, &layerRect);
399	        layerState = (leLayerState*)leList_Get(&state->layerList, itr);
400	
401	        layerState->driverPosition.x = layerRect.x;
402	        layerState->driverPosition.y = layerRect.y;
403	
404	        layerState->root.fn->setPosition(&layerState->root,
405	                                         0,
406	                                         0);
407	
408	#if LE_RENDER_ORIENTATION == 90 || LE_RENDER_ORIENTATION == 270
409	        layerState->root.fn->setSize(&layerState->root,
410	                                     layerRect.height,
411	                                     layerRect.width);
412	#else
413	        layerState->root.fn->setSize(&layerState->root,
414	                                     layerRect.width,
415	                                     layerRect.height);
416	#endif
417	    }
418	#endif
419	
420	#if LE_STREAMING_ENABLED == 1
421	    // there is an active stream in progress, service that to completion
422	    // before painting anything else
423	    if(_state.activeStream != NULL)
424	    {
425	        if(_state.activeStream->isDone(_state.activeStream) == LE_TRUE)
426	        {
427	            _state.activeStream = NULL;
428	        }
429	        else
430	        {
431	            _state.activeStream->exec(_state.activeStream);
432	
433	            return LE_SUCCESS;
434	        }
435	    }
436	#endif
437	
438	    updateWidgets(dt);
439	
440	    leRenderer_Paint();
441	
442	    return LE_SUCCESS;
443	}

165	                            const gfxRect* rectSrc,
166	                            const gfxPixelBuffer* dest,
167	                            const gfxRect* rectDest)
168	{
169	    void* srcPtr;
170	    void* destPtr;
171	    uint32_t row, rowSize;
172	    unsigned int width, height;
173	    gfxResult res = GFX_FAILURE;
174	
175	#if (CONFIG_CANVAS_GPU_BLIT_ENABLE == true)
176	    res = gfxcGPU->blitBuffer(source,
177	                              rectSrc,
178	                              dest,
179	                              rectDest);
180	#endif
181	
182	    if (res != GFX_SUCCESS)
183	    {
184	        width = (rectSrc->width < rectDest->width) ?
185	                    rectSrc->width : rectDest->width;
186	        height = (rectSrc->height < rectDest->height) ?
187	                    rectSrc->height : rectDest->height;
188	        rowSize = width * gfxColorInfoTable[dest->mode].size;
189	
190	        for(row = 0; row < height; row++)
191	        {
192	            srcPtr = gfxPixelBufferOffsetGet(source, rectSrc->x, rectSrc->y + row);
193	            destPtr = gfxPixelBufferOffsetGet(dest, rectDest->x, rectDest->y + row);
194	
195	            memcpy(destPtr, srcPtr, rowSize);
196	        }
197	    }
198	
199	    return GFX_SUCCESS;
200	}

31	int32_t leList_Create(leList* l)
32	{
33	    if(l == NULL)
34	        return -1;
35	
36	    l->head = NULL;
37	    l->tail = NULL;
38	
39	    l->size = 0;
40	
41	    return 0;
42	}
43	
44	int32_t leList_Assign(leList* l, size_t idx, void* val)
45	{
46	    leListNode* node;
47	    size_t pos;
48	
49	    if(l == NULL || val == NULL || idx >= l->size)
50	        return -1;
51	    
52	    /* iterate through the nodes for the desired idx */
53	    node = l->head;
54	
55	    for(pos = 0; pos < idx; pos++)
56	    {
57	        node = node->next;
58	    }
59	    
60	    /* assign the new val to the node */
61	    node->val = val;
62	
63	    return 0;
64	}
65	    
66	int32_t leList_PushFront(leList* l, void* val)
67	{
68	    leListNode* node;
69	    void* ptr;
70	
71	    if(l == NULL || val == NULL)
72	        return -1;
73	
74	    /* create a new node */
75	    ptr = LE_MALLOC(sizeof(leListNode));
76	
77	    if(ptr == NULL)
78	        return -1;
79	
80	    node = (leListNode*)ptr;
81	
82	    node->next = NULL;
83	    node->val = val;
84	
85	    /* if list is empty just insert */
86	    if(l->size == 0)
87	    {
88	        l->head = node;
89	        l->tail = node;
90	    }
91	    /* insert into list */
92	    else
93	    {
94	        /* set node's next to _head */
95	        node->next = l->head;
96	
97	        /* set _head to node */
98	        l->head = node;                    
99	    }
100	
101	    l->size++;
102	
103	    return 0;
104	}
105	
106	void leList_PopFront(leList* l)
107	{
108	    leListNode* n;
109	
110	    if(l == NULL)
111	        return;
112	
113	    if(l->size == 0)
114	        return;
115	
116	    /* clear the list */
117	    if(l->size == 1)
118	    {
119	        LE_FREE(l->head);
120	
121	        l->head = NULL;
122	        l->tail = NULL;
123	
124	        l->size = 0;
125	    }
126	    /* remove the head */
127	    else
128	    {
129	        n = l->head;
130	
131	        /* set the new head */
132	        l->head = n->next;
133	        
134	        /* free the old head */
135	        LE_FREE(n);
136	        
137	        l->size--;
138	    }
139	}

## Findings: Marvin UI Layer Architecture & Detachment Analysis

Based on systematic exploration of the Marvin firmware UI layer, here are the answers to your five specific questions:

---

### 1. **Dashboard Interactivity & Event Callbacks**

**Dashboard widgets with event callbacks:**
- `Dashboard_BUTTON_SYSYEM_NAVIGATION` (hamburger): line 301 of `le_gen_screen_Dashboard.c` has `setPressedEventCallback(Dashboard_BUTTON_SYSYEM_NAVIGATION, event_Dashboard_BUTTON_SYSYEM_NAVIGATION_OnPressed)`
- `Dashboard_BUTTON_GUITAR_STRUM_UP`: line 1124-1125 has both `setPressedEventCallback` and `setReleasedEventCallback`
- `Dashboard_BUTTON_GUITAR_STRUM_DOWN`: line 1160-1161 has both callbacks

**Repaint mechanism:** When a button is pressed, `setPressed()` in `/config/default/gfx/legato/widget/button/legato_widget_button.c` line 191 executes:
1. Calls the `pressedEvent` callback (line 203-205)
2. Marks the widget dirty if the pressed/released images differ or if there's a pressed offset (lines 232-249)
3. Calls `_this->fn->invalidate(_this)` at line 253, which **queues damage to the renderer's damage rect array**

**Legato attachment requirement:** YES, the screen's root **must remain attached** to the layer (canvas) for damage tracking to work. The `invalidate()` call queues damage into `leRendererState.currentRenderLayer->currentDamageRects` (line 481 of `legato_renderer.c`). If the root is detached via `leRemoveRootWidget()` (which removes it as a child of `layer->root`), it is no longer in the widget tree that the renderer traverses during damage computation, so invalidations will be silently ignored or operate on a dangling tree.

---

### 2. **Nav Drawer Re-rendering**

**Nav re-render triggers:**
- `nav_open()` line 137: calls `Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->invalidate()` to force full repaint before showing
- `nav_close()` line 150: calls `nav_slide_to(NAV_CLOSED_X)` which uses canvas effects; no widget-tree damage
- `nav_highlight()` line 69: calls `b->fn->setScheme()` on each button; setScheme internally marks the button dirty (calls `invalidate`)
- Slide animation: via `gfxcStartEffectMove()` (canvas-level, not Legato widget damage)

**Navigation_OnShow (lines 185-201 of `screen_nav.c`):**
1. Removes nav root from canvas 0 (line 188)
2. Re-adds it to NAV_CANVAS (canvas 1) via `leAddRootWidget()` at line 189
3. Sets nav panel enabled/visible at lines 191-192
4. Configures canvas window position (off-screen at NAV_CLOSED_X) and layer binding at lines 195-198
5. Calls `nav_buttons_init()` which registers runtime event callbacks (lines 104, 106)

**Root attachment:** The nav root is **continuously attached to NAV_CANVAS** while the drawer exists. It is detached only if explicitly removed. The slide animation works at the **canvas window level** (gfxcStartEffectMove clips the canvas window position) independent of Legato's widget tree attachment; however, widget damage (from `nav_highlight` via `setScheme`) still requires the root to be attached to propagate `invalidate()` calls into the renderer's damage system.

---

### 3. **Live Telemetry Updates**

**Current state:** No runtime text updates found wired into dashboard widgets. Search for `setText`/`setString` calls targeting `Dashboard_*` widgets outside generated files yields **no results**. All label text (CPU, MEMORY, TEMP, UPTIME, LATENCY, SCORE, ACCURACY, COMBO, HIT, MISS, voltage "12.4V", etc.) in `le_gen_screen_Dashboard.c` are authored statically at generation time (e.g., line 426: `Dashboard_label_START->fn->setString(Dashboard_label_START, (leString*)&string_figmaStr_START)`).

**Telemetry wiring:** No application-side update loop discovered binding live telemetry to dashboard labels. If telemetry updates were to be added, they would call `setString()` on the label widget, which internally triggers `invalidate()` via string callbacks (lines 277-281 of `legato_widget_button.c` show the pattern; labels follow the same model).

---

### 4. **Steady-State Render Cost (Attached, No Damage)**

**Damage early-out:** In `legato_renderer.c` line 487-491, the `preLayer()` function checks if the scratch damage rect list is empty after merging prev + current damage:

```c
if(_rendererState.currentRenderLayer->scratchRectList.size == 0)
{
    _rendererState.frameState = LE_FRAME_POSTLAYER;
    return;
}
```

**Cost when attached with no damage:** **Minimal, nearly free.** If no widgets have been invalidated:
- `leUpdate()` (line 376 of `legato_state.c`) calls `leEvent_ProcessEvents()` (line 385), then `updateWidgets()` (line 438), then `leRenderer_Paint()` (line 440)
- `leRenderer_Paint()` advances through frame states; at `PRELAYER` (line 303 of `legato_renderer.c`), `preLayer()` runs, the damage list is empty, and it early-returns to `POSTLAYER` without drawing anything
- This is a **O(1) skip** per layer per frame

**Cost when detached:** The root is simply not in the widget tree; no traversal, no damage accumulation. However, re-attaching requires a full paint (line 126 of `ui_manager.c`: `dash->fn->invalidate(dash)` after `leAddRootWidget`).

---

### 5. **Concurrency: leAddRootWidget / leRemoveRootWidget Safety**

**Root-list mutation & locking:** 

In `legato_state.c` lines 755-790, `leAddRootWidget()` and `leRemoveRootWidget()` mutate `_state.layerList` by calling `leList_Get()` (line 763, 780) and then `LE_OCALL(layer->root, addChild/removeChild, wgt)` (lines 767, 782). 

**No locking found:** Inspection of `legato_list.c` (the underlying list implementation) and `legato_state.c` reveals **no mutex, semaphore, critical section, or atomic operations**. The code is not RTOS-aware:
- No `portENTER_CRITICAL()` / `portEXIT_CRITICAL()` (FreeRTOS guards)
- No `xSemaphoreTake()` / `xSemaphoreGive()`
- No volatile or atomic qualifiers on shared state

**Race condition exists:** If `leAddRootWidget()` / `leRemoveRootWidget()` is called while `leUpdate()` → `leRenderer_Paint()` traverses the `layerList` (lines 390-417 of `legato_state.c` iterate over `state->layerList.size`), a concurrent modification would corrupt the list or skip layers. The current architecture assumes **single-threaded Legato operation** or that the caller (ui_manager.c, screen_nav.c) serializes add/remove calls with render task scheduling.

**Evidence of single-threaded design:** In `ui_manager.c` lines 106-113, `leRemoveRootWidget()` is called **before the scheduler starts** (pre-scheduler in `UiManager_Initialize`), avoiding any concurrency. Re-attachment in `UiManager_AttachMainScreens()` is called by the loader task, which must be externally synchronized with the render task (no in-code protection observed).

---

### Summary

- **Dashboard buttons emit damage via invalidate()** → requires root attached for damage to be queued and rendered
- **Nav drawer slide is canvas-level** (independent of widget attachment), but nav-menu selection (setScheme → invalidate) **requires root attached**
- **No live telemetry wiring** currently; if added, would follow setString → invalidate pattern
- **No damage = no render work** (early-out in preLayer at ~487 lines of legato_renderer.c); steady-state cost is negligible
- **No thread-safety** on root-list mutations; single-threaded operation or external serialization required

My exploration turned up something decisive that changes the trade-off, so let me surface it before planning further.

**Key finding:** detaching a screen from Legato after it paints would **break its interactivity**. Dashboard buttons (hamburger, strum up/down) and the nav's selection highlight all repaint by calling `invalidate()`, which only queues damage if the screen's root is **attached** to its layer (`legato_widget_button.c:253` → `legato_renderer.c:481`). Detach it and those visual updates are silently dropped. And the payoff for detaching is ~nil: when an attached screen has no damage, the renderer early-outs in O(1) (`legato_renderer.c:487`), so leaving the dashboard attached-but-idle costs essentially nothing per frame.

Also relevant: the reason the screens are *currently* detached during boot isn't to save render cost — it's to keep `LEGATO_Tasks` (priority 2) from starving the priority-1 SD tasks during the splash read. That detach-until-after-the-read is load-bearing for the ~446 ms read time we measured.

So "unbind after painting" would cost interactivity and buy nothing. Let me confirm the direction with you before I write the plan.

---

# Clean rewrite design: `ui_manager.{c,h}` + `loader.{c,h}`

## Key facts established from the code

- **`LE_LAYER_COUNT == 3`** (`legato_config.h:156`). Legato has exactly 3 logical layers (0,1,2). Every generated `screenInit_*` builds its tree detached, then ends with `leAddRootWidget(root0, 0)` — they **all target layer 0**. `screenGetRoot_X(idx)` returns the root only for `idx==0`, NULL otherwise. So the only way to init N screens that each build into layer 0 is sequential: init → remove from layer 0 → init next. This confirms the prompt's "one at a time into layer 0" requirement is forced by the generator, not a choice.
- **The race surface is exactly two calls**: `leAddRootWidget` / `leRemoveRootWidget` (`legato_state.c:755-790`). Each does `leList_Get` on `_state.layerList` + `leRenderer_DamageArea` + `addChild/removeChild` on `layer->root`. No locking. `LEGATO_Tasks` (prio 2) and `SYS_INPUT_Tasks` (prio 2) both traverse these lists every tick. The tree *build* (the `addChild` storm inside `screenInit_*`) operates on a detached `root0`, so it is race-free; only the final attach/detach touches shared state.
- **At Phase 2 entry, no app roots are attached to any layer** (splash is a raw FB, not Legato). So Legato is genuinely idle — its layer roots are empty. Suspending `LEGATO_Tasks` at that moment cannot interrupt a render of our content because there is no content yet. This is materially different from the old "suspend LEGATO to manually drive rendering" pattern the journal abandoned: here suspend is a one-shot mutual-exclusion guard around list mutation, then resume hands rendering back to Legato.
- **Task names/priorities** (tasks.c): `"LEGATO_Tasks"` p2, `"SYS_INPUT_Tasks"` p2, `"GFX_CANVAS_Tasks"` p2, `"XLCDC_Tasks"` p2. Loader is p2. `xTaskGetHandle` by name works (INCLUDE flags on per the prompt).
- **`GFX_CANVAS_Tasks`** commits canvas → layer scanout latches and frees scratch tiles. It is NOT a consumer of Legato's root lists; suspending it is unnecessary and harmful (the canvas commit between render passes is what frees scratch — `wait_render_idle` already documents this). Leave it running.

---

## Division of responsibilities (the core cleanup)

The current files tangle three distinct concerns into `ui_manager.c`. Split into two clear roles:

**`ui_manager` = the compositor / screen manager (stateless mechanism + screen registry).**
Owns: canvas surface pool, canvas↔HW-layer binding, layer color-mode pokes, the splash framebuffer, backlight GPIO, and a **screen table** that knows how to init/bind each Legato screen. Exposes verbs. Knows nothing about *timing* or *boot order*.

**`loader` = the boot sequencer (policy + ordering).**
Owns: the two-phase boot *sequence*, SD I/O, the serialization guard around Phase 2, the splash-hold timing, render-idle wait, and the handoff to `App_StartServices` + video. Calls `ui_manager` verbs in order. Knows nothing about *how* a canvas binds to a layer.

This is the central fix: today `UiManager_Initialize` runs an implicit boot sequence (build, show, detach) pre-scheduler, and the loader runs the rest post-scheduler. The sequence is split across two files and two execution phases with subtle ordering comments gluing them. The rewrite moves **all sequencing into the loader** and makes `ui_manager` a pure verb provider. `App_Initialize` only allocates surfaces + creates the loader task.

---

## `ui_manager.h` — public API

Constants (move HW layer + canvas ids + geometry here as the single source of truth; `screen_nav.c` should `#include "ui_manager.h"` for `HW_OVR1` rather than redefining it — see "things that should move"):

```
HW_BASE / HW_OVR1 / HW_OVR2          (LCDC indices 0/2/3; HEO=1 off-limits)
BASE_W / BASE_H                       (1280x800)
```

**Phase 0 — surface setup (pre-scheduler, from App_Initialize):**
- `void UiManager_Initialize(void);`
  Assigns the static canvas buffers (`gfxcSetPixelBuffer` for dash + splash), calls `Nav_InitSurface()`, drives `GFX_CANVAS_Task()` once to reach RUNNING, sets the Legato string table. **Does NOT build, show, or detach any screen.** No layer binds. This is the only thing that must run pre-scheduler, and it is pure allocation. Everything sequencing-related leaves this function.

**Phase 1 — splash verbs (Legato-independent):**
- `void *UiManager_SplashFramebuffer(uint32_t *bytes);` — raw RGBA8888 buffer + size (read target).
- `void UiManager_FillSplash(void);` — opaque-black fallback fill.
- `void UiManager_ShowSplash(void);` — bind splash canvas → splash HW layer, set window full-screen, `gfxcShowCanvas` + `gfxcCanvasUpdate`, poke layer to RGBA8888 via `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode`. (Today this is inline at the bottom of `UiManager_Initialize`; it becomes an explicit verb the loader calls *after* the SD read.)
- `void UiManager_CommitSplash(void);` — re-latch after a buffer write (`gfxcCanvasUpdate`).
- `void UiManager_HideSplash(void);` — hide splash canvas + restore the shared overlay layer's color mode to RGB565 for the nav. (This is today's `RevealDashboard` minus the dashboard knowledge — renamed to describe *what it does* mechanically. The loader composes "hide splash" as the reveal.)
- `void UiManager_EnableBacklight(void);` — PC18 GPIO (unchanged).

**Phase 2 — screen registry + binding verbs:**

This is the new abstraction that makes it scale to 6+ screens. A static screen table:

```
typedef struct {
    leResult (*init)(void);            // generated screenInit_X
    leWidget*(*getRoot)(uint32_t);     // generated screenGetRoot_X
    void     (*bind)(void);            // canvas+layer bind hook (e.g. Dashboard_OnShow / Navigation_OnShow)
    uint32_t canvasId;                 // canvas this screen renders into
} ui_screen_t;
```

- `void UiManager_InitScreens(void);`
  Iterates the table and performs the **init-each → disconnect** dance, entirely within layer 0:
  for each screen: `s->init()` (builds tree, ends attached to Legato layer 0) → `leRemoveRootWidget(s->getRoot(0), 0)` to free layer 0 for the next screen. After the loop, **no screen is attached anywhere.** This generalizes to N screens with zero per-screen code — adding screen #7 is one table row.
- `void UiManager_BindActiveScreens(void);`
  Calls each active screen's `bind()` hook, which re-hosts its root onto its own canvas and binds that canvas to its display HW layer, then `leAddRootWidget(root, canvasId)` and `invalidate()`. Dashboard → BASE, nav → OVR1. For 6+ screens, only the currently-visible set is bound; off-screen screens stay built-but-detached and are bound on demand at switch time (same verb, called per-screen).

  Note the existing `Dashboard_OnShow`/`Navigation_OnShow` already *are* the per-screen bind hooks (they do `gfxcSetLayer` + window + show). They become the `bind` table entries. `screenShow_X` (the generated wrapper) is bypassed because it also flips a `showing` guard and re-attaches to layer 0 — the registry calls the OnShow bind directly after attaching to the screen's own canvas, matching what `Navigation_OnShow` already does (`leRemoveRootWidget(root,0); leAddRootWidget(root, NAV_CANVAS)`).

The split of `InitScreens` (the racy list-mutation phase) from `BindActiveScreens` lets the loader wrap **only** the mutation phase in the suspend guard, and is what makes the runtime-switch story clean: switching screens later is just `BindActiveScreens`-style attach/detach on already-built trees, guarded the same way.

**Remove from the public API:** `UiManager_AttachMainScreens` (folded into `BindActiveScreens`) and `UiManager_RevealDashboard` (becomes `UiManager_HideSplash`, owned compositionally by the loader). `Dashboard_OnShow` stays defined in `ui_manager.c` (it is the dashboard's bind hook) but is referenced via the table, not called by name.

- `s_fb_base` (RGB565) and `s_fb_splash` (RGBA8888) statics — unchanged, nocache.
- `static const ui_screen_t s_screens[]` — `{Dashboard..., Navigation...}` today; grows later.
- `UiManager_Initialize` — surfaces only (see above).
- Splash verbs — `ShowSplash`/`CommitSplash`/`HideSplash`/`FillSplash`/`SplashFramebuffer` as above.
- `UiManager_InitScreens` / `UiManager_BindActiveScreens` — table-driven.
- `Dashboard_OnShow` — stays (dashboard's bind hook; binds canvas 0 → BASE).
- `UiManager_EnableBacklight` — unchanged.

The big comment block at the top of today's file (canvas/layer model) stays as a file header — it is accurate and load-bearing.

## `loader.h` — public API

Unchanged surface: `void Loader_Start(void);`. The header comment should be rewritten to describe the **two-phase** sequence accurately (Phase 1 splash before anything Legato; Phase 2 guarded screen init; reveal; handoff).

---

## `loader.c` — the boot sequence (the policy owner)

New static helpers, in addition to the existing `load_splash_into` and `wait_render_idle` (both kept verbatim — they are good):

- `static void legato_guard_enter(void)` / `static void legato_guard_exit(void)`:
  Look up `"LEGATO_Tasks"` and `"SYS_INPUT_Tasks"` via `xTaskGetHandle`, `vTaskSuspend` both on enter, `vTaskResume` both on exit. Cache the two handles in file statics so exit doesn't re-look-up. If a handle is NULL (name mismatch), log and **skip the guard** rather than crash — degrade to unguarded (the old behavior) rather than hang. `GFX_CANVAS_Tasks` is deliberately left running.

`loader_task` sequence (the explicit two-phase boot, all in one place):

```
PHASE 1 — splash, as fast as the SD allows, before any Legato work:
  fb = UiManager_SplashFramebuffer(&cap)
  if (!load_splash_into(fb, cap)) UiManager_FillSplash()   // mount+read ~785ms, or fallback
  UiManager_CommitSplash()
  UiManager_ShowSplash()         // bind splash→overlay layer, poke 32bpp
  UiManager_EnableBacklight()    // panel lights NOW
  shown_at = now

PHASE 2 — Legato screens, behind the lit splash, guarded:
  legato_guard_enter()           // suspend LEGATO_Tasks + SYS_INPUT_Tasks; Legato idle (no roots attached)
  UiManager_InitScreens()        // init-each → leRemoveRootWidget; all detached at end
  UiManager_BindActiveScreens()  // dashboard→BASE, nav→OVR1; leAddRootWidget + invalidate
  legato_guard_exit()            // resume; normal LEGATO_Tasks now paints the bound trees

  // --- asset pre-load slot (album art → DDR) goes here, none yet ---

  wait_render_idle()             // bounded; never reveal a partial dashboard
  hold-to-SPLASH_MIN_MS since shown_at
  UiManager_HideSplash()         // reveal dashboard (already painted behind splash); restore OVR1→RGB565

HANDOFF (unchanged):
  App_StartServices()
  Video_SetWindow / CaptureEnable / DisplayShow
  vTaskDelete(NULL)
```

Why the guard wraps only Phase 2 init+bind: the only shared-state mutations are the `leRemoveRootWidget` calls in `InitScreens` and the `leAddRootWidget` calls in `BindActiveScreens`. Suspending across both makes the whole "build the scene graph" operation atomic w.r.t. the two reader tasks. We resume *before* `wait_render_idle` precisely because normal rendering must run to paint the now-bound trees.

---

## Why suspend (not priority-raise) is the right serialization here

The prompt asks to evaluate suspend vs. temporarily raising the loader's priority above LEGATO.

- **Suspend `LEGATO_Tasks` + `SYS_INPUT_Tasks`:** A hard guarantee. The two readers cannot run between `vTaskSuspend` and `vTaskResume` regardless of blocking. Crucially, **at suspend time no app roots are attached**, so LEGATO is idle — suspending cannot freeze a half-rendered frame of our content, and there is no content on screen but the raw splash FB (which is pure XLCDC scanout, unaffected by LEGATO being suspended). This is the clean choice and matches the prompt's leaning. The journal's earlier retreat from suspending LEGATO was about *driving* rendering manually while suspended; that anti-pattern does not apply to a one-shot construction guard followed by resume.
- **Priority-raise:** Only protects against preemption, *not* against the loader blocking. `InitScreens` calls `leRemoveRootWidget` per screen with no I/O, so today it won't block — but the moment Phase 2 grows (e.g. a screen init that touches a cached asset, or a future yield), a blocked higher-prio loader lets a p2 reader run mid-mutation. It is a guarantee that erodes as the code grows. Reject it.

So: suspend, with a NULL-handle fallback to unguarded. Document at the suspend site that it is safe *because* no roots are attached yet.

---

## Extensibility to 6+ runtime-switched screens

- Adding a screen = one row in `s_screens[]` (`init`, `getRoot`, `bind`, `canvasId`) + one static canvas buffer. `InitScreens` already loops, so init/disconnect scales for free within the 3-Legato-layer constraint (each builds into layer 0 then vacates it).
- **3 Legato layers vs. 6 screens is fine** because Legato layers are *render targets during construction*, not display layers. After `InitScreens`, every screen's root is detached. A screen is "live" only when `BindActiveScreens` (or a future `UiManager_ShowScreen(id)` / `UiManager_HideScreen(id)`) attaches its root to its **own canvas id** (`leAddRootWidget(root, canvasId)`) and points that canvas at a HW layer. Multiple built-but-detached screens coexist; only the bound ones consume a HW layer. Runtime switching = detach the outgoing root from its canvas, attach the incoming — same guard mechanism, reusable as `legato_guard_enter/exit` (consider promoting it to a `UiManager_BeginSceneEdit/EndSceneEdit` pair if switches happen outside the loader; the loader is the only caller today, so keep it in loader.c for now and lift it when the second caller appears).
- The HW-layer budget (BASE, OVR1, OVR2, with HEO reserved) is the real constraint on *simultaneously visible* screens, not on how many are built. Document that in the `ui_manager.c` header.

---

133	/* The splash canvas's pixel buffer (OVR2 scanout). The loader reads splash.raw
134	 * straight into this — it's RGBA8888 in the layer's native byte order, so the
135	 * read IS the load; no decode or blit. *bytes (if non-NULL) = its size. */
136	void *UiManager_SplashFramebuffer(uint32_t *bytes)
137	{
138	    if (bytes != NULL) { *bytes = (uint32_t)sizeof(s_fb_splash); }
139	    return s_fb_splash;
140	}
141	
142	/* Fill the splash buffer with the fallback colour (opaque black). The loader
143	 * calls this only when the SD splash read fails — the happy-path read overwrites
144	 * the whole buffer, so there's no point pre-filling it at init. */
145	void UiManager_FillSplash(void)
146	{
147	    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < (BASE_W * BASE_H); i++) { s_fb_splash[i] = SPLASH_FILL; }
148	}
149	
150	/* Re-latch the splash canvas after the loader writes new pixels into it, so the
151	 * splash layer scans the updated buffer. */
152	void UiManager_CommitSplash(void)
153	{
154	    gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_SPLASH);
155	}
156	
157	/* Reveal the (already painted, behind-the-splash) dashboard by dropping the
158	 * splash overlay. The dashboard canvas is already bound to BASE and full; hiding
159	 * the splash's OVR1 uncovers it instantly. Called by the loader once the dashboard
160	 * is painted. The splash has no Legato root (it's a raw framebuffer), so there's
161	 * nothing in the input pick path to detach — just hide the canvas. */
162	void UiManager_RevealDashboard(void)
163	{
164	    gfxcHideCanvas(CANVAS_SPLASH);
165	    gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_SPLASH);
166	
167	    /* Restore OVR1 to RGB565. The splash poked it to 32bpp, but the nav drawer
168	     * (the other OVR1 user, shown only after this) is RGB565 and the XLCDC driver
169	     * won't rewrite the layer mode on its own. */
170	    XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, true);
171	}
172	
173	/* Turn on the LCD backlight. The backlight is a plain GPIO enable
174	 * (AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN / PC18), NOT the LCDC PWM that XLCDC_EnableBacklight()
175	 * drives — that PWM output isn't wired to this board's backlight, so enabling it
176	 * does nothing visible. Drive the enable pin directly instead. The pin starts
177	 * low at boot (MCC PIO config), so the panel stays dark until the loader calls
178	 * this once the splash is painted — no pre-splash frame. Active-high assumed
179	 * (the _Set name == enable); flip to _Clear if the board is active-low. */
180	void UiManager_EnableBacklight(void)
181	{
182	    AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN_Set();
183	}
184	
185	/* Dashboard screen composition root (declared in le_gen_screen_Dashboard.h).
186	 * Binds the dashboard canvas to the BASE hardware layer. The nav drawer is its own screen
187	 * (Navigation), hosted by ui/nav from its own OnShow hook. */
188	void Dashboard_OnShow(void)
189	{
190	    gfxcSetWindowPosition(CANVAS_DASH, 0, 0);
191	    gfxcSetWindowSize(CANVAS_DASH, BASE_W, BASE_H);
192	    gfxcSetLayer(CANVAS_DASH, HW_BASE);
193	    gfxcShowCanvas(CANVAS_DASH);
194	    gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_DASH);
195	}

14	#include "video/video.h"
15	#include "ui/ui_manager.h"
16	#include "gfx/legato/renderer/legato_renderer.h"  /* leRenderer_IsIdle */
17	
18	#define LOADER_TASK_STACK_WORDS  1024u
19	#define LOADER_TASK_PRIORITY     2u    /* UI band; blocks on SD I/O + the render wait */
20	
21	#define SPLASH_REL_PATH    "/ui/splash.raw"
22	#define SPLASH_READ_CHUNK  (64u * 1024u)
23	
24	#define SPLASH_MIN_MS              5000u  /* hold the splash at least this long */
25	
26	/* Render-completion wait. leRenderer_IsIdle() is just frameState == READY, which
27	 * is also true in the gaps *between* leUpdate calls — and LEGATO_Tasks only ticks
28	 * every ~10 ms, so a full-screen paint spans several frames. A single idle sample
29	 * therefore reads "done" mid-paint. So require idle to hold continuously for a
30	 * window several leUpdate cycles long before trusting it. Bounded overall. */
31	#define RENDER_POLL_MS              5u
32	#define RENDER_IDLE_STABLE_MS     120u   /* idle must persist this long (>> ~10 ms tick) */
33	#define RENDER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS   8000u
34	
35	/* Video window: 720×480 video at (280, 76) on the 1280×800 panel — 1:1 with the
36	 * bridge's typical 480p source, leaving a UI strip below. */
37	#define VIDEO_WIN_X   280u
38	#define VIDEO_WIN_Y    76u
39	#define VIDEO_WIN_W   720u
40	#define VIDEO_WIN_H   480u
41	
42	static StackType_t  s_task_stack[LOADER_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
43	static StaticTask_t s_task_tcb;
44	
45	/* Read the raw splash file straight into the OVR2 canvas buffer `dst` (capacity
46	 * `cap` bytes — the buffer OVR2 scans out). The file is raw RGBA8888 in the
47	 * layer's byte order, so the read IS the load: no decode, no blit. Returns false
48	 * on any failure (no card, missing file, wrong size, short read) — caller leaves
49	 * the pre-filled solid splash in place. */
50	static bool load_splash_into(uint8_t *dst, uint32_t cap)
51	{
52	    if (!Storage_Mount()) { return false; }
53	
54	    /* Time the file access (open + read + close) separately from the mount,
55	     * which Storage_Mount already logs — so the boot log shows the mount-vs-read
56	     * split of the "mount + read" window. */
57	    TickType_t read_t0 = xTaskGetTickCount();
58	
59	    char path[64];
60	    (void)snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s%s", Storage_MountPoint(), SPLASH_REL_PATH);
61	
62	    SYS_FS_HANDLE h = SYS_FS_FileOpen(path, SYS_FS_FILE_OPEN_READ);
63	    if (h == SYS_FS_HANDLE_INVALID)
64	    {
65	        LOG_WARN("LOADER: no splash %s (fs err %d)\r\n", path, (int)SYS_FS_Error());
66	        return false;
67	    }
68	
69	    /* Raw is fixed-size: anything else is the wrong dimensions/format and would
70	     * render as garbage, so require an exact match to the canvas buffer. */
71	    int32_t sz = SYS_FS_FileSize(h);
72	    if (sz != (int32_t)cap)
73	    {
74	        LOG_WARN("LOADER: splash size %ld != expected %u\r\n", (long)sz, (unsigned)cap);
75	        (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);
76	        return false;
77	    }
78	
79	    uint32_t total = 0u;
80	    bool err = false;
81	    while (total < (uint32_t)sz)
82	    {
83	        size_t want = (size_t)((uint32_t)sz - total);
84	        if (want > SPLASH_READ_CHUNK) { want = SPLASH_READ_CHUNK; }
85	
86	        size_t got = SYS_FS_FileRead(h, &dst[total], want);
87	        if (got == 0u || got == (size_t)-1) { err = true; break; }
88	        total += (uint32_t)got;
89	    }
90	    (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);
91	
92	    if (err || total != (uint32_t)sz)
93	    {
94	        LOG_WARN("LOADER: splash read short %lu/%ld\r\n", (unsigned long)total, (long)sz);
95	        return false;
96	    }
97	    uint32_t read_ms = (uint32_t)((xTaskGetTickCount() - read_t0) * portTICK_PERIOD_MS);
98	    LOG_INFO("LOADER: splash %lu B read in %lu ms\r\n", (unsigned long)total, (unsigned long)read_ms);
99	    return true;
100	}
101	
102	/* Block until the Legato render task has fully painted all pending damage.
103	 *
104	 * We do NOT drive leUpdate ourselves — the normal LEGATO_Tasks + GFX_CANVAS_Task
105	 * pair renders the full screen correctly (a full-screen surface spans several
106	 * scratch tiles, and the scratch is freed by the canvas commit between render
107	 * passes; that only happens when those tasks actually run). So the loader just
108	 * yields and polls the public idle flag. First wait for the task to pick up the
109	 * queued damage (go busy), then wait for it to finish — both bounded so a render
110	 * stall can't hang boot. */
111	static void wait_render_idle(void)
112	{
113	    TickType_t  deadline   = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS);
114	    TickType_t  idle_since = 0;
115	    bool        idle_run   = false;
116	
117	    while (xTaskGetTickCount() < deadline)
118	    {
119	        if (leRenderer_IsIdle())
120	        {
121	            /* Idle must hold continuously — a lone idle sample is just an
122	             * inter-frame gap, not a finished paint. */
123	            if (!idle_run)
124	            {
125	                idle_run   = true;
126	                idle_since = xTaskGetTickCount();
127	            }
128	            else if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - idle_since) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_STABLE_MS))
129	            {
130	                return;
131	            }
132	        }
133	        else
134	        {
135	            idle_run = false;   /* a frame started → reset the streak */
136	        }
137	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_POLL_MS));
138	    }
139	    LOG_WARN("LOADER: render-idle wait timed out\r\n");
140	}
141	
142	static void loader_task(void *param)
143	{
144	    (void)param;
145	
146	    /* UiManager_Initialize set up the splash canvas (OVR2, pre-filled solid) and
147	     * built the dashboard + nav pre-scheduler but left them detached. Sequence:
148	     * read the raw splash straight into the OVR2 buffer, light the panel, then
149	     * attach the dashboard + nav so they paint behind the splash while it's held,
150	     * then reveal. */
151	
152	    /* Mount the card and read the raw splash directly into the OVR2 canvas buffer
153	     * — no decode, no blit, the read is the load. Storage_Mount polls until the
154	     * SDMMC driver finishes card analysis (and logs how long), so this is one
155	     * bounded attempt. On failure the pre-filled solid splash stays. */
156	    uint32_t cap = 0u;
157	    uint8_t *fb  = (uint8_t *)UiManager_SplashFramebuffer(&cap);
158	    if (!load_splash_into(fb, cap))
159	    {
160	        LOG_WARN("LOADER: solid-fill splash (no image)\r\n");
161	        UiManager_FillSplash();   /* fallback colour — only paid for on failure */
162	    }
163	    UiManager_CommitSplash();
164	
165	    /* The splash is a raw framebuffer OVR2 scans out directly — no render to wait
166	     * on. Light the panel immediately. */
167	    UiManager_EnableBacklight();
168	    TickType_t shown_at = xTaskGetTickCount();
169	
170	    /* Splash is up. Now pull the dashboard + nav into the render path; they paint
171	     * behind the opaque splash while it's held, off the splash-to-screen path. */
172	    UiManager_AttachMainScreens();
173	
174	    /* --- Asset pre-load goes here (album art → DDR cache, etc.). None yet. --- */
175	
176	    /* Wait for the dashboard to finish painting (bounded) so the reveal never
177	     * shows a partial frame, then hold the splash at least SPLASH_MIN_MS so a
178	     * fast paint doesn't flash it away. */
179	    wait_render_idle();
180	    TickType_t elapsed   = xTaskGetTickCount() - shown_at;
181	    TickType_t min_ticks = pdMS_TO_TICKS(SPLASH_MIN_MS);
182	    if (elapsed < min_ticks) { vTaskDelay(min_ticks - elapsed); }
183	
184	    /* Drop the splash → the dashboard (painted behind it) is revealed, complete. */
185	    UiManager_RevealDashboard();
186	
187	    /* Splash handoff done — bring up the deferred subsystems (video, detector,
188	     * actuator links, gameplay, console, perf drain). Held off until now so
189	     * their higher-priority tasks didn't preempt the SD mount + splash render. */
190	    App_StartServices();
191	
192	    /* Camera go-live: these just set intent flags the (now-running) video task
193	     * reconciles, so the order relative to Video_Initialize above is benign. */
194	    Video_SetWindow(VIDEO_WIN_X, VIDEO_WIN_Y, VIDEO_WIN_W, VIDEO_WIN_H);
195	    Video_CaptureEnable();
196	    Video_DisplayShow();
197	
198	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
199	}
200	
201	void Loader_Start(void)
202	{
203	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(loader_task, "LoaderTask", LOADER_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
204	                            NULL, LOADER_TASK_PRIORITY, s_task_stack, &s_task_tcb);
205	}
