```text
134	     * damage fills it in. The repaint lands over the next frames as it slides.
135	     * Show first so the move is visible (the FX engine enables the layer from
136	     * canvas.active). */
137	    Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->invalidate(Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION);
138	    gfxcShowCanvas(NAV_CANVAS);
139	    nav_slide_to(0);
140	    s_nav_open = true;
141	}
142	
143	static void nav_close(void)
144	{
145	    /* Slide out to NAV_CLOSED_X (off-screen), then nav_fx_done disables the
146	     * layer. NAV_CLOSED_X avoids the -NAV_W window-clip row-wrap (see its
147	     * definition); the layer update busy-waits for the vsync latch, so the final
148	     * frame is displayed before the hide lands — keeping it in-bounds makes that
149	     * frame a harmless edge sliver instead of the panel's left columns. */
150	    nav_slide_to(NAV_CLOSED_X);
151	    s_nav_open = false;
152	}
153	
154	/* Move-effect completion callback. At the off-screen end of a close slide the
155	 * window clip leaves a degenerate sliver of the drawer composited at screen
156	 * left; disabling OVR1 outright once the slide finishes removes it cleanly. Only
157	 * acts on a completed close — an open leaves the layer shown, and a re-open
158	 * mid-close restarts the move (so this won't fire for the abandoned close). */
159	static void nav_fx_done(unsigned int canvasID, GFXC_FX_TYPE effect,
160	                        GFXC_FX_STATUS status, void *parm)
161	{
162	    (void)canvasID;
163	    (void)parm;
164	
165	    if (effect == GFXC_FX_MOVE && status == GFXC_FX_DONE && !s_nav_open)
166	    {
167	        gfxcHideCanvas(NAV_CANVAS);
168	        gfxcCanvasUpdate(NAV_CANVAS);
169	    }
170	}
171	
172	void Nav_InitSurface(void)
173	{
174	    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(NAV_CANVAS, NAV_W, NAV_H, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, s_fb_nav);
175	}
176	
177	/* Navigation screen composition root (declared in le_gen_screen_Navigation.h),
178	 * raised by screenShow_Navigation. The MGS screen authors its content on canvas
179	 * 0; move that root so it renders into NAV_CANVAS instead (the dashboard keeps
180	 * canvas 0), then bind NAV_CANVAS to the OVR1 hardware layer. Keep the panel
181	 * visible+enabled so Legato renders it into the canvas continuously, and start
182	 * closed (parked off-screen + hidden); the touch pick rect follows the canvas
183	 * window position (LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE), so a closed (off-screen) nav can't
184	 * intercept dashboard touches. The off-screen X also seeds the slide-in. */
185	void Navigation_OnShow(void)
186	{
187	    leWidget *root = screenGetRoot_Navigation(0);
188	    leRemoveRootWidget(root, 0);
189	    leAddRootWidget(root, NAV_CANVAS);
190	
191	    Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->setEnabled(Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION, LE_TRUE);
192	    Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION->fn->setVisible(Navigation_PANEL_NAVIGATION, LE_TRUE);
193	
194	    gfxcSetWindowSize(NAV_CANVAS, NAV_W, NAV_H);
195	    gfxcSetWindowPosition(NAV_CANVAS, NAV_CLOSED_X, 0);
196	    gfxcSetLayer(NAV_CANVAS, HW_OVR1);
197	    gfxcSetEffectsCallback(NAV_CANVAS, nav_fx_done, NULL);
198	    gfxcCanvasUpdate(NAV_CANVAS);
199	
200	    nav_buttons_init();
201	}
202	
203	/* Hamburger on the Dashboard screen (BASE) toggles the nav drawer. */
204	void event_Dashboard_BUTTON_SYSYEM_NAVIGATION_OnPressed(leButtonWidget* btn)
205	{
206	    (void)btn;
207	    if (s_nav_open) { nav_close(); } else { nav_open(); }
208	}
```

```text
101	
102	void APP_Initialize ( void )
103	{
104	    appData.state = APP_STATE_INIT;
105	
106	    /* Logging shim: thin wrapper over libc printf with severity filter
107	     * and FreeRTOS-aware locking. Initialized first so subsequent code
108	     * (including video task startup) can use LOG_*. Default level is
109	     * INFO; flip to DEBUG via log_set_level() to enable verbose. */
110	    log_init(LOG_LEVEL_INFO);
111	
112	    /* UI manager: owns the canvas surface pool + LCDC layer mapping and screen
113	     * startup (string table + screenInit/Show — the MGS screen state machine is
114	     * disabled). Runs before the scheduler so surfaces exist and the canvas is
115	     * RUNNING before the first render; the Dashboard screen's On-Show hook binds the
116	     * dashboard to BASE and hands the nav drawer to ui/nav. */
117	    UiManager_Initialize();
118	
119	    /* Per-frame performance log: producer-side queues only. Init here so any
120	     * producer that posts has a valid queue; the drain task spawns later in
121	     * App_StartServices (it sits above the SD tasks in priority). */
122	    PerfLog_Initialize();
123	
124	    /* SD-card storage: sets up mount state only (no I/O here — the SDMMC
125	     * driver hasn't analyzed the card pre-scheduler). The loader mounts it. */
126	    Storage_Initialize();
127	
128	    /* Per-player results log (CSV on the card). State only here; file I/O is
129	     * lazy (mounts on demand) from Results_Append / the player/scores/results
130	     * console commands. */
131	    Results_Initialize();
132	
133	    /* Song catalog (labels keyed by the recognizer's (setlist,index)). State
134	     * only here; the CSV is lazy-loaded from the card on first lookup / the
135	     * `catalog` console command. A missing catalog degrades to "Unknown song"
136	     * and never affects recognition. See game/catalog.h. */
137	    Catalog_Initialize();
138	
139	    /* Boot loader task: mounts the SD card, paints the splash image, lights the
140	     * backlight, then reveals the dashboard and calls App_StartServices to bring
141	     * up the rest of the system. Created here (pre-scheduler); runs once the
142	     * scheduler is up (it needs blocking SD/FatFs I/O). Self-deletes after the
143	     * handoff. Follows Storage/UiManager init, which it depends on.
144	     *
145	     * The video pipeline, detector, actuator links, gameplay observer, console,
146	     * and perf-log drain are NOT started here: they spawn tasks at priorities
147	     * above the SDMMC/filesystem tasks, so starting them during boot starves the
148	     * card mount and the splash render. The loader starts them post-splash via
149	     * App_StartServices. */
150	    Loader_Start();
151	}
152	
153	
154	/* Bring up the runtime subsystems deferred out of APP_Initialize. Called by the
155	 * loader once the splash is up and the dashboard revealed, so none of these
156	 * higher-priority tasks preempt the SDMMC/filesystem tasks during the card mount
157	 * + splash render. Order honors the dependencies: Video first (it owns the frame
158	 * queue the detector + gameplay observer subscribe to from their tasks). */
159	void App_StartServices(void)
160	{
161	    /* Video capture pipeline (ISC, TC358743, HEO unbind) + capture/display
162	     * state machine + bridge-status polling. Spawns VideoTask. */
163	    Video_Initialize();
164	
165	    /* Reference detector (cv_marvin_v1) + detector-state bus. Must follow
166	     * Video_Initialize since cv_marvin_v1 subscribes to the video frame queue
167	     * from inside its task. Detectors default disabled; enable + select the
168	     * active one for the timing pipeline. */
169	    Detector_Initialize();
170	    Detector_Enable(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1);
171	    Detector_SetActive(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1);
172	
173	    /* M2 actuator path: fretboard_link owns the submit queue + FLEXCOM1 USART
174	     * writer and the RX parse task (and brings up the T1S link). */
175	    FretboardLink_Initialize();
176	
177	    /* timing_pipeline runs the chord-window + strum scheduler against the
178	     * active detector and pushes the resulting 7-bit mask through
179	     * FretboardLink_Send. */
180	    TimingPipeline_Initialize();
181	
182	    /* manual_control is a peer producer for direct UI-driven actuation. UI
183	     * buttons are authored in Microchip Graphics Composer; the generated
184	     * screenShow registers the callbacks defined in ui/manual_input.c, so no
185	     * explicit bind step is needed here. */
186	    ManualControl_Initialize();
187	
188	    /* Game-state observer (spec §4.8, M9): a video-frame consumer that
189	     * classifies the current GH3 screen and publishes game_state_t events. Like
190	     * cv_marvin_v1 it subscribes to the video frame queue from its task, so it
191	     * follows Video_Initialize. Enable observation explicitly (default off). */
192	    GameplayEngine_Initialize();
193	    GameplayEngine_SetObserveEnabled(true);
194	
195	    /* Interactive operator console on FLEXCOM2 (115200), separate from the DBGU
196	     * log channel. Started after the actuator/detector modules so its commands
197	     * can drive their setters. */
198	    Console_Initialize();
199	
200	    /* Per-frame perf-log drain task, launched last so every producer's queue
201	     * handle is already valid when the first records hit the sink. */
202	    PerfLog_Start();
203	}

213	
214	void APP_Tasks ( void )
215	{
216	    /* Heap_1 free space at the end of APP_Initialize (heap_1 never frees — free
217	     * space only shrinks). The runtime subsystems spawn later via
218	     * App_StartServices, so this is the pre-services floor, not the final one.
219	     * Surfaces remaining headroom so an allocation walking into the wall is
220	     * visible rather than a silent malloc-failed spin. */
221	    LOG_INFO("freertos heap: %u bytes free\r\n", (unsigned)xPortGetFreeHeapSize());
222	
223	    /* APP is a one-shot launcher — task creation happened in APP_Initialize.
224	     * Self-delete here so the (1024-word) stack and TCB are released to the
225	     * idle task. The MCC-generated lAPP_Tasks loop will not iterate again
226	     * because vTaskDelete(NULL) never returns to its caller. */
227	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
228	}
```

---

# Clean rewrite design: `ui_manager.{c,h}` + `loader.{c,h}`

## Key facts established from the code

- **`LE_LAYER_COUNT == 3`** (`legato_config.h:156`). Legato has exactly 3 logical layers (0,1,2). Every generated `screenInit_*` builds its tree detached, then ends with `leAddRootWidget(root0, 0)` — they **all target layer 0**. `screenGetRoot_X(idx)` returns the root only for `idx==0`, NULL otherwise. So the only way to init N screens that each build into layer 0 is sequential: init → remove from layer 0 → init next. This confirms the prompt's "one at a time into layer 0" requirement is forced by the generator, not a choice.
- **The race surface is exactly two calls**: `leAddRootWidget` / `leRemoveRootWidget` (`legato_state.c:755-790`). Each does `leList_Get` on `_state.layerList` + `leRenderer_DamageArea` + `addChild/removeChild` on `layer->root`. No locking. `LEGATO_Tasks` (prio 2) and `SYS_INPUT_Tasks` (prio 2) both traverse these lists every tick. The tree *build* (the `addChild` storm inside `screenInit_*`) operates on a detached `root0`, so it is race-free; only the final attach/detach touches shared state.
- **At Phase 2 entry, no app roots are attached to any layer** (splash is a raw FB, not Legato). So Legato is genuinely idle — its layer roots are empty. Suspending `LEGATO_Tasks` at that moment cannot interrupt a render of our content because there is no content yet. This is materially different from the old "suspend LEGATO to manually drive rendering" pattern the journal abandoned: here suspend is a one-shot mutual-exclusion guard around list mutation, then resume hands rendering back to Legato.
- **Task names/priorities** (tasks.c): `"LEGATO_Tasks"` p2, `"SYS_INPUT_Tasks"` p2, `"GFX_CANVAS_Tasks"` p2, `"XLCDC_Tasks"` p2. Loader is p2. `xTaskGetHandle` by name works (INCLUDE flags on per the prompt).
- **`GFX_CANVAS_Tasks`** commits canvas → layer scanout latches and frees scratch tiles. It is NOT a consumer of Legato's root lists; suspending it is unnecessary and harmful (the canvas commit between render passes is what frees scratch — `wait_render_idle` already documents this). Leave it running.

---

## Division of responsibilities (the core cleanup)

The current files tangle three distinct concerns into `ui_manager.c`. Split into two clear roles:

**`ui_manager` = the compositor / screen manager (stateless mechanism + screen registry).**
Owns: canvas surface pool, canvas↔HW-layer binding, layer color-mode pokes, the splash framebuffer, backlight GPIO, and a **screen table** that knows how to init/bind each Legato screen. Exposes verbs. Knows nothing about *timing* or *boot order*.

**`loader` = the boot sequencer (policy + ordering).**
Owns: the two-phase boot *sequence*, SD I/O, the serialization guard around Phase 2, the splash-hold timing, render-idle wait, and the handoff to `App_StartServices` + video. Calls `ui_manager` verbs in order. Knows nothing about *how* a canvas binds to a layer.

This is the central fix: today `UiManager_Initialize` runs an implicit boot sequence (build, show, detach) pre-scheduler, and the loader runs the rest post-scheduler. The sequence is split across two files and two execution phases with subtle ordering comments gluing them. The rewrite moves **all sequencing into the loader** and makes `ui_manager` a pure verb provider. `App_Initialize` only allocates surfaces + creates the loader task.

---

## `ui_manager.h` — public API

Constants (move HW layer + canvas ids + geometry here as the single source of truth; `screen_nav.c` should `#include "ui_manager.h"` for `HW_OVR1` rather than redefining it — see "things that should move"):

```
HW_BASE / HW_OVR1 / HW_OVR2          (LCDC indices 0/2/3; HEO=1 off-limits)
BASE_W / BASE_H                       (1280x800)
```

**Phase 0 — surface setup (pre-scheduler, from App_Initialize):**
- `void UiManager_Initialize(void);`
  Assigns the static canvas buffers (`gfxcSetPixelBuffer` for dash + splash), calls `Nav_InitSurface()`, drives `GFX_CANVAS_Task()` once to reach RUNNING, sets the Legato string table. **Does NOT build, show, or detach any screen.** No layer binds. This is the only thing that must run pre-scheduler, and it is pure allocation. Everything sequencing-related leaves this function.

**Phase 1 — splash verbs (Legato-independent):**
- `void *UiManager_SplashFramebuffer(uint32_t *bytes);` — raw RGBA8888 buffer + size (read target).
- `void UiManager_FillSplash(void);` — opaque-black fallback fill.
- `void UiManager_ShowSplash(void);` — bind splash canvas → splash HW layer, set window full-screen, `gfxcShowCanvas` + `gfxcCanvasUpdate`, poke layer to RGBA8888 via `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode`. (Today this is inline at the bottom of `UiManager_Initialize`; it becomes an explicit verb the loader calls *after* the SD read.)
- `void UiManager_CommitSplash(void);` — re-latch after a buffer write (`gfxcCanvasUpdate`).
- `void UiManager_HideSplash(void);` — hide splash canvas + restore the shared overlay layer's color mode to RGB565 for the nav. (This is today's `RevealDashboard` minus the dashboard knowledge — renamed to describe *what it does* mechanically. The loader composes "hide splash" as the reveal.)
- `void UiManager_EnableBacklight(void);` — PC18 GPIO (unchanged).

**Phase 2 — screen registry + binding verbs:**

This is the new abstraction that makes it scale to 6+ screens. A static screen table:

```
typedef struct {
    leResult (*init)(void);            // generated screenInit_X
    leWidget*(*getRoot)(uint32_t);     // generated screenGetRoot_X
    void     (*bind)(void);            // canvas+layer bind hook (e.g. Dashboard_OnShow / Navigation_OnShow)
    uint32_t canvasId;                 // canvas this screen renders into
} ui_screen_t;
```

- `void UiManager_InitScreens(void);`
  Iterates the table and performs the **init-each → disconnect** dance, entirely within layer 0:
  for each screen: `s->init()` (builds tree, ends attached to Legato layer 0) → `leRemoveRootWidget(s->getRoot(0), 0)` to free layer 0 for the next screen. After the loop, **no screen is attached anywhere.** This generalizes to N screens with zero per-screen code — adding screen #7 is one table row.
- `void UiManager_BindActiveScreens(void);`
  Calls each active screen's `bind()` hook, which re-hosts its root onto its own canvas and binds that canvas to its display HW layer, then `leAddRootWidget(root, canvasId)` and `invalidate()`. Dashboard → BASE, nav → OVR1. For 6+ screens, only the currently-visible set is bound; off-screen screens stay built-but-detached and are bound on demand at switch time (same verb, called per-screen).

  Note the existing `Dashboard_OnShow`/`Navigation_OnShow` already *are* the per-screen bind hooks (they do `gfxcSetLayer` + window + show). They become the `bind` table entries. `screenShow_X` (the generated wrapper) is bypassed because it also flips a `showing` guard and re-attaches to layer 0 — the registry calls the OnShow bind directly after attaching to the screen's own canvas, matching what `Navigation_OnShow` already does (`leRemoveRootWidget(root,0); leAddRootWidget(root, NAV_CANVAS)`).

The split of `InitScreens` (the racy list-mutation phase) from `BindActiveScreens` lets the loader wrap **only** the mutation phase in the suspend guard, and is what makes the runtime-switch story clean: switching screens later is just `BindActiveScreens`-style attach/detach on already-built trees, guarded the same way.

**Remove from the public API:** `UiManager_AttachMainScreens` (folded into `BindActiveScreens`) and `UiManager_RevealDashboard` (becomes `UiManager_HideSplash`, owned compositionally by the loader). `Dashboard_OnShow` stays defined in `ui_manager.c` (it is the dashboard's bind hook) but is referenced via the table, not called by name.

---

## `ui_manager.c` — function breakdown

- `s_fb_base` (RGB565) and `s_fb_splash` (RGBA8888) statics — unchanged, nocache.
- `static const ui_screen_t s_screens[]` — `{Dashboard..., Navigation...}` today; grows later.
- `UiManager_Initialize` — surfaces only (see above).
- Splash verbs — `ShowSplash`/`CommitSplash`/`HideSplash`/`FillSplash`/`SplashFramebuffer` as above.
- `UiManager_InitScreens` / `UiManager_BindActiveScreens` — table-driven.
- `Dashboard_OnShow` — stays (dashboard's bind hook; binds canvas 0 → BASE).
- `UiManager_EnableBacklight` — unchanged.

The big comment block at the top of today's file (canvas/layer model) stays as a file header — it is accurate and load-bearing.

---

## `loader.h` — public API

Unchanged surface: `void Loader_Start(void);`. The header comment should be rewritten to describe the **two-phase** sequence accurately (Phase 1 splash before anything Legato; Phase 2 guarded screen init; reveal; handoff).

---

## `loader.c` — the boot sequence (the policy owner)

New static helpers, in addition to the existing `load_splash_into` and `wait_render_idle` (both kept verbatim — they are good):

- `static void legato_guard_enter(void)` / `static void legato_guard_exit(void)`:
  Look up `"LEGATO_Tasks"` and `"SYS_INPUT_Tasks"` via `xTaskGetHandle`, `vTaskSuspend` both on enter, `vTaskResume` both on exit. Cache the two handles in file statics so exit doesn't re-look-up. If a handle is NULL (name mismatch), log and **skip the guard** rather than crash — degrade to unguarded (the old behavior) rather than hang. `GFX_CANVAS_Tasks` is deliberately left running.

`loader_task` sequence (the explicit two-phase boot, all in one place):

```
PHASE 1 — splash, as fast as the SD allows, before any Legato work:
  fb = UiManager_SplashFramebuffer(&cap)
  if (!load_splash_into(fb, cap)) UiManager_FillSplash()   // mount+read ~785ms, or fallback
  UiManager_CommitSplash()
  UiManager_ShowSplash()         // bind splash→overlay layer, poke 32bpp
  UiManager_EnableBacklight()    // panel lights NOW
  shown_at = now

PHASE 2 — Legato screens, behind the lit splash, guarded:
  legato_guard_enter()           // suspend LEGATO_Tasks + SYS_INPUT_Tasks; Legato idle (no roots attached)
  UiManager_InitScreens()        // init-each → leRemoveRootWidget; all detached at end
  UiManager_BindActiveScreens()  // dashboard→BASE, nav→OVR1; leAddRootWidget + invalidate
  legato_guard_exit()            // resume; normal LEGATO_Tasks now paints the bound trees

  // --- asset pre-load slot (album art → DDR) goes here, none yet ---

  wait_render_idle()             // bounded; never reveal a partial dashboard
  hold-to-SPLASH_MIN_MS since shown_at
  UiManager_HideSplash()         // reveal dashboard (already painted behind splash); restore OVR1→RGB565

HANDOFF (unchanged):
  App_StartServices()
  Video_SetWindow / CaptureEnable / DisplayShow
  vTaskDelete(NULL)
```

Why the guard wraps only Phase 2 init+bind: the only shared-state mutations are the `leRemoveRootWidget` calls in `InitScreens` and the `leAddRootWidget` calls in `BindActiveScreens`. Suspending across both makes the whole "build the scene graph" operation atomic w.r.t. the two reader tasks. We resume *before* `wait_render_idle` precisely because normal rendering must run to paint the now-bound trees.

---

## Why suspend (not priority-raise) is the right serialization here

The prompt asks to evaluate suspend vs. temporarily raising the loader's priority above LEGATO.

- **Suspend `LEGATO_Tasks` + `SYS_INPUT_Tasks`:** A hard guarantee. The two readers cannot run between `vTaskSuspend` and `vTaskResume` regardless of blocking. Crucially, **at suspend time no app roots are attached**, so LEGATO is idle — suspending cannot freeze a half-rendered frame of our content, and there is no content on screen but the raw splash FB (which is pure XLCDC scanout, unaffected by LEGATO being suspended). This is the clean choice and matches the prompt's leaning. The journal's earlier retreat from suspending LEGATO was about *driving* rendering manually while suspended; that anti-pattern does not apply to a one-shot construction guard followed by resume.
- **Priority-raise:** Only protects against preemption, *not* against the loader blocking. `InitScreens` calls `leRemoveRootWidget` per screen with no I/O, so today it won't block — but the moment Phase 2 grows (e.g. a screen init that touches a cached asset, or a future yield), a blocked higher-prio loader lets a p2 reader run mid-mutation. It is a guarantee that erodes as the code grows. Reject it.

So: suspend, with a NULL-handle fallback to unguarded. Document at the suspend site that it is safe *because* no roots are attached yet.

---

## Extensibility to 6+ runtime-switched screens

- Adding a screen = one row in `s_screens[]` (`init`, `getRoot`, `bind`, `canvasId`) + one static canvas buffer. `InitScreens` already loops, so init/disconnect scales for free within the 3-Legato-layer constraint (each builds into layer 0 then vacates it).
- **3 Legato layers vs. 6 screens is fine** because Legato layers are *render targets during construction*, not display layers. After `InitScreens`, every screen's root is detached. A screen is "live" only when `BindActiveScreens` (or a future `UiManager_ShowScreen(id)` / `UiManager_HideScreen(id)`) attaches its root to its **own canvas id** (`leAddRootWidget(root, canvasId)`) and points that canvas at a HW layer. Multiple built-but-detached screens coexist; only the bound ones consume a HW layer. Runtime switching = detach the outgoing root from its canvas, attach the incoming — same guard mechanism, reusable as `legato_guard_enter/exit` (consider promoting it to a `UiManager_BeginSceneEdit/EndSceneEdit` pair if switches happen outside the loader; the loader is the only caller today, so keep it in loader.c for now and lift it when the second caller appears).
- The HW-layer budget (BASE, OVR1, OVR2, with HEO reserved) is the real constraint on *simultaneously visible* screens, not on how many are built. Document that in the `ui_manager.c` header.

---

## Things that should move between files / cleanups

1. **HW layer + canvas-id constants → `ui_manager.h`.** `screen_nav.c` currently redefines `HW_OVR1` and `NAV_CANVAS` locally (lines 17-18). Have it include `ui_manager.h` for the HW layer index. (Canvas id `NAV_CANVAS=1` can stay nav-private since nav owns that surface, but the comment cross-references should point at ui_manager.h as the registry.)
2. **All boot sequencing leaves `UiManager_Initialize`.** Today it builds+shows+detaches screens inline (lines 87-113) and shows the splash inline (99-104). All of that moves to the loader as explicit verb calls. `UiManager_Initialize` shrinks to ~surface allocation + canvas-pump + string table.
3. **`AttachMainScreens` + `RevealDashboard` collapse** into `BindActiveScreens` + `HideSplash`. The reveal becomes a pure compositor verb ("hide splash, restore overlay color mode") with the dashboard semantics living in the loader's sequence comment.
4. **Comments: strip the dev-diary tone.** Several current comments narrate decisions ("done AFTER Navigation_OnShow so…", "the loader re-attaches them with…"). Rewrite to describe current behavior only, per the constraint. Keep the load-bearing hardware facts (RGBMODE poke rationale, backlight-is-GPIO-not-PWM, canvas-vs-layer independence, NAV_CLOSED_X clip math).
5. **The `OVR1`/`OVR2` splash-layer name** must be parameterized through one `SPLASH_HW_LAYER` macro in `ui_manager.c`/`.h` so the open question below is a one-line change, and the `HideSplash` color-mode restore targets the layer the **nav** will reclaim (only relevant if splash and nav share a layer).

---

## Open questions (resolve before implementation)

1. **Splash HW layer: OVR1 or OVR2?** The code + earlier decision use **OVR1** (so OVR2 stays free for a loading-bar overlay over the splash). The latest message says "point OVR2 at it." These conflict. This changes two things: (a) which `XLCDC_LAYER_*` gets the 32bpp poke and the RGB565 restore, and (b) whether the splash shares a layer with the nav.
   - If **splash on OVR1** (shares with nav): `HideSplash` must restore OVR1→RGB565 for the nav (current behavior). OVR2 free for loading bar.
   - If **splash on OVR2** (nav keeps OVR1): splash and nav no longer share a layer, so `HideSplash` needs no color-mode restore for the nav (nav never touched OVR2); instead OVR2 must be restored/freed for whatever uses it next, and the "loading bar over splash" idea loses its dedicated free layer (only OVR1 would be free during splash, but OVR1 is the nav's). **Recommend OVR1 for the splash** unless the loading-bar plan is dropped — flag for the user.
2. **Loading-bar overlay:** is it still planned? It determines whether keeping a free overlay layer during splash is a real requirement (drives Q1).
3. **`screenShow_X` `showing` guard:** the registry bypasses `screenShow_*` and calls the OnShow bind directly. Confirm nothing downstream reads the generated `showing`/`initialized` flags (a quick grep suggests not, but the runtime-switch code may later want them). If a future `UiManager_ShowScreen` is wanted, decide whether to track active state in the screen table or lean on Legato's flags.
4. **Suspend-time assumption:** confirm no other module attaches a Legato root before the loader's Phase 2 (grep shows only nav/dashboard via the registry). If anything else ever calls `leAddRootWidget` at startup, the "Legato idle at suspend" guarantee needs re-checking.

**Answer:** OVR1. STOP ASSIGNING FIXED LAYERS TO SCREENS LIKE NAV! NAV is just a screen / canvas. we can put it on whatever damn layer we please at runtime. Yes it will typically end up on OVR1, but DO NOT ASSUME THIS!!!

# Clean rewrite: `ui_manager` + `loader`

## Context

The boot UI path works (splash ~785 ms, dashboard behind it, then services) but `ui_manager.c` and `loader.c` got tangled iterating toward that result: boot *sequencing* is split across both files and two execution phases (some pre-scheduler in `UiManager_Initialize`, some post-scheduler in the loader), with ordering comments gluing them. The splash is already a raw framebuffer (Legato-independent), so the path is ripe to separate cleanly.

Two principles from the user drive this rewrite:
1. **Splash first, self-contained:** read `/ui/splash.raw` from SD → splash framebuffer → bind it to an overlay layer → backlight on. *Then* do any MGS/Legato init.
2. **Screens do NOT own hardware layers.** A screen owns its *canvas* (render surface). Which HW layer a canvas is shown on is a runtime decision made by the boot/compositor policy — nav typically ends on OVR1, but nothing may assume that. MGS builds every screen into Legato layer 0 by default; screens init one-at-a-time through layer 0, each disconnecting to free it for the next; the active ones are then bound to display layers.

Outcome: `ui_manager` = a stateless **compositor / screen manager** (verbs + a screen registry); `loader` = the **boot sequencer** (policy + ordering). Extensible to the planned 6+ runtime-switched screens.

## Roles

- **`ui_manager`** — owns: canvas surface pool, the splash framebuffer + backlight, a screen registry (how to init each screen and host it onto its canvas), and the canvas↔HW-layer binding verb (which pokes the layer's color mode to match the canvas). Knows nothing about boot order/timing.
- **`loader`** — owns: the two-phase boot sequence, SD I/O, the serialization guard around Legato scene-graph edits, splash-hold timing, render-idle wait, and handoff to `App_StartServices()` + video. Chooses which canvas goes on which layer.

## `ui_manager.h` API

Constants (single source of truth; `screen_nav.c` includes this for the HW layer indices instead of redefining them):
- `HW_BASE=0`, `HW_OVR1=2`, `HW_OVR2=3` (HEO=1 = camera, off-limits), `BASE_W=1280`, `BASE_H=800`.
- `SPLASH_HW_LAYER` = `HW_OVR1` (one macro; OVR2 stays free for a future loading-bar overlay over the splash).

Surface setup (pre-scheduler, from `App_Initialize`):
- `void UiManager_Initialize(void)` — assign canvas pixel buffers (dashboard + splash), `Nav_InitSurface()`, pump `GFX_CANVAS_Task()` to RUNNING, set the Legato string table. **No screen build, no show, no layer bind, no sequencing.** Pure allocation.

Splash verbs (Legato-independent):
- `void *UiManager_SplashFramebuffer(uint32_t *bytes)` — raw RGBA8888 buffer + size (SD read target).
- `void UiManager_FillSplash(void)` — opaque-black fallback fill.
- `void UiManager_ShowSplash(void)` — bind splash canvas → `SPLASH_HW_LAYER`, full-screen window, show + update (uses the generic bind verb below, which pokes RGBA8888).
- `void UiManager_HideSplash(void)` — hide the splash canvas (reveal whatever's on BASE).
- `void UiManager_EnableBacklight(void)` — PC18 GPIO (unchanged).

Screen registry + binding (Phase 2):
- `void UiManager_InitScreens(void)` — iterate the screen table; for each: `screenInit_*()` (builds tree, ends attached to Legato layer 0) → `leRemoveRootWidget(getRoot(0), 0)` to vacate layer 0 for the next. Ends with every screen built and fully detached. Scales to N screens with no per-screen code.
- `void UiManager_ShowScreenOnLayer(ui_screen_id id, uint32_t hw_layer)` — host the screen onto its own canvas (its bind hook: attach root → canvas, content/window setup) and bind that canvas to `hw_layer`. The binding pokes `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(hw_layer, <canvas's mode>)` so the layer's color mode always follows the canvas placed on it (the GFX-XLCDC driver never writes RGBMODE itself). This is the one place a screen meets a layer, and the layer is a parameter — no screen hardcodes one.

Registry shape (in `ui_manager.c`):
\```
typedef struct {
    leResult (*init)(void);          // generated screenInit_X
    leWidget*(*getRoot)(uint32_t);   // generated screenGetRoot_X
    void     (*host)(void);          // attach root → own canvas + content setup (no layer bind)
    uint32_t  canvasId;              // the screen's render surface
} ui_screen_t;   // table: { DASHBOARD, NAV, ... }
\```
`canvasId` is intrinsic (the screen's surface). The **HW layer is not in the table** — it's chosen at `ShowScreenOnLayer` call time.

Removed: `UiManager_AttachMainScreens`, `UiManager_RevealDashboard`, `UiManager_CommitSplash` (folded in / renamed). `Dashboard_OnShow`/`Navigation_OnShow` become the `host` hooks (see screen_nav change).

## `loader.c` — the boot sequence (policy)

Keep `load_splash_into()` and `wait_render_idle()` (good as-is). Add a scene-edit guard:
- `legato_guard_enter()/exit()` — `xTaskGetHandle("LEGATO_Tasks")` + `"SYS_INPUT_Tasks"`, `vTaskSuspend`/`vTaskResume` both (cache handles in statics; NULL handle → log + skip guard, degrade to unguarded rather than hang). `GFX_CANVAS_Tasks` is left running (it commits canvases; not a root-list reader).

`loader_task`:
\```
// PHASE 1 — splash, before any Legato work
fb = UiManager_SplashFramebuffer(&cap)
if (!load_splash_into(fb, cap)) UiManager_FillSplash()
UiManager_ShowSplash()           // bind splash canvas → OVR1, poke RGBA8888, show
UiManager_EnableBacklight()      // panel lights here
shown_at = now

// PHASE 2 — Legato screens, behind the lit splash, guarded
legato_guard_enter()             // suspend LEGATO + SYS_INPUT; safe: no roots attached yet
UiManager_InitScreens()          // init-each → detach; all built, none attached
UiManager_ShowScreenOnLayer(DASHBOARD, HW_BASE)   // policy chooses the layers
UiManager_ShowScreenOnLayer(NAV,       HW_OVR1)   // nav hosted on OVR1 (hidden/closed)
legato_guard_exit()              // resume; LEGATO now paints the bound trees

// (asset pre-load slot — none yet)
wait_render_idle()               // bounded; never reveal a partial dashboard
hold until SPLASH_MIN_MS since shown_at   // currently 5000 ms
UiManager_HideSplash()           // reveal dashboard
App_StartServices(); Video_SetWindow/CaptureEnable/DisplayShow; vTaskDelete(NULL)
\```

Why suspend only wraps InitScreens + ShowScreenOnLayer: the sole shared-state mutations are the `leRemoveRootWidget`/`leAddRootWidget` calls. Legato has no locking (`legato_state.c` ~755-790) and `LEGATO_Tasks`/`SYS_INPUT_Tasks` (both prio 2) traverse those lists every tick. At guard-enter no app roots are attached (splash is pure XLCDC scanout), so LEGATO is idle — suspend can't freeze a half-rendered frame; resume hands rendering back. (Distinct from the journal's abandoned pattern of suspending LEGATO to *drive* rendering manually.) Priority-raise was considered and rejected: it only stops preemption, not a future blocking call mid-edit.

## `screen_nav.c` — surgical change (not a rewrite)

Remove the **hardcoded layer assumption**: today `Navigation_OnShow` (screen_nav.c:196) calls `gfxcSetLayer(NAV_CANVAS, HW_OVR1)`. Move the canvas→layer bind out to `UiManager_ShowScreenOnLayer`; `Navigation_OnShow` (the `host` hook) keeps only: attach root → `NAV_CANVAS`, panel enable/visible, window size + `NAV_CLOSED_X` position, effects callback. The slide animation already works on the canvas window (layer-agnostic), so it's unaffected. Drop the local `HW_OVR1` define; include `ui_manager.h` if a layer index is ever needed. `NAV_CANVAS` (its surface id) stays nav-private.

## Critical files
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.c` / `.h` — rewrite (compositor/screen-manager).
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/loader.c` / `.h` — rewrite (boot sequencer).
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/nav/screen_nav.c` — surgical: remove hardcoded `gfxcSetLayer(.., HW_OVR1)` + local `HW_OVR1`.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c` — verify `UiManager_Initialize` is still the only pre-scheduler UI call and the loader owns the rest (likely no change).

## Extensibility (6+ screens)
Adding a screen = one `ui_screen_t` row + one static canvas buffer. `InitScreens` loops, so init/disconnect scales within the 3-Legato-layer constraint (layers are construction targets, not display slots). A built-but-detached screen consumes no HW layer; runtime switching is `UiManager_ShowScreenOnLayer(target, layer)` for the incoming screen + hide the outgoing — same guard mechanism (promote `legato_guard_*` into `ui_manager` as `BeginSceneEdit/EndSceneEdit` when a second caller beyond the loader appears). The HW-layer budget (BASE/OVR1/OVR2; HEO=camera) limits *simultaneously visible* screens, not how many are built — documented in the `ui_manager.c` header.

## Verification
- Build in MPLAB (note `screen_splash.*` already removed; no new files added — only rewrites).
- On hardware: splash still appears (~785 ms, image correct on OVR1); after the 5 s hold the dashboard reveals fully painted; nav hamburger opens/closes and highlights correctly (confirms it was hosted on OVR1 and RGBMODE is RGB565 there); buttons respond (confirms screens stayed attached). Watch the boot log for any `LEGATO_Tasks`/`SYS_INPUT_Tasks` handle-not-found warning from the guard.
- Confirm no regression in the camera go-live (video window over the dashboard).

## Resolved / open
- **Splash layer: OVR1** (OVR2 reserved for a future loading-bar overlay) — resolved.
- Layer assignment is **runtime policy**, never screen-owned — baked into the design (`ShowScreenOnLayer(id, layer)`).
- Memory `marvin-canvas-layer-binding` to be strengthened during implementation (don't assume nav==OVR1).

# Clean rewrite: splash-as-module + ui_manager orchestrator (retire `loader`)

## Context

`ui_manager.c` and `loader.c` got tangled iterating toward the fast-splash boot: UI sequencing, layer assignment, SD I/O, and the service/video handoff are smeared across both files and across the pre-/post-scheduler boundary. The splash is already a raw framebuffer (Legato-independent), so we can separate concerns cleanly.

Target model (from the user):
1. **Splash is its own self-contained screen module** under `screens/`, **independent of Legato** — it owns its framebuffer and knows how to load itself from SD and be displayed.
2. **`ui_manager` orchestrates and composites.** It kicks off the splash, and once the splash is displayed it (a) signals the app to start everything else, and (b) proceeds to bring up the Legato screens behind the splash.
3. **Screens never own a hardware layer.** A screen owns its *canvas* (render surface); `ui_manager` decides which HW layer a canvas is shown on, at runtime. (Nav usually lands on OVR1 — never assume it.)
4. **App services start the instant the splash is shown**, in parallel with the heavier behind-the-scenes screen painting, so the whole system is warm by the time we cut over to the dashboard. Splash is held at least a few seconds.
5. **The `loader` module goes away** — splash bits → the splash module; orchestration → `ui_manager`; service/video handoff → `app` via an interlock callback.

## Modules & responsibilities

- **`screens/splash/splash.{c,h}` (new, Legato-independent):** owns `s_fb_splash` (RGBA8888, nocache) and the splash canvas surface. Verbs: `Splash_InitSurface()` (pre-scheduler `gfxcSetPixelBuffer`), `bool Splash_Load()` (read `/ui/splash.raw` into the buffer; on failure fill opaque-black and return false — still displayable), `uint32_t Splash_CanvasId()`. No layer choice, no Legato, no backlight — just "load my pixels into my canvas." Depends on `storage`, not Legato.
- **`ui_manager.{c,h}` (rewrite): orchestrator + compositor.** Owns the canvas pool numbering (`ui_manager.h` defines canvas ids + HW layer indices — the single source of truth), the boot bringup task, layer assignment, backlight, and the screen registry. It is the only thing that binds a canvas to a HW layer.
- **`app.c` (small change):** registers a "splash shown" callback; the callback starts `App_StartServices()` + camera go-live. `APP_Initialize` drops `Loader_Start()`, keeps the cheap state inits, and calls `UiManager_Initialize()`.
- **`screens/nav/screen_nav.c` (surgical):** remove the hardcoded `gfxcSetLayer(NAV_CANVAS, HW_OVR1)` from `Navigation_OnShow` and the local `HW_OVR1` define — layer binding is `ui_manager`'s call now. Nav keeps its canvas, content setup, and slide animation (canvas-window based, layer-agnostic).
- **Delete `loader.{c,h}`** and its `user.cmake` entry; add `screens/splash/splash.c`.

## `ui_manager.h` API

Constants (single source of truth): `HW_BASE=0`, `HW_OVR1=2`, `HW_OVR2=3` (HEO=1 camera, off-limits); canvas ids `CANVAS_DASH/CANVAS_NAV/CANVAS_SPLASH`; `BASE_W/BASE_H`; `SPLASH_HW_LAYER = HW_OVR1` (OVR2 left free for a future loading-bar overlay over the splash).

- `void UiManager_Initialize(void)` — pre-scheduler: assign canvas buffers (dash + `Splash_InitSurface()` + `Nav_InitSurface()`), pump `GFX_CANVAS_Task()` to RUNNING, set the Legato string table, and create the bringup task. Pure setup; no build/show/sequence inline.
- `void UiManager_SetSplashShownCallback(void (*cb)(void))` — app registers its "splash is up, start everything else" hook.
- `void UiManager_EnableBacklight(void)` — PC18 GPIO (unchanged).
- (compositor verb, used internally + reusable for future screen switching) `void UiManager_ShowScreenOnLayer(ui_screen_id id, uint32_t hw_layer)` — host the screen onto its own canvas (its `host` hook) and bind that canvas to `hw_layer`, poking `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(hw_layer, <canvas's color mode>)` so the layer's mode always follows the canvas placed on it (the GFX-XLCDC driver never writes RGBMODE itself — this removes the old "restore OVR1→RGB565 for nav" special case).

Screen registry (in `ui_manager.c`): `{ leResult(*init)(void); leWidget*(*getRoot)(uint32_t); void(*host)(void); uint32_t canvasId; }` rows for Dashboard, Nav (+future). `canvasId` is intrinsic; **HW layer is never in the table** — passed at `ShowScreenOnLayer` time.

## Boot bringup task (in `ui_manager.c`)

\```
// PHASE 1 — splash (Legato-independent), first
Splash_Load()                       // splash module: SD read into its fb, or fallback fill
UiManager_ShowScreenOnLayer(SPLASH, SPLASH_HW_LAYER)   // bind splash canvas → OVR1, poke RGBA8888, show
UiManager_EnableBacklight()         // panel lights → splash displayed
shown_at = now
if (splash_shown_cb) splash_shown_cb()   // INTERLOCK: app starts services + camera now, in parallel

// PHASE 2 — Legato screens, behind the lit splash (runs concurrently with app services)
legato_guard_enter()                // suspend LEGATO_Tasks + SYS_INPUT_Tasks; safe: no roots attached yet
UiManager_InitScreens()             // each screenInit_* (builds into Legato layer 0) → leRemoveRootWidget(.,0); all detached
UiManager_ShowScreenOnLayer(DASHBOARD, HW_BASE)
UiManager_ShowScreenOnLayer(NAV,       HW_OVR1)   // hosted on OVR1, starts hidden/closed
legato_guard_exit()                 // resume; LEGATO paints the bound trees

wait_render_idle()                  // bounded; never reveal a partial dashboard
hold until SPLASH_MIN_MS since shown_at   // ≥ a few seconds (currently 5000)
UiManager_HideSplash()              // cut over: reveal the (warm) dashboard
vTaskDelete(NULL)
\```

`legato_guard_enter/exit` (file-static in `ui_manager.c`): `xTaskGetHandle("LEGATO_Tasks")` + `"SYS_INPUT_Tasks"` → `vTaskSuspend`/`vTaskResume` (cache handles; NULL → log + skip, degrade to unguarded). `GFX_CANVAS_Tasks` left running (commits canvases; not a root-list reader). Guard wraps only the root-list mutations (`InitScreens` + the two `ShowScreenOnLayer`s). Safe because at guard-enter no app roots are attached (splash is pure XLCDC scanout), so LEGATO is idle; this is a one-shot construction guard, then resume for normal rendering (not the journal's abandoned "drive rendering while suspended" pattern). Service tasks (video/detector/…) don't touch Legato trees, so they may run during the guard without conflict.

## `app.c`

- `APP_Initialize`: `log_init`, `PerfLog_Initialize`, `Storage_Initialize`, `Results_Initialize`, `Catalog_Initialize`, `UiManager_SetSplashShownCallback(app_on_splash_shown)`, `UiManager_Initialize()`. No `Loader_Start`.
- `static void app_on_splash_shown(void)` — `App_StartServices()` + `Video_SetWindow/CaptureEnable/DisplayShow` (move the `VIDEO_WIN_*` geometry here from loader.c). Runs in the bringup-task context the instant the splash is displayed; the camera warms up behind the splash and is live at reveal.

## Critical files
- New: `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/splash/splash.{c,h}` (+ `user.cmake`).
- Rewrite: `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.{c,h}`.
- Delete: `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/loader.{c,h}` (− `user.cmake`).
- Edit: `firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c` (callback + drop loader); `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/nav/screen_nav.c` (drop hardcoded layer).
- Reference only: generated `le_gen_screen_Dashboard.c` / `le_gen_screen_Navigation.c` (registry hooks); `legato_state.c` (confirms the add/remove-root race surface).
- Also: strengthen memory `marvin-canvas-layer-binding` (screens never own a layer; don't assume nav==OVR1) — done at implementation time.

## Extensibility (6+ runtime-switched screens)
Add a screen = one registry row + one canvas buffer. `InitScreens` loops (each builds into layer 0 then vacates it — works within Legato's 3-layer limit since layers are construction targets, not display slots). Built-but-detached screens cost no HW layer; switching at runtime is `ShowScreenOnLayer(incoming, layer)` + hide outgoing, under the same guard (promote `legato_guard_*` to `UiManager_BeginSceneEdit/EndSceneEdit` when a caller beyond the bringup task appears). HW-layer budget (BASE/OVR1/OVR2) limits *simultaneously visible* screens, documented in the `ui_manager.c` header.

## Verification
- Build in MPLAB (new `splash.c`; `loader.c` gone; check `user.cmake`).
- Hardware: splash appears ~785 ms, image correct on OVR1; boot log shows services starting right after the splash line (not at reveal); after the ≥5 s hold the dashboard reveals fully painted with the camera already live; nav opens/closes/highlights (confirms it was hosted on OVR1 with RGB565 mode and stayed attached); dashboard buttons respond. Watch for any guard handle-not-found warning.

## Resolved
- Splash on **OVR1**; OVR2 reserved for a loading-bar overlay.
- Layer assignment is **ui_manager** policy at runtime (`ShowScreenOnLayer(id, layer)`), never screen-owned, never in the loader.
- Services start at **splash-shown** (interlock callback), parallel to screen painting.

```text
## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# Clean rewrite: splash-as-module + ui_manager orchestrator (retire `loader`)

## Context

`ui_manager.c` and `loader.c` got tangled iterating toward the fast-splash boot: UI sequencing, layer assignment, SD I/O, and the service/video handoff are smeared across both files and across the pre-/post-scheduler boundary. The splash is already a raw framebuffer (Legato-independent), so we can separate concerns cleanly.

Target model (from the user):
1. **Splash is its own self-contained screen module** under `screens/`, **independent of Legato** — it owns its framebuffer and knows how to load itself from SD and be displayed.
2. **`ui_manager` orchestrates and composites.** It kicks off the splash, and once the splash is displayed it (a) signals the app to start everything else, and (b) proceeds to bring up the Legato screens behind the splash.
3. **Screens never own a hardware layer.** A screen owns its *canvas* (render surface); `ui_manager` decides which HW layer a canvas is shown on, at runtime. (Nav usually lands on OVR1 — never assume it.)
4. **App services start the instant the splash is shown**, in parallel with the heavier behind-the-scenes screen painting, so the whole system is warm by the time we cut over to the dashboard. Splash is held at least a few seconds.
5. **The `loader` module goes away** — splash bits → the splash module; orchestration → `ui_manager`; service/video handoff → `app` via an interlock callback.

## Modules & responsibilities

- **`screens/splash/splash.{c,h}` (new, Legato-independent):** owns `s_fb_splash` (RGBA8888, nocache) and the splash canvas surface. Verbs: `Splash_InitSurface()` (pre-scheduler `gfxcSetPixelBuffer`), `bool Splash_Load()` (read `/ui/splash.raw` into the buffer; on failure fill opaque-black and return false — still displayable), `uint32_t Splash_CanvasId()`. No layer choice, no Legato, no backlight — just "load my pixels into my canvas." Depends on `storage`, not Legato.
- **`ui_manager.{c,h}` (rewrite): orchestrator + compositor.** Owns the canvas pool numbering (`ui_manager.h` defines canvas ids + HW layer indices — the single source of truth), the boot bringup task, layer assignment, backlight, and the screen registry. It is the only thing that binds a canvas to a HW layer.
- **`app.c` (small change):** registers a "splash shown" callback; the callback starts `App_StartServices()` + camera go-live. `APP_Initialize` drops `Loader_Start()`, keeps the cheap state inits, and calls `UiManager_Initialize()`.
- **`screens/nav/screen_nav.c` (surgical):** remove the hardcoded `gfxcSetLayer(NAV_CANVAS, HW_OVR1)` from `Navigation_OnShow` and the local `HW_OVR1` define — layer binding is `ui_manager`'s call now. Nav keeps its canvas, content setup, and slide animation (canvas-window based, layer-agnostic).
- **Delete `loader.{c,h}`** and its `user.cmake` entry; add `screens/splash/splash.c`.

## `ui_manager.h` API

Constants (single source of truth): `HW_BASE=0`, `HW_OVR1=2`, `HW_OVR2=3` (HEO=1 camera, off-limits); canvas ids `CANVAS_DASH/CANVAS_NAV/CANVAS_SPLASH`; `BASE_W/BASE_H`; `SPLASH_HW_LAYER = HW_OVR1` (OVR2 left free for a future loading-bar overlay over the splash).

- `void UiManager_Initialize(void)` — pre-scheduler: assign canvas buffers (dash + `Splash_InitSurface()` + `Nav_InitSurface()`), pump `GFX_CANVAS_Task()` to RUNNING, set the Legato string table, and create the bringup task. Pure setup; no build/show/sequence inline.
- `void UiManager_SetSplashShownCallback(void (*cb)(void))` — app registers its "splash is up, start everything else" hook.
- `void UiManager_EnableBacklight(void)` — PC18 GPIO (unchanged).
- (compositor verb, used internally + reusable for future screen switching) `void UiManager_ShowScreenOnLayer(ui_screen_id id, uint32_t hw_layer)` — host the screen onto its own canvas (its `host` hook) and bind that canvas to `hw_layer`, poking `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(hw_layer, <canvas's color mode>)` so the layer's mode always follows the canvas placed on it (the GFX-XLCDC driver never writes RGBMODE itself — this removes the old "restore OVR1→RGB565 for nav" special case).

Screen registry (in `ui_manager.c`): `{ leResult(*init)(void); leWidget*(*getRoot)(uint32_t); void(*host)(void); uint32_t canvasId; }` rows for Dashboard, Nav (+future). `canvasId` is intrinsic; **HW layer is never in the table** — passed at `ShowScreenOnLayer` time.

## Boot bringup task (in `ui_manager.c`)

```
// PHASE 1 — splash (Legato-independent), first
Splash_Load()                       // splash module: SD read into its fb, or fallback fill
UiManager_ShowScreenOnLayer(SPLASH, SPLASH_HW_LAYER)   // bind splash canvas → OVR1, poke RGBA8888, show
UiManager_EnableBacklight()         // panel lights → splash displayed
shown_at = now
if (splash_shown_cb) splash_shown_cb()   // INTERLOCK: app starts services + camera now, in parallel

// PHASE 2 — Legato screens, behind the lit splash (runs concurrently with app services)
legato_guard_enter()                // suspend LEGATO_Tasks + SYS_INPUT_Tasks; safe: no roots attached yet
UiManager_InitScreens()             // each screenInit_* (builds into Legato layer 0) → leRemoveRootWidget(.,0); all detached
UiManager_ShowScreenOnLayer(DASHBOARD, HW_BASE)
UiManager_ShowScreenOnLayer(NAV,       HW_OVR1)   // hosted on OVR1, starts hidden/closed
legato_guard_exit()                 // resume; LEGATO paints the bound trees

wait_render_idle()                  // bounded; never reveal a partial dashboard
hold until SPLASH_MIN_MS since shown_at   // ≥ a few seconds (currently 5000)
UiManager_HideSplash()              // cut over: reveal the (warm) dashboard
vTaskDelete(NULL)
```

`legato_guard_enter/exit` (file-static in `ui_manager.c`): `xTaskGetHandle("LEGATO_Tasks")` + `"SYS_INPUT_Tasks"` → `vTaskSuspend`/`vTaskResume` (cache handles; NULL → log + skip, degrade to unguarded). `GFX_CANVAS_Tasks` left running (commits canvases; not a root-list reader). Guard wraps only the root-list mutations (`InitScreens` + the two `ShowScreenOnLayer`s). Safe because at guard-enter no app roots are attached (splash is pure XLCDC scanout), so LEGATO is idle; this is a one-shot construction guard, then resume for normal rendering (not the journal's abandoned "drive rendering while suspended" pattern). Service tasks (video/detector/…) don't touch Legato trees, so they may run during the guard without conflict.

## `app.c`

- `APP_Initialize`: `log_init`, `PerfLog_Initialize`, `Storage_Initialize`, `Results_Initialize`, `Catalog_Initialize`, `UiManager_SetSplashShownCallback(app_on_splash_shown)`, `UiManager_Initialize()`. No `Loader_Start`.
- `static void app_on_splash_shown(void)` — `App_StartServices()` + `Video_SetWindow/CaptureEnable/DisplayShow` (move the `VIDEO_WIN_*` geometry here from loader.c). Runs in the bringup-task context the instant the splash is displayed; the camera warms up behind the splash and is live at reveal.

## Critical files
- New: `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/splash/splash.{c,h}` (+ `user.cmake`).
- Rewrite: `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.{c,h}`.
- Delete: `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/loader.{c,h}` (− `user.cmake`).
- Edit: `firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c` (callback + drop loader); `firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/nav/screen_nav.c` (drop hardcoded layer).
- Reference only: generated `le_gen_screen_Dashboard.c` / `le_gen_screen_Navigation.c` (registry hooks); `legato_state.c` (confirms the add/remove-root race surface).
- Also: strengthen memory `marvin-canvas-layer-binding` (screens never own a layer; don't assume nav==OVR1) — done at implementation time.

## Extensibility (6+ runtime-switched screens)
Add a screen = one registry row + one canvas buffer. `InitScreens` loops (each builds into layer 0 then vacates it — works within Legato's 3-layer limit since layers are construction targets, not display slots). Built-but-detached screens cost no HW layer; switching at runtime is `ShowScreenOnLayer(incoming, layer)` + hide outgoing, under the same guard (promote `legato_guard_*` to `UiManager_BeginSceneEdit/EndSceneEdit` when a caller beyond the bringup task appears). HW-layer budget (BASE/OVR1/OVR2) limits *simultaneously visible* screens, documented in the `ui_manager.c` header.

## Verification
- Build in MPLAB (new `splash.c`; `loader.c` gone; check `user.cmake`).
- Hardware: splash appears ~785 ms, image correct on OVR1; boot log shows services starting right after the splash line (not at reveal); after the ≥5 s hold the dashboard reveals fully painted with the camera already live; nav opens/closes/highlights (confirms it was hosted on OVR1 with RGB565 mode and stayed attached); dashboard buttons respond. Watch for any guard handle-not-found warning.

## Resolved
- Splash on **OVR1**; OVR2 reserved for a loading-bar overlay.
- Layer assignment is **ui_manager** policy at runtime (`ShowScreenOnLayer(id, layer)`), never screen-owned, never in the loader.
- Services start at **splash-shown** (interlock callback), parallel to screen painting.
```

```h
#ifndef UI_SCREEN_SPLASH_H
#define UI_SCREEN_SPLASH_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

/* Boot splash — a full-screen raw RGBA8888 image, NOT a Legato screen.
 *
 * It owns its canvas surface and pixel buffer and knows how to load itself: the
 * image is stored on the SD card as raw RGBA8888 pixels in the layer's native
 * byte order, so displaying it is a file read straight into the canvas buffer
 * (the buffer the LCDC scans out) — no JPEG decode, no widgets, no Legato. A
 * software JPEG decode of the full-screen image cost ~1.5 s; the raw form trades
 * ~4 MB of file size for skipping it entirely.
 *
 * This module does the load only. ui_manager (the compositor) decides which
 * hardware layer the splash canvas is shown on and lights the backlight. */

/* Assign the splash canvas pixel buffer. Call once pre-scheduler, before the
 * canvas state machine runs. */
void Splash_InitSurface(void);

/* Read the splash image off the SD card into the splash canvas buffer. Returns
 * true if it loaded; on any failure (no card, missing file, wrong size, short
 * read) the buffer is filled with an opaque fallback colour and false is
 * returned — either way the canvas is displayable. Blocking SD I/O; call from a
 * task once the scheduler is running. */
bool Splash_Load(void);

/* The splash canvas id, so the compositor can bind it to a hardware layer. */
uint32_t Splash_CanvasId(void);

#endif /* UI_SCREEN_SPLASH_H */

```

```c
#include "ui/screens/splash/splash.h"

#include <stdio.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"

#include "definitions.h"            /* SYS_FS_* */
#include "log.h"
#include "storage/storage.h"
#include "gfx/canvas/gfx_canvas_api.h"
#include "ui/ui_manager.h"          /* CANVAS_SPLASH, BASE_W, BASE_H */

#define SPLASH_REL_PATH    "/ui/splash.raw"
#define SPLASH_READ_CHUNK  (64u * 1024u)

/* Fallback fill: opaque black. The canvas is RGBA_8888 (packs 0xRRGGBBAA), so a
 * little-endian pixel word of 0x000000FF is R=G=B=0, A=0xFF. */
#define SPLASH_FILL        0x000000FFu

/* The splash pixels, also the buffer the splash layer scans out. Non-cached so
 * the SD DMA-in and the LCDC scan-out are coherent without cache maintenance
 * (the SD read is DMA-to-DRAM either way, so nocache costs nothing); 32-byte
 * aligned for the FatFs multi-block read fast path. */
static uint32_t s_fb[BASE_W * BASE_H]
    __attribute__((section(".region_nocache"), aligned(32)));

void Splash_InitSurface(void)
{
    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(CANVAS_SPLASH, BASE_W, BASE_H, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888, s_fb);
}

uint32_t Splash_CanvasId(void)
{
    return CANVAS_SPLASH;
}

static void fill_fallback(void)
{
    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < (BASE_W * BASE_H); i++) { s_fb[i] = SPLASH_FILL; }
}

bool Splash_Load(void)
{
    if (!Storage_Mount()) { fill_fallback(); return false; }

    char path[64];
    (void)snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s%s", Storage_MountPoint(), SPLASH_REL_PATH);

    SYS_FS_HANDLE h = SYS_FS_FileOpen(path, SYS_FS_FILE_OPEN_READ);
    if (h == SYS_FS_HANDLE_INVALID)
    {
        LOG_WARN("SPLASH: no image %s (fs err %d)\r\n", path, (int)SYS_FS_Error());
        fill_fallback();
        return false;
    }

    /* Raw is fixed-size: any other size is the wrong dimensions/format and would
     * render as garbage, so require an exact match to the canvas buffer. */
    int32_t sz = SYS_FS_FileSize(h);
    if (sz != (int32_t)sizeof(s_fb))
    {
        LOG_WARN("SPLASH: size %ld != expected %u\r\n", (long)sz, (unsigned)sizeof(s_fb));
        (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);
        fill_fallback();
        return false;
    }

    TickType_t t0 = xTaskGetTickCount();
    uint8_t   *dst = (uint8_t *)s_fb;
    uint32_t   total = 0u;
    bool       err = false;
    while (total < (uint32_t)sz)
    {
        size_t want = (size_t)((uint32_t)sz - total);
        if (want > SPLASH_READ_CHUNK) { want = SPLASH_READ_CHUNK; }

        size_t got = SYS_FS_FileRead(h, &dst[total], want);
        if (got == 0u || got == (size_t)-1) { err = true; break; }
        total += (uint32_t)got;
    }
    (void)SYS_FS_FileClose(h);

    if (err || total != (uint32_t)sz)
    {
        LOG_WARN("SPLASH: read short %lu/%ld\r\n", (unsigned long)total, (long)sz);
        fill_fallback();
        return false;
    }

    uint32_t ms = (uint32_t)((xTaskGetTickCount() - t0) * portTICK_PERIOD_MS);
    LOG_INFO("SPLASH: %lu B read in %lu ms\r\n", (unsigned long)total, (unsigned long)ms);
    return true;
}

```

```h
#ifndef UI_UI_MANAGER_H
#define UI_UI_MANAGER_H

#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* Canvas ids — the per-screen render surfaces in the GFX_CANVAS pool. ui_manager
 * owns this numbering (the single source of truth); each screen renders into its
 * own canvas. A canvas is NOT tied to a hardware layer — see below. */
#define CANVAS_DASH    0u
#define CANVAS_NAV     1u
#define CANVAS_SPLASH  2u

/* LCDC hardware-layer indices (drvLayer / layerOrder): BASE 0, HEO 1, OVR1 2,
 * OVR2 3. HEO is the live camera (off-limits). A canvas is bound to a hardware
 * layer at *display time* by the compositor (ui_manager) via gfxcSetLayer — a
 * screen never owns a layer. The HW-layer budget limits how many canvases can be
 * *visible at once*, not how many screens can be built. */
#define HW_BASE   0u
#define HW_OVR1   2u
#define HW_OVR2   3u

#define BASE_W   1280u
#define BASE_H    800u

/* Hardware layer the boot splash is shown on. OVR1 (above BASE so it covers the
 * dashboard); OVR2 is left free for an overlay drawn over the splash, e.g. a
 * loading bar. */
#define SPLASH_HW_LAYER   HW_OVR1

/* Bring up the UI. Call once from APP_Initialize, before the scheduler and after
 * Legato_Initialize. Assigns the per-screen canvas surfaces and creates the boot
 * task that runs the bring-up sequence (splash → screens → reveal) once the
 * scheduler is up. Pure setup; no screen is built or shown here. */
void UiManager_Initialize(void);

/* Register a callback fired the instant the splash is on screen, from the boot
 * task. The app uses it to start everything else (services + camera) in parallel
 * with the behind-the-splash screen painting, so the system is warm at reveal.
 * Set before UiManager_Initialize. */
void UiManager_SetSplashShownCallback(void (*cb)(void));

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* UI_UI_MANAGER_H */
```

```c
#include "ui/ui_manager.h"
#include "ui/screens/nav/screen_nav.h"
#include "ui/screens/splash/splash.h"

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"

#include "definitions.h"   /* XLCDC_*, AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN_Set */
#include "log.h"
#include "gfx/canvas/gfx_canvas_api.h"
#include "gfx/legato/legato.h"
#include "gfx/legato/generated/le_gen_assets.h"
#include "gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Dashboard.h"   /* screenInit/GetRoot/OnShow */
#include "gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Navigation.h"
#include "gfx/legato/renderer/legato_renderer.h"                   /* leRenderer_IsIdle */

/* ui_manager is the UI orchestrator + compositor.
 *
 * Canvas vs. hardware layer: a canvas (CANVAS_* in ui_manager.h) is a RAM
 * surface a screen renders into; a hardware layer (HW_*) is what the LCDC scans
 * out. They are independent — ui_manager binds a canvas onto whatever HW layer
 * suits at the moment with gfxcSetLayer. A screen never owns a layer; the layer
 * is chosen here, at display time. Note gfxcSetLayer only takes effect while the
 * canvas is hidden, so layer binds always precede gfxcShowCanvas.
 *
 * Boot is two phases, run by the boot task once the scheduler is up:
 *   1. Splash — the splash module loads a raw RGBA8888 image off the SD straight
 *      into its canvas; we bind that canvas to SPLASH_HW_LAYER and light the
 *      backlight. No Legato. The splash-shown callback then lets the app start
 *      everything else in parallel.
 *   2. Screens — each MGS/Legato screen is built one at a time (they all build
 *      into Legato layer 0, so each is detached after init to free layer 0 for
 *      the next), then the active screens are bound to their display layers and
 *      paint behind the splash. After a minimum hold the splash is hidden,
 *      revealing the (warm) dashboard. */

#define SPLASH_MIN_MS   5000u   /* hold the splash at least this long */

/* Render-completion wait. leRenderer_IsIdle() is also true in the gaps between
 * leUpdate calls (LEGATO_Tasks ticks ~10 ms), so a single idle sample can read
 * "done" mid-paint. Require idle to hold continuously for a window several ticks
 * long before trusting it; bounded overall so a stall can't hang boot. */
#define RENDER_POLL_MS            5u
#define RENDER_IDLE_STABLE_MS   120u
#define RENDER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS 8000u

#define BOOT_TASK_STACK_WORDS  2048u
#define BOOT_TASK_PRIORITY        2u   /* UI band; blocks on SD I/O + the render wait */

#define FB_NOCACHE   __attribute__((section(".region_nocache"), aligned (32)))

/* Dashboard surface, non-cached so the 2D engine and LCDC DMA read CPU-rendered
 * pixels coherently. RGB565 — steady-state UI needs no more. (The nav owns its
 * own surface via Nav_InitSurface; the splash owns its own via Splash_InitSurface.) */
static uint16_t FB_NOCACHE s_fb_base[BASE_W * BASE_H];

static void (*s_splash_shown_cb)(void);

static StackType_t  s_boot_stack[BOOT_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t s_boot_tcb;

/* ── Legato screen registry ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * Each screen: the generated init (builds the tree into Legato layer 0), the
 * generated root getter, a host hook (attach the root onto the screen's own
 * canvas + content setup; layer-agnostic, leaves the canvas hidden), and the
 * canvas it renders into. Adding a screen is one row + one canvas surface. */
typedef struct
{
    leResult  (*init)(void);
    leWidget *(*get_root)(uint32_t);
    void      (*host)(void);
    uint32_t  canvas;
} ui_screen_t;

typedef enum { UI_SCREEN_DASHBOARD = 0, UI_SCREEN_NAV, UI_SCREEN_COUNT } ui_screen_id;

static const ui_screen_t s_screens[UI_SCREEN_COUNT] =
{
    [UI_SCREEN_DASHBOARD] = { screenInit_Dashboard,  screenGetRoot_Dashboard,  Dashboard_OnShow,  CANVAS_DASH },
    [UI_SCREEN_NAV]       = { screenInit_Navigation, screenGetRoot_Navigation, Navigation_OnShow, CANVAS_NAV  },
};

/* ── compositor primitives ───────────────────────────────────────────────── */

/* GFX-canvas drvLayer index → XLCDC layer enum (the XLCDC poke namespace). */
static XLCDC_LAYER xlcdc_layer(uint32_t hw)
{
    switch (hw)
    {
        case HW_BASE: return XLCDC_LAYER_BASE;
        case HW_OVR2: return XLCDC_LAYER_OVR2;
        case HW_OVR1:
        default:      return XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1;
    }
}

/* Bind a canvas to a hardware layer and optionally show it. The GFX-XLCDC driver
 * never writes RGBMODE itself, so we poke the layer's colour mode to match the
 * canvas placed on it — the layer always follows its current canvas. gfxcSetLayer
 * requires the canvas hidden, which it is until shown. */
static void bind_canvas(uint32_t canvas, uint32_t hw, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE mode, bool show)
{
    gfxcSetLayer(canvas, hw);
    if (show) { gfxcShowCanvas(canvas); }
    gfxcCanvasUpdate(canvas);
    XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(xlcdc_layer(hw), mode, true);
}

static void enable_backlight(void)
{
    /* The backlight is a plain GPIO (AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN / PC18), NOT the LCDC
     * PWM that XLCDC_EnableBacklight() drives (that output isn't wired to this
     * board's backlight). The pin starts low at boot, so the panel stays dark
     * until here — no pre-splash frame. Active-high (the _Set name == enable). */
    AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN_Set();
}

/* ── Legato render serialization ──────────────────────────────────────────────
 * leAddRootWidget/leRemoveRootWidget mutate Legato's per-layer root lists with no
 * locking, and LEGATO_Tasks + SYS_INPUT_Tasks (both run from scheduler start)
 * traverse those lists. The boot task edits the scene graph post-scheduler, so it
 * suspends those two readers around the edits. Safe to suspend here: at guard
 * time no app roots are attached (the splash is pure LCDC scanout), so the
 * renderer is idle; resuming hands rendering back. GFX_CANVAS_Tasks is left
 * running (it commits canvases; not a root-list reader). */
static TaskHandle_t s_legato_task;
static TaskHandle_t s_input_task;

static void scene_edit_begin(void)
{
    s_legato_task = xTaskGetHandle("LEGATO_Tasks");
    s_input_task  = xTaskGetHandle("SYS_INPUT_Tasks");
    if (s_legato_task != NULL) { vTaskSuspend(s_legato_task); }
    if (s_input_task  != NULL) { vTaskSuspend(s_input_task);  }
    if (s_legato_task == NULL || s_input_task == NULL)
    {
        LOG_WARN("UI: render task handle not found; scene edit unguarded\r\n");
    }
}

static void scene_edit_end(void)
{
    if (s_input_task  != NULL) { vTaskResume(s_input_task);  }
    if (s_legato_task != NULL) { vTaskResume(s_legato_task); }
}

/* Build every screen and leave them all detached. They each build into Legato
 * layer 0, so detach each before the next so layer 0 is free to reuse. */
static void init_screens(void)
{
    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < UI_SCREEN_COUNT; i++)
    {
        (void)s_screens[i].init();
        leRemoveRootWidget(s_screens[i].get_root(0), 0);
    }
}

/* Block until the Legato render task has painted all pending damage. We don't
 * drive leUpdate — LEGATO_Tasks + GFX_CANVAS_Task render correctly when they run;
 * we just yield and poll the public idle flag, requiring it to hold continuously
 * (a lone idle sample is an inter-frame gap, not a finished paint). Bounded. */
static void wait_render_idle(void)
{
    TickType_t deadline   = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS);
    TickType_t idle_since = 0;
    bool       idle_run   = false;

    while (xTaskGetTickCount() < deadline)
    {
        if (leRenderer_IsIdle())
        {
            if (!idle_run)
            {
                idle_run   = true;
                idle_since = xTaskGetTickCount();
            }
            else if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - idle_since) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_STABLE_MS))
            {
                return;
            }
        }
        else
        {
            idle_run = false;
        }
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_POLL_MS));
    }
    LOG_WARN("UI: render-idle wait timed out\r\n");
}

/* ── boot sequence ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static void ui_boot_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    /* PHASE 1 — splash, before any Legato work, as fast as the SD allows. */
    (void)Splash_Load();   /* loads the image, or fills the fallback colour */
    bind_canvas(Splash_CanvasId(), SPLASH_HW_LAYER, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGBA_8888, true);
    enable_backlight();
    TickType_t shown_at = xTaskGetTickCount();

    /* Splash is up — let the app start everything else (services + camera) now,
     * in parallel with the screen painting below, so it's all warm at reveal. */
    if (s_splash_shown_cb != NULL) { s_splash_shown_cb(); }

    /* PHASE 2 — build + host the Legato screens behind the splash. Scene-graph
     * edits are guarded against the render tasks; the canvas/layer binds after
     * are GFX-canvas only (no root-list mutation) so they need no guard. */
    scene_edit_begin();
    init_screens();
    s_screens[UI_SCREEN_DASHBOARD].host();
    s_screens[UI_SCREEN_NAV].host();
    scene_edit_end();

    /* Dashboard live on BASE (covered by the splash until reveal). The nav is
     * hosted + painting into its own canvas, but not bound to a layer yet — it
     * shares OVR1 with the splash, so it takes OVR1 only after the splash vacates
     * it at reveal. */
    bind_canvas(CANVAS_DASH, HW_BASE, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, true);

    wait_render_idle();

    /* Hold the splash a minimum time so a fast boot doesn't flash it away. */
    TickType_t elapsed   = xTaskGetTickCount() - shown_at;
    TickType_t min_ticks = pdMS_TO_TICKS(SPLASH_MIN_MS);
    if (elapsed < min_ticks) { vTaskDelay(min_ticks - elapsed); }

    /* REVEAL — cut over to the (painted) dashboard, then give the nav OVR1. */
    gfxcHideCanvas(Splash_CanvasId());
    gfxcCanvasUpdate(Splash_CanvasId());
    bind_canvas(CANVAS_NAV, HW_OVR1, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, false);

    vTaskDelete(NULL);
}

/* ── screen host hooks ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * Attach the screen's root onto its own canvas and set its window/content. No
 * layer bind, no show — the compositor decides the layer and visibility. (The nav
 * has its own host hook, Navigation_OnShow, in screen_nav.c.) */
void Dashboard_OnShow(void)
{
    leWidget *root = screenGetRoot_Dashboard(0);
    leAddRootWidget(root, CANVAS_DASH);
    gfxcSetWindowPosition(CANVAS_DASH, 0, 0);
    gfxcSetWindowSize(CANVAS_DASH, BASE_W, BASE_H);
    root->fn->invalidate(root);
}

/* ── public API ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

void UiManager_Initialize(void)
{
    /* Assign the per-screen canvas surfaces, then drive the canvas state machine
     * to RUNNING so a blit isn't dropped by the RUNNING gate, then set the Legato
     * string table the screens need. All pre-scheduler config — no screen built
     * or shown here; the boot task does the sequence. */
    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(CANVAS_DASH, BASE_W, BASE_H, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, s_fb_base);
    Splash_InitSurface();
    Nav_InitSurface();
    GFX_CANVAS_Task();

    leSetStringTable(&stringTable);
    initializeStrings();

    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(ui_boot_task, "UiBoot", BOOT_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
                            NULL, BOOT_TASK_PRIORITY, s_boot_stack, &s_boot_tcb);
}

void UiManager_SetSplashShownCallback(void (*cb)(void))
{
    s_splash_shown_cb = cb;
}
```

```text
124	 * traverse those lists. The boot task edits the scene graph post-scheduler, so it
125	 * suspends those two readers around the edits. Safe to suspend here: at guard
126	 * time no app roots are attached (the splash is pure LCDC scanout), so the
127	 * renderer is idle; resuming hands rendering back. GFX_CANVAS_Tasks is left
128	 * running (it commits canvases; not a root-list reader). */
129	static TaskHandle_t s_legato_task;

134	    s_legato_task = xTaskGetHandle("LEGATO_Tasks");
135	    s_input_task  = xTaskGetHandle("SYS_INPUT_Tasks");
136	    if (s_legato_task != NULL) { vTaskSuspend(s_legato_task); }
137	    if (s_input_task  != NULL) { vTaskSuspend(s_input_task);  }
138	    if (s_legato_task == NULL || s_input_task == NULL)
139	    {
140	        LOG_WARN("UI: render task handle not found; scene edit unguarded\r\n");
141	    }
142	}
143	
144	static void scene_edit_end(void)
145	{
146	    if (s_input_task  != NULL) { vTaskResume(s_input_task);  }
147	    if (s_legato_task != NULL) { vTaskResume(s_legato_task); }
148	}

150	/* Build every screen and leave them all detached. They each build into Legato
151	 * layer 0, so detach each before the next so layer 0 is free to reuse. */
152	static void init_screens(void)
153	{
154	    for (uint32_t i = 0u; i < UI_SCREEN_COUNT; i++)
155	    {
156	        (void)s_screens[i].init();
157	        leRemoveRootWidget(s_screens[i].get_root(0), 0);
158	    }

161	/* Block until the Legato render task has painted all pending damage. We don't
162	 * drive leUpdate — LEGATO_Tasks + GFX_CANVAS_Task render correctly when they run;
163	 * we just yield and poll the public idle flag, requiring it to hold continuously
164	 * (a lone idle sample is an inter-frame gap, not a finished paint). Bounded. */
165	static void wait_render_idle(void)
166	{
167	    TickType_t deadline   = xTaskGetTickCount() + pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS);
168	    TickType_t idle_since = 0;
169	    bool       idle_run   = false;
170	
171	    while (xTaskGetTickCount() < deadline)
172	    {
173	        if (leRenderer_IsIdle())
174	        {
175	            if (!idle_run)
176	            {
177	                idle_run   = true;
178	                idle_since = xTaskGetTickCount();
179	            }
180	            else if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - idle_since) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_IDLE_STABLE_MS))
181	            {
182	                return;
183	            }
184	        }
185	        else
186	        {
187	            idle_run = false;
188	        }
189	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(RENDER_POLL_MS));
190	    }
191	    LOG_WARN("UI: render-idle wait timed out\r\n");
192	}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 14:27:57Z)**_

Implementation complete. The boot UI is now cleanly separated along the lines you described.

## What changed

**New: [screens/splash/splash.{c,h}](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/splash/splash.c)** — a self-contained, Legato-independent splash screen. It owns its framebuffer and knows how to load itself (`Splash_Load()` reads `/ui/splash.raw` straight into its canvas, or fills the fallback). No layer choice, no Legato, no backlight.

**Rewritten: [ui_manager.{c,h}](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.c)** — the orchestrator + compositor:
- Owns the canvas-id/HW-layer constants (single source of truth), a screen registry (`{init, get_root, host, canvas}` — add a screen = one row), the boot task, and **all layer assignment**.
- `bind_canvas(canvas, hw, mode, show)` is the *only* place a canvas meets a layer, and it pokes RGBMODE to match the canvas — so the old "restore OVR1→RGB565" special case is gone.
- Boot task: **Phase 1** splash (load → bind OVR1 → backlight → fire callback), **Phase 2** (guarded) build each screen through layer 0 + detach, host dashboard/nav, bind dashboard to BASE, paint behind splash, then after the hold reveal and hand the nav OVR1.

**[screen_nav.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/nav/screen_nav.c)** — dropped the hardcoded `gfxcSetLayer(NAV_CANVAS, HW_OVR1)` and the local `HW_OVR1`/`NAV_CANVAS`; `Navigation_OnShow` is now a layer-agnostic host hook. Nav no longer assumes it owns a layer.

**[app.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c)** — registers `app_on_splash_shown` (→ `App_StartServices()` + camera), fired the instant the splash is up so everything warms in parallel with the screen painting. `Loader_Start` gone; `loader.{c,h}` deleted.

**Concurrency:** the post-scheduler scene-graph edits are wrapped in `scene_edit_begin/end` (suspend `LEGATO_Tasks` + `SYS_INPUT_Tasks`) — safe because Legato is idle at that point (no roots attached; `Legato_Initialize` ran pre-scheduler).

I also strengthened the `marvin-canvas-layer-binding` memory so I stop treating nav==OVR1 as fixed.

## To verify (your MPLAB build + hardware)
- Splash still ~785 ms on OVR1; the `SPLASH:` read line, then services logging right after.
- After the 5 s hold, dashboard reveals fully painted with the camera live.
- Nav opens/closes/highlights (it gets OVR1 + RGB565 at reveal) and dashboard buttons respond.
- Watch for a `UI: scene edit unguarded` warning (would mean a task-handle name mismatch) and any stack-overflow hook (boot task is 2048 words now that it builds the screens).

Not committed — say the word when you've built and confirmed it on hardware. The plan is at `.claude/plans/greedy-launching-shamir.md` for reference.

```bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
marvin: rewrite UI boot — splash module + ui_manager orchestrator, retire loader

Untangle ui_manager + loader, which had grown to smear UI sequencing, layer
assignment, SD I/O, and the service handoff across both files and the pre-/
post-scheduler boundary. Behavior-preserving (confirmed on hardware).

- New screens/splash/splash.{c,h}: a self-contained, Legato-independent splash
  screen that owns its RGBA8888 framebuffer and loads /ui/splash.raw straight
  into it (opaque-black fallback). No layer choice, no Legato, no backlight.
- ui_manager is now the UI orchestrator + compositor: owns the canvas-id /
  HW-layer constants, a screen registry (add a screen = one row), the boot task,
  and all layer assignment. bind_canvas() is the one place a canvas meets a
  layer and pokes the layer's RGBMODE to match it. Boot is two phases run by the
  boot task: (1) splash load + bind OVR1 + backlight, then fire a splash-shown
  callback; (2) guarded build of the Legato screens (one at a time through layer
  0, detaching each), bind dashboard to BASE, paint behind the splash, then
  reveal after the hold and hand the nav OVR1.
- Screens never own a hardware layer: screen_nav drops the hardcoded
  gfxcSetLayer(.., HW_OVR1) and local layer/canvas defines; Navigation_OnShow is
  a layer-agnostic host hook using CANVAS_NAV from ui_manager.h.
- Services start at splash-shown (app_on_splash_shown → App_StartServices +
  camera), in parallel with screen painting, so the system is warm at reveal.
  Loader_Start dropped from APP_Initialize; loader.{c,h} deleted.
- Post-scheduler scene-graph edits are guarded by suspending LEGATO_Tasks +
  SYS_INPUT_Tasks (safe: Legato is idle with no roots attached at that point).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
```
