```text
void PWM_ChannelDutySet(PWM_CHANNEL_NUM channel, uint32_t duty)
{
    if(0U != ((PWM_REGS->PWM_SR >> channel) & 0x1U))
    {
        PWM_REGS->PWM_CH_NUM[channel].PWM_CMR &= ~PWM_CMR_CPD_Msk;
        PWM_REGS->PWM_CH_NUM[channel].PWM_CUPD = duty;
    }
    else
    {
        PWM_REGS->PWM_CH_NUM[channel].PWM_CDTY = duty;
    }
}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 14:43:25Z)**_

Done. The backlight is now PWM-dimmed instead of a GPIO toggle.

## What changed

MCC moved PC18 from a plain GPIO (`AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN`) to **PWM channel 0** (MCK/1024, left-aligned, period `CPRD` = 256). The old `AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN_Set()` macro no longer exists, so the committed `enable_backlight()` wouldn't have compiled — this fixes that.

In [ui_manager.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/ui_manager.c):
- **`set_backlight(pct)`** — reads the channel period at runtime (so it tracks whatever MCC sets) and sets duty = `period·pct/100`. It uses `PWM_ChannelDutySet`, which writes `CDTY` directly while the channel is stopped and the update register once running — so the same helper is valid at boot *and* for runtime brightness changes later.
- **`enable_backlight()`** — sets the default **50%** then `PWM_ChannelsStart`. Because duty is set while the channel is stopped, it starts straight at 50% with no transient. `BACKLIGHT_DEFAULT_PCT` is a one-line knob.

50% maps to `period/2` (= 128), which is the correct half-brightness target regardless of the channel's polarity.

## To confirm on hardware
- Backlight comes up at ~50% when the splash appears.
- **Pre-splash:** the channel is stopped (no PWM output) until `enable_backlight`, so the panel should stay dark until the splash — but the exact idle level of a stopped PWM pin is board-dependent, so watch for any pre-splash glow. If there is one, we'd nudge the polarity/idle handling.
- Whether 50% duty looks like ~50% perceived brightness (depends on the backlight driver's response curve).

I did **not** commit this — your earlier "commit" was for the UI-rewrite set, and per the project rule I don't commit on my own initiative. It's staged-ready when you are; say the word and I'll commit (this is one file, `ui_manager.c`, plus the journal). If you want a runtime brightness control (e.g. a `console` command or a UI slider), `set_backlight` is ready to be promoted to a public `UiManager_SetBacklight(pct)`.

    if (s == NULL || s[0] == '\0') { return dflt; }

        if (*p < '0' || *p > '9') { return dflt; }
        v = (v * 10u) + (uint32_t)(*p - '0');
    }

marvin: PWM backlight dimming on PC18 + `backlight` console command

MCC reconfigured PC18 from a plain GPIO (AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN) to a PWM output
(PWM channel 0: MCK/1024, left-aligned, period 256), which removed the old
GPIO enable macro. Drive the backlight via PWM instead.

- ui_manager: UiManager_SetBacklight(pct) sets duty = period·pct/100 (period read
  at runtime; 50% = period/2 is polarity-independent), UiManager_GetBacklight()
  reports it. PWM_ChannelDutySet writes CDTY while the channel is stopped and the
  update register once running, so the same call works at boot and at runtime.
  enable_backlight() sets the default (50%) before PWM_ChannelsStart, so it comes
  up straight at 50% with no transient; the channel is stopped until then, so the
  panel stays dark until the splash.
- console: `backlight <0-100>` sets/reports brightness at runtime.

Confirmed on hardware (50% at boot). Includes the MCC PWM reconfiguration
(plib_pwm, pin config, PWM_Initialize).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 14:49:32Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 14:49:36Z)**_

You got the config right; I got the code direction wrong. Here's the reasoning:

The channel is `CPOL_LOW`, and you observed `CDTY=0` → full bright, `CDTY=256` → off. So **brightness tracks the *high* time** (`period − CDTY`), and `CDTY` is the low-time. My code set `CDTY = period·pct/100`, which inverts it.

And critically — **your `CPOL_LOW` config is the correct choice**: a stopped channel idles at the CPOL level (low), which is *dark*, so the panel stays off until the splash. If we "fixed" it by flipping to `CPOL_HIGH` in MCC, the pin would idle *high* and the backlight would glare before the splash. So the fix belongs in code: invert the duty. Let me do that.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 14:50:03Z)**_

Done. The one-line fix: `CDTY = period·(100−pct)/100` instead of `period·pct/100`.

Now:
- `backlight 100` → CDTY 0 → full bright
- `backlight 0` → CDTY 256 → off

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 14:53:39Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-27 14:53:51Z)**_

Good question — it's genuinely a SAM-PWM quirk, not a mistake on either of our parts.

## Why it looks backwards

Most PWMs define duty as **on-time** (high-time), so duty 0 = always-low = off. The SAM PWM defines `CDTY` as **"time spent at the `CPOL` level"** — i.e. it's relative to the polarity, not absolute high-time. So:

- **`CPOL_LOW`** (what you configured): `CDTY` = the **low** time. The output is low for `CDTY` counts, then high for the rest. So `CDTY=0` → no low time → always high → **full bright**; `CDTY=CPRD` → always low → **off**. That's exactly what you saw.
- **`CPOL_HIGH`**: `CDTY` = the **high** time — the intuitive "duty," where `CDTY=0` = off.

That's why it reads backwards from a "normal" PWM: with `CPOL_LOW` the raw `CDTY` register is inverted relative to brightness.

## The catch: you can't have both on this peripheral

`CPOL` sets the **start/idle level too**, not just the duty reference:

- `CPOL_LOW` → stopped channel idles **low** = **dark** (what you want — no pre-splash glare). But raw `CDTY=0` = bright.
- `CPOL_HIGH` → raw `CDTY` = intuitive on-time (`CDTY=0` = off). But the stopped channel idles **high** = backlight **glares before the splash**.

So "idle low when stopped" and "raw `CDTY=0` = off" are coupled through the one `CPOL` bit — you can't get both directly (short of also wiring up the output-override registers, which is more config for no real gain).

## Where that leaves us

Your config (`CPOL_LOW`) is the right one — idle-low/dark is the hard requirement. The "weirdness" is contained entirely in the raw register; **`UiManager_SetBacklight` inverts it**, so the *API* is the intuitive one:

- `backlight 0` → off
- `backlight 100` → full bright

That's the standard split: keep the polarity that gives the safe idle state, and let the driver present brightness in human terms. No code change needed — the fix I just made already does this; I only wanted to confirm the direction is right at the command level (it is: 0 = off, 100 = bright).

If you'd genuinely rather the raw register read intuitively, the path is `CPOL_HIGH` **plus** configuring the PWM output-override to force the pin low while the channel is stopped — but I'd advise against it; it's more moving parts to solve something the one-line software inversion already handles cleanly. Your call.
